item.title: [MLB.com] Despite wrist issue, Gunnar doesn't want to make excuses for down '26
item.dc:creator: Jake Rill
item.description: NEW YORK -- Asked the question late Friday night inside the visitors’ clubhouse at Yankee Stadium, Gunnar Henderson hesitated for a moment. item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK -- Asked the question late Friday night inside the visitors’ clubhouse at Yankee Stadium, Gunnar Henderson hesitated for a moment. His reluctance to answer shows exactly the type of competitor that the Orioles’ shortstop is.
In 2025, Henderson played through a left shoulder impingement for much of the season -- an ailment that impacted his play, but didn’t become public knowledge until he shared it last offseason. Has there been anything similar bothering the 25-year-old in ‘26?
Henderson paused, then divulged some new details.
“I really don’t like making excuses, because everybody’s banged up at this point in the year. But yeah, I had a little [right] wrist issue going on,” Henderson said. “But I felt like bat knob changes helped that out. So it was just minor, getting that a little bit better. But like I said, everybody’s banged up at this point in the year. It just sucks that it happened. It is what it is.”
It makes sense that Henderson may not have been close to 100 percent for periods of this season. In fact, he said the wrist bothered him for “pretty much half the year.”
Henderson can be a star player. He’s shown it. In 2023, he was an All-Star who placed fourth in American League MVP Award voting. He hit 37 home runs and posted an .893 OPS, both highs for his five-year MLB career.
The numbers have trended in the wrong direction since. This year, Henderson has especially struggled, hitting only .225 with a .714 OPS, both career lows. The power has still been there (24 homers), but the 2019 second-round Draft pick and former top prospect hasn’t looked quite like the player capable of taking over games for much of the year.
There have been small glimpses. But not like it was early in Henderson’s career, when he was a burgeoning superstar.
If it wasn’t the wrist injury, then what was it?
“Some of it was probably a little bit of doing too much in certain situations, just not allowing myself to take over. And then, me trying to force stuff to happen,” Henderson said. “That’s some of it, and then some of it was obviously just swing feels and stuff. When I get to that point in the offseason, I’m excited to go to work on that, because I’ve felt like I’ve felt a lot of good here recently. It’s just a matter of putting that all together and being able to be confident in that.”
Henderson knows he can still be one of the best players in the sport. He didn’t forget how to play baseball overnight.
“Obviously, a couple games here and there, I’ve shown it’s still in there. It’s not a matter of it just disappearing one day,” Henderson said. “It’s just the game. Obviously, the pitchers are getting paid, too, and they’re getting paid to make adjustments to you and get you out. So, I feel like they did a really good job of making adjustments, and I just didn’t make that adjustment that I needed this year.”
When manager Craig Albernaz was asked about Henderson’s season prior to the Orioles’ doubleheader split vs. the Yankees in New York on Friday, the first-year skipper was quick to point out the shortstop’s availability. It’s not easy to play 157 games (like Henderson has), especially at such a premier position.
But one thing Albernaz believes can help Henderson going forward is the emergence of first baseman Pete Alonso as a team leader. Henderson doesn’t need to put as much pressure on himself to singlehandedly carry the team, because Alonso has shown he can carry a large chunk of that responsibility.
“Gunnar doesn’t have to shoulder the load,” Albernaz said. “He can go out and be the best version of himself, and the best version of Gunnar is his ability to play baseball, his ability to run the bases, to play good defense, to hit the ball to all fields. He doesn’t have to be the sole guy taking on all the weight.”
The Orioles (79-82) have one game remaining on the 2026 schedule -- Sunday’s series finale at Yankee Stadium. Then, Henderson and his teammates will part ways, beginning their offseasons without experiencing any postseason baseball.
As much as Henderson wants to get back on track from an individual standpoint, what bothers him most is the team’s lack of success. Baltimore has now missed the playoffs in back-to-back years, after previously reaching the postseason in both 2023 and ‘24.
Henderson got a taste of October, and he wants more than anything to get back there.
“The postseason is something that I myself have as the mindset going into every year, and I feel like that’s the same for every individual in here,” Henderson said. “Obviously, not being able to get back to the postseason this year is a failed year for us. So I feel like that’s something that’s going to be, for me at least, sitting on my mind. Because I want to play postseason baseball every year, and that’s something that I enjoy playing and want to do each and every year. Take it into the offseason and prepare for the postseason next year.”
If Henderson can return to form in 2027, then there shouldn’t be any reason why Baltimore can’t do that.

item.content:encoded:
Salvador Pérez todavía no ha decidido cuándo será su último juego, pero “retiro” dejó de ser una palabra demasiado lejana. Después de 17 temporadas en las Grandes Ligas, el receptor venezolano tiene garantizado un año más con los Reales de Kansas City. Después de 2027 deberá conversar con el gerente para saber qué opciones existen, aunque su intención es continuar.



“Quiero jugar un par de años más”, dijo.

Su temporada 2026 también refleja una etapa diferente. Pérez ha tenido una carga menor detrás del plato y ha asumido más responsabilidades en otras posiciones. Aun así, mantiene su producción ofensiva: llega al tramo final con 20 jonrones y 75 carreras impulsadas.
Más allá de los números, el propio Pérez reconoce que su cuerpo necesita atención y que quiere aprovechar el descanso para prepararse. Pero todavía tiene una motivación que lo mantiene mirando hacia adelante. Volver a jugar en octubre con Kansas.
Pérez ya sabe lo que significa ser campeón. En 2015 fue una de las figuras de los Reales que conquistaron la Serie Mundial. Ahora quiere volver a disputar un "Clásico de Otoño" y tener la oportunidad de ganarlo nuevamente.
“Quiero regresar a los playoffs, tratar de tener la oportunidad de jugar una Serie Mundial otra vez, tratar de ganarla”, afirmó.
Para él, conseguirlo sería una manera ideal de cerrar su carrera. “Creo que eso sería algo bien bonito y algo para retirarme bien, con el favor de Dios”, añadió.
El Salón de la Fama en el horizonte
En medio de esa reflexión sobre el final de su carrera aparece otra pregunta: ¿qué pasará cinco años después de su último juego?
Pérez sabe que existe la posibilidad de que su nombre sea considerado para el Salón de la Fama. No da por hecho que terminará en Cooperstown. Simplemente reconoce que es una aspiración natural para un jugador que ha construido una carrera como la suya.
“Todo pelotero en Grandes Ligas quisiera llegar al Salón de la Fama”, dijo. “¿Quién no quiere ser inmortal?”
La conversación tendrá que esperar. Primero debe terminar su carrera y después llegará el período de espera.
“Esperemos a ver qué pasa cuando me retire. Esperemos los cinco años y que sea lo que Dios quiera”, señaló.
Mientras tanto, puede mirar hacia atrás. Pérez contó que recientemente publicó una fotografía con algunos de sus logros y que verla le permitió dimensionar todo lo conseguido.
“Uno mismo no se da como cuenta todo lo que ha hecho en la pelota”, explicó.
La lista incluye una Serie Mundial, el premio de Jugador Más Valioso de aquel clásico, nueve Juegos de Estrellas, cinco Guantes de Oro y cuatro Bates de Plata. En 2021, además, lideró las Grandes Ligas con 48 jonrones y 121 carreras impulsadas. Este año agregó el cetro del Clásico Mundial de Béisbol a su palmarés.
“Ver todos esos triunfos, todos esos premios, todo lo que Dios me ha regalado en este deporte tan bonito, me hace orgulloso de mí mismo”, dijo.
Venezuela, el último capítulo
Si Kansas City representa prácticamente toda su vida profesional, Venezuela es el lugar donde Pérez quiere escribir el último capítulo.
Cuando fue consultado si estaba abierta la posibilidad de retirarse en su país, respondió sin dudar. “Está súper abierto”.
Su deseo es jugar un año más en Venezuela antes de retirarse. La experiencia reciente con los Leones del Caracas reforzó esa intención, aunque primero quiere descansar y preparar su cuerpo después de una carrera de 17 años.
Pero cuando Pérez imagina su retiro, la escena va más allá del béisbol. Se ve en la playa, en un bote, en su casa. Se ve llevando a sus hijos a la escuela, acompañándolos a una graduación y disfrutando un verano con ellos.
“La gente en verdad nos mira en las dos horas y media de un juego, pero a través de eso hemos perdido tiempo hasta con la familia de uno”, explicó.
Por eso, cuando llegue el momento de decir que no jugará más, quiere detenerse. “No me quiero salir de la pelota, pero sí me quiero tomar un tiempo libre, un año, dos”, dijo.
Todavía quiere jugar. Quiere volver a los playoffs y buscar otra Serie Mundial. Pero también sabe que el final llegará. Y cuando llegue, Salvador Pérez quiere que sea en Venezuela, cerca de su familia y con el tiempo para disfrutar una vida que durante 17 años tuvo que esperar.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers predicted to win Tarik Skubal sweepstakes with decade-long deal
item.dc:creator: Matt Sullivan
item.description: Dodgers predicted to win Tarik Skubal sweepstakes with decade-long deal originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here. item.content:encoded:
Dodgers predicted to win Tarik Skubal sweepstakes with decade-long deal originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Los Angeles Dodgers are the favorites to win the 2026 MLB World Series, and once the offseason begins, they're going to be the favorites to sign all of the top players as well.
But the one prize they're likely to go after more than any other is the starting pitcher they acquired at the deadline this year: Tarik Skubal. He's hitting free agency this offseason and is going to be a hot commodity for a lot of teams around baseball.
Bleacher Report's Zach Buckley is predicting the Dodgers will win the sweepstakes for Skubal, thanks to a likely record-breaking decade-long commitment to the 30-year-old left-hander.
Dodgers predicted to win Tarik Skubal sweepstakes with 10-year commitment
"The New York Mets could and should make this interesting, but the Dodgers could absolutely win another Skubal sweepstakes," Buckley writes. "Prediction: Skubal signs a 10-year deal and stays in L.A."
Re-signing Skubal might prove difficult, as he's easily the best player set to hit the open market this offseason. With a chance to land a massive multi-year deal, Skubal is going to play his cards right this offseason.
The Dodgers are likely the favorites, especially after winning the bidding war for Skubal at the MLB trade deadline when they got him from the Detroit Tigers.
But when it comes to the open market this upcoming offseason, the New York Mets, New York Yankees, and a few of the other big-spenders are sure to show serious interest.
However, none can likely compare to the long-term commitment on top of the massive, likely record-breaking contract that Skubal is going to demand, as the Dodgers can.
Skubal is going to be 30 years old at the start of the 2027 MLB season, so a 10-year-long commitment would be quite the risky endeavor, especially for a pitcher who just had surgery on his elbow in the middle of the season.
As the Dodgers have shown time and time again, they're not afraid of such a risk. So long as they get the player, they have the financial advantage to make a risky deal worthwhile in the long run.
Skubal, the 2024 and 2025 AL Cy Young winner, is exactly the kind of player worth signing to a record-setting deal that carries significant long-term risks.
While other teams might be trying to do shorter deals, the Dodgers can lock him up to a long-term contract other teams aren't likely to be comfortable handing out.
Buckley is predicting the Dodgers will win the Skubal sweepstakes this offseason thanks to their willingness to go to a long-term deal, with a decade-long commitment being the deal he's predicting Skubal will get from the Dodgers this winter.

item.title: [New York Post] Dodgers get A grade in final Post MLB Power Rankings. But who gets an F?
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris

item.content:encoded:
Throughout the season, the California Post power-ranked MLB’s 30 teams and checked in on intriguing awards races. Records as of Saturday morning:
1) Brewers (101-59): A+
It was another perfect regular season for the Brewers, who won 100 games for the first time in franchise history to clinch the best record in the majors. Of course, their repeated failures in recent postseasons mean the real test is still to come in October. They have one superstar in Jacob Misiorowski but will need others to emerge in this year’s playoffs.
2) Dodgers (98-62): A
It was a familiar story for the Dodgers this year. A hot start. A second-half slump. Plenty of injuries along the way. Yet, another division crown that sets them up for another deep October run. That formula has worked the past two years for the two-time defending champions. Their real grade this season will depend on whether they can complete a World Series three-peat.
3) Rays (97-63): A+
After two years of missing the playoffs, the Rays had a very Rays-esque season. Uncovered gems on the mound. A relentlessly consistent lineup at the plate. And, as a result, the AL’s best record — and their best chance to get back to the World Series since 2020.
4) Braves (93-67): A
The Braves are back in the playoffs and back atop the NL East, rebounding as hoped from a disappointing 86-loss campaign last season that snapped a six-year postseason streak.
5) Yankees (93-68): B+
This grade might’ve been higher, if not for the uncertainty shrouding the Bronx Bombers as they enter the postseason. They managed to survive one extended Aaron Judge absence this regular season. Trying to do so again in October would be a tall task.
6) Padres (89-71): A-
In the weeks leading up to the trade deadline, the Padres seemed bound to be sellers. But then their offense — especially Fernando Tatis Jr. — came back to life. They bolstered their rotation by being buyers at the trade deadline instead. And now they are back in the playoffs as a potential dark horse, thanks to their 16-5 record in September.
7) Cubs (88-73): B+
The Cubs are back in the playoffs for a second straight year. They have the presumptive National League MVP in Pete Crow-Armstrong. And they managed to overcome a wave of pitching injuries. Now, they will try to mount a deeper October run after being knocked out in Game 5 of the NLDS last year.
8) Red Sox (87-74): B+
A strange regular season in Boston has reached a satisfactory ending, with the Red Sox — led by interim-now-turned-permanent manager Chad Tracy — getting a shot to avenge last year’s postseason elimination to the Yankees in next week’s wild-card series.
9) Phillies (87-73): Incomplete
Check back with us on Sunday night for this final grade. Because after seemingly salvaging their nightmarish start to the season under interim manager Don Mattingly, the Phillies are flirting with what would be a monumental September collapse, having yet to secure their place in the playoffs amid a 2-5 slump this week.
10) Diamondbacks (86-74): B-
We are only tentatively grading the Dbacks for now, thanks to their slim (but very much possible) chances of sneaking into the playoffs. If they don’t, it will be another conflicting season for the Dbacks, who have won 80-plus games in four straight seasons but still have just their surprise 2023 World Series run to show for it.
11) Guardians (84-76): A
The Guardians did what they do this season. Prevent runs. Score just enough. Fly under the radar for most of the year. Then round into form late to (most likely) win another AL Central title.
12) White Sox (83-77): A
This could still become an A+ if the White Sox wind up winning the AL Central. But even if not, the South Siders have been the most pleasant surprise in the majors this season, going from three straight 100-loss seasons to an upstart playoff berth with their young and promising roster.
13/14) Astros/Rangers (79-81): Incomplete
To be clear, neither of these teams has had a good 2026. And yet, they both enter the final days of the season with a chance to win the AL West — even though they can finish no better than .500. It will be the first time in MLB history a team will make the playoffs without a winning record. What a year in the AL West.
15) Pirates (81-79): C+
Good news: The Pirates avoided a losing record for the first time since 2018. Bad news: It wasn’t enough to keep them in playoff contention despite a surprisingly productive year from their offense.
16) Marlins (79-81): C+
The Marlins flirted with playoff contention for a while before ultimately fading down the stretch. They could be poised to take another step next year. Then again, they’ve looked that way before (remember that surprise playoff appearance in 2023?) and been unable to keep progressing.
17) Orioles (79-82): D
The Orioles’ signing of Pete Alonso worked out. But little else did in Baltimore this year. The once-budding contender has now missed the playoffs in two straight years after being swept in back-to-back postseasons the two years before that.
18) Blue Jays (78-82): D
As if the Blue Jays’ post-pennant campaign wasn’t bad enough, Vladimir Guerrero Jr. provided one more low point with his comments about his $500 million contract this week. There is hope for next season. But this year stung.
19) Cardinals (77-83): B
Given nonexistent preseason expectations, the rebuilding Cardinals mostly accomplished what they wanted to this year. They have young talent in Jordan Walker and JJ Wetherholt. They have rebuilt what is now a highly ranked farm system. And they look like a team capable of making a jump in 2027 and beyond.
20) Nationals (76-84): C
The Nats were never serious playoff contenders (their MLB-record 42 blown saves made sure of that). But they have identified a core of young talent to build around. Whether they will spend to add the necessary pieces around them, however, remains to be seen.
21) Mets (73-87): D-
The Mets can only hope this train wreck of a year serves as some sort of cleanse as they look to retool their roster this winter. The only thing that saved this from being an F was their second-half performance under another interim-now-turned-permanent manager in Andy Green.
22) Twins (76-84): C
For some reason, the Twins were intent on being playoff contenders this year. For a while, they hung around in a bad AL wild-card race. But in the end, they’ve wound up back where they started: With an OK, but not-at-all contending, roster that leaves them stuck in MLB’s no-man’s land.
23) Tigers (75-85): D
How much will the Tigers rue their decision to not maximize Tarik Skubal’s trade value by dealing him last winter? It could depend, first and foremost, on River Ryan’s development in their rotation. At the least, he offered signs of promise with a scoreless three-inning debut with the team this week.
24) Reds (74-86): D
Whatever momentum the Reds thought they were building after last year’s postseason berth vanished this summer, despite Elly De La Cruz cementing himself as one of the best players in baseball. The next time their owner asks why they aren’t the Brewers, someone should hold up a mirror.
25) Mariners (74-86): F
At the beginning of the year, only the Dodgers had a higher probability of making the playoffs (according to FanGraphs’ computer models) than the Mariners’ 80.9% mark. Instead, they suffered what might be the most disappointing season in their long-tortured history. They could be good again next year. But this season was a reminder that’s anything but a guarantee.
26) Royals (68-92): D
Another disastrous Royals season leaves them facing an existential crisis, trying to figure out how to return to competitiveness before they waste the prime of Bobby Witt Jr.’s career.
27) Giants (65-95): F
The Giants thought they could be contenders this year. Instead, they now find themselves at a crossroads. They have little choice but to run it back with their thus-far disappointing core of Willy Adames, Matt Chapman and Rafael Devers (plus Logan Webb). But this year, they looked a long way off from even being competitive.
28) Athletics (64-96): D-
There was some thought before the year that the Athletics’ young roster could be feisty. Now, the only question is how much longer they have to waste away in their minor-league ballpark purgatory.
29) Angels (62-98): C
This grade has little to do with the Angels’ on-field product, as they flirt with what would be the first 100-loss season in franchise history, and everything to do with the changes they’ve made behind the scenes. New owner. New front office. And for the first time in a while, new reason for long-term hope.
30) Rockies (57-103): D
The best thing we can say about the Rockies: They proved slightly tougher to beat during this 100-loss season, as opposed to each of the three previous ones they have suffered the last three years. Progress!
Awards Predictions
NL MVP: Pete Crow-Armstrong, Cubs
AL MVP: Yordan Alvarez, Astros
NL Cy Young: Jacob Misiorowski, Brewers
AL Cy Young: Cam Schlittler, Yankees
NL Rookie of the Year: Sal Stewart, Reds
AL Rookie of the Year: Kevin McGonigle, Tigers
NL Reliever of the Year: Mason Miller, Padres
AL Reliever of the Year: Louis Varland, Blue Jays

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Manny Machado Needs To Do More Than Lead In Postseason
item.dc:creator: Bob McCullough

item.content:encoded:
The San Diego Padres just made the playoffs, and they're looking to move up to clinch the top spot so they can stay at home through the wild-card round. Not many people believed this was possible back in June when the team was playing .500 baseball, but one who did was third baseman Manny Machado, who professed faith in the team's ability to turn things around throughout the season.
It's been a strange season for Machado. He hasn't been good, but he has been steady, and he's contributed power. The average posted on the scoreboard every night is still ugly at .215, but Machado currently has 29 home runs and counting.
Dennis Lin of The Athletic did an intriguing story on Machado, and he noted how some of his teammates have reacted to the third baseman's struggles, which are still punctuated here and there with some great games.
Ty France was one. France has had a breakout campaign, and he noted that a lot of what he does is watching how Machando "goes about his business."
But the spotlight is about to get a lot more focused. The Padres lost last year because their three stars didn't hit, and in some ways Machado's struggles last year against the Chicago Cubs in the wild-card series were a harbinger of what was to come.
Machado went 1-for'10 against the Cubs with a two-run homer — i.e., he hit for power but didn't hit for much else. Fernando Tatis Jr. and Jackson Merrill were also shut down, and the result was a team that couldn't score enough runs to win games.
The Padres have been that at times this season, and if they do that again, they'll be heading on vacation, regardless of where they do it in the postseason.
France noted that Machado's steady, calm approach to his struggles has been a key in San Diego's recent surge, as he said that he's played for teams where the leaders are "full of panic and anxiety and stress" and it spreads throughout the team.
Machado still hunts mistakes as well as any hitter in the game, although he misses a lot more than he used to. His homer against Los Angeles Dodgers starter Yoshinobu Yamamoto on Wednesday left the bat at an exit velocity of 108.6 mph, per Lin, and France said the value Machado brings to the locker room is "irreplaceable."
But the focus on dealing with the Padres lineup will be the same, and whether Machado can step up and do more is a big question going into the playoffs.

item.content:encoded:
Sep 26, 2026, 1:28 PM ET
Toronto Blue Jays starting pitcher Dylan Cease (shoulder) said that he will take some downtime over the next few weeks to allow the inflammation in his shoulder to subside. However, the 30-year-old also expects to have a relatively normal offseason, hopefully alleviating any long-term concerns about a major injury. With surgery currently off the table, the belief is that time away from throwing will give his shoulder what it needs to return to full health. With the expectation that he will be ready for Opening Day in 2027, he is someone to remember at the top end of drafts come draft day, as his track record for endurance is unparalleled. That being said, how he responds to a ramp-up in the winter will be a key indicator of whether this shoulder issue is truly behind him. He will finish the 2026 season with 239 strikeouts over 169.0 innings pitched, along with an impressive 2.40 ERA, 1.10 WHIP, and 11 wins.--Dave Funnell - RotoBaller
Source: Arden Zwelling
More Recent News
Josh Jung Has Fractured Hand


Dave Funnell




Sep 26, 2026, 1:16 PM ET
Texas Rangers third baseman Josh Jung (hand) suffered a fractured right hand, according to X-rays after an early removal from Friday's game. A pitch hit the 28-year-old in the first inning of a pivotal game against Minnesota, and the testing later confirmed the injury. He will miss time while he heals, ending his 2026 season on a sour note. Still, despite battling multiple injuries all season, he will finish with a .299 batting average and 12 home runs over 104 games. While nothing has been confirmed, it would appear that he will be ready for Spring Training next season. He remains in the mix for late-round fantasy upside heading into 2027, with the potential for more should he be able to stay healthy. That said, his draft price will surely take his extensive injury history into account.--Dave Funnell - RotoBaller
Source: Evan Grant
Elmer Rodriguez to Pitch on Sunday for Yankees


Keith Hernandez




Sep 26, 2026, 12:47 PM ET
New York Yankees right-handed pitching prospect Elmer Rodriguez will pitch on Sunday against the division-rival Baltimore Orioles in the final game of the 2026 regular season, weather permitting, according to Bryan Hoch of MLB.com. It will be Rodriguez's seventh start in his first year in the big leagues, and his first since he allowed four earned runs in 3 2/3 innings with three walks and five strikeouts in a loss to the Los Angeles Angels on the road on Aug. 31. The 23-year-old Puerto Rican native is 0-3 with the Yankees this year with a 5.40 ERA (4.86 FIP) and 1.57 WHIP with 21 strikeouts and 16 walks in 26 2/3 innings pitched over his six starts. The former fourth-rounder by the Boston Red Sox in 2021 went 8-4 with a 2.45 ERA, 1.31 WHIP, and 105:54 K:BB in 106 1/3 innings across 21 starts in the minors for Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre. Rodriguez is the team's No. 2 overall prospect, per MLB Pipeline, but his lack of control at the major-league level in a small sample size will make him extremely risky for fantasy managers still vying for a championship on the final weekend of the regular season.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com - Bryan Hoch
Jeff Hoffman Lands on Injured List to End the Season


Keith Hernandez




Sep 26, 2026, 12:39 PM ET
The Minnesota Twins placed right-handed reliever Jeff Hoffman (forearm) on the 15-day injured list on Saturday with inflammation in his right forearm, according to Aaron Gleeman. The Twins activated shortstop prospect Kaelen Culpepper (hamstring) from the 10-day injured list in a corresponding move. After blowing the save in Game 7 of last year's World Series against the Dodgers, Hoffman finishes his 2026 campaign with a 6-8 record, 3.55 ERA (2.47 FIP), a 1.32 WHIP, only six saves, a career-high 102 strikeouts, and 30 walks in 66 innings out of the bullpen for the Twins and Toronto Blue Jays. He had five of his six saves on the year in Toronto, but also an ERA near 4.00. Although Hoffman was used as more of a late-inning setup man after being acquired in a trade by Minnesota, he fared better in his 20 relief outings with the Twins, with a 2.50 ERA, 1.17 WHIP, and 27:12 K:BB in 18 innings pitched. Despite not seeing many save chances, Hoffman picked up a career-high 22 holds and was still very valuable in fantasy formats that reward points for holds.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Aaron Gleeman
Kaelen Culpepper Returns From Injured List on Saturday


Keith Hernandez




Sep 26, 2026, 12:32 PM ET
The Minnesota Twins officially activated shortstop prospect Kaelen Culpepper (hamstring) from the 10-day injured list on Saturday and placed right-handed reliever Jeff Hoffman (forearm) on the 15-day injured list with inflammation in his right forearm in a corresponding move, according to Aaron Gleeman. The Twins have elected to bring Culpepper back for the final two games of the regular season after he was placed on the IL on Sept. 16 with a left-hamstring strain. He should be back in action on Saturday evening at home against the Texas Rangers and right-hander Nathan Eovaldi. The 23-year-old former first-rounder in 2024 from Kansas State University is viewed as the team's shortstop of the future, and MLB Pipeline has him ranked as Minnesota's No. 3 overall prospect, behind only outfielder Walker Jenkins and catcher Vahn Lackey. Culpepper has looked good in his first 109 major-league at-bats, hitting .275 with three home runs, 11 RBI, 15 runs scored, and a stolen base. He brings a strong contact-oriented approach with good bat speed and the ability to send line drives to all parts of the field.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Aaron Gleeman
Sep 26, 2026, 12:27 PM ET
Arizona Diamondbacks manager Torey Lovullo said that catcher Gabriel Moreno (hamstring) left Friday night's win over the division-rival San Diego Padres with a tender left hamstring, according to Steve Gilbert of MLB.com. The skipper expects Moreno to be in the starting lineup on Saturday night at Petco Park as the designated hitter. The D-backs will call up a catcher to have another backup just in case. Outfielder Jesus Sanchez was designated for assignment to open up a spot on the roster. In the Snakes' 11-4 victory on Friday night, Moreno went 2-for-3 at the plate with an RBI, two runs scored, and a walk before being replaced behind the dish by James McCann. The D-backs can ill-afford to lose their starting catcher with just two games remaining in the regular season, as the Venezuelan backstop is hitting over .300 on the year with 16 home runs. Arizona enters play on Saturday just one game behind the Philadelphia Phillies for the final wild-card spot in the National League with two games left to play.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com - Steve Gilbert
Sep 25, 2026, 10:00 PM ET
Milwaukee Brewers first baseman Andrew Vaughn (illness) was placed on the 10-day Injured List on Friday, retroactive to Tuesday. Before Friday's game, Vaughn had been sidelined for four straight games due to a lingering illness. The Brewers decided to place him on the shelf now, so Vaughn will be eligible to return before the postseason on October 3. This season, Vaughn slashed .306/.390/.444 with six home runs and 43 RBI across 331 plate appearances. In a corresponding move, outfielder Brandon Lockridge has been recalled to give the Brewers a fresh body for the final few games of the regular season.--Andy Webb
Source: Milwaukee Brewers
Sep 25, 2026, 9:53 PM ET
Arizona Diamondbacks starting pitcher Corbin Burnes (shoulder) was placed on the 15-day Injured List on Friday. Burnes was expected to make his final start of the season on Sunday, but instead, he'll go to the shelf due to right shoulder inflammation. Burnes only made three starts this season as he missed most of the year while recovering from Tommy John surgery. He was lit up for a 7.84 ERA and 1.55 WHIP across his 10.1 innings of work this season. The D-Backs still have a chance to make the postseason, so there's a chance that Burnes can contribute in October. His regular season is over, and it's unclear what exactly fantasy managers should expect out of Burnes next season.--Andy Webb
Source: Arizona Diamondbacks
Chandler Simpson Exits with Foot Injury


Andy Webb




Sep 25, 2026, 9:43 PM ET
Tampa Bay Rays outfielder Chandler Simpson (foot) was forced to make an early exit during Friday's game against the Philadelphia Phillies, Marc Topkin reports. Simpson sustained an injury after fouling a ball off his foot in the sixth inning. He attempted to stay in the game, but he was pulled in the seventh inning. He was hitless during his three plate appearances during the victory over the Phillies. The expectation is that he'll undergo imaging to determine the severity of the injury. For now, Simpson should be considered day-to-day until more information is known.--Andy Webb
Source: Marc Topkin
Sep 25, 2026, 9:25 PM ET
Texas Rangers third baseman Josh Jung (hand) was removed from Friday's game against the Minnesota Twins. Jung was taken out of the game after getting hit by a pitch on the hand, Kennedi Landry reports. He remained in the game to run the bases and play the field, but Jung was removed for a pinch-hitter once his spot in the batting order came up again. Before being removed, Jung went hitless with a run scored. The assumption is that Jung will undergo X-rays to determine the severity of the injury. Cody Freeman would likely see more starts at third base if Jung is forced to miss any time. Fantasy managers should check back on Saturday for another update on Jung.--Andy Webb
Source: Kennedi Landry
Andres Munoz Goes to 15-Day Injured List


Andy Webb




Sep 25, 2026, 9:16 PM ET
Seattle Mariners relief pitcher Andres Munoz (knee) was placed on the 15-day Injured List on Friday, Ryan Divish reports. Munoz hasn't pitched since Sunday and now goes to the shelf due to right knee inflammation. His inconsistent 2026 season will now come to an end with a few games left in the regular season. He'll finish the season with a 4.24 ERA, 1.22 WHIP, and an 89/24 K/BB ratio with 28 saves across 57.2 innings of work. The expectation is that Jose A. Ferrer and Seranthony Dominguez will work in save situations over the final few days of the regular season. Fantasy managers should expect Munoz to be back in the closer role and fully healthy for the start of next season.--Andy Webb
Source: Ryan Divish
Xavier Edwards Still Out for Marlins


Keith Hernandez




Sep 25, 2026, 6:07 PM ET
Miami Marlins middle infielder Xavier Edwards (thumb) remains out of the starting nine for Friday's series opener at home against the division-rival Atlanta Braves, per MLB.com. Jared Serna will make another start at second base for the Fish and will hit in the nine-hole against Braves left-hander Ray Kerr. This will be Edwards' fifth straight missed game after he aggravated a left-thumb injury last Saturday against the San Diego Padres. The Marlins have not rushed the 27-year-old back after being eliminated from playoff contention. At this point, he only has two more chances to return before the end of the regular season on Saturday and Sunday against Atlanta. The switch-hitting middle infielder was having a second straight solid season for the Fish this year, slashing .280/.360/.371 with a .730 OPS, a career-high six home runs, 52 RBI, 21 stolen bases, and 61 runs scored across 142 games and 595 plate appearances. You are not going to get any power from Edwards, but he remains useful for his speed and contact-oriented approach at the dish in fantasy leagues.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com
Luis Arraez Out on Friday, Report "Not a Great One"


Keith Hernandez




Sep 25, 2026, 6:01 PM ET
Philadelphia Phillies infielder Luis Arraez (ankle) is out of the team's starting lineup on Friday against the visiting Tampa Bay Rays, and the report on his ankle injury from Thursday night is "not a great one," interim manager Don Mattingly told Scott Lauber of The Philadelphia Inquirer. Mattingly did not give a grade on the sprain, and the Phillies have not decided on an injured-list placement, which would take Arraez out until at least Oct. 5, or around Game 3 of the divisional round. X-rays on Arraez's left ankle came back negative on Thursday night, but his sprained ankle is still stiff and sore, which is why he will not play on Friday. Bryson Stott is at second base and batting fifth on Friday, with Edmundo Sosa at third base and hitting ninth against Rays right-hander Freddy Peralta. The Phillies would obviously love to avoid putting the 29-year-old All-Star on the IL, but if he cannot play at all this weekend, they might have no choice. The four-time All-Star and three-time batting champion has hit only .278 (49-for-176) in his 46 games with the Phillies this year after being traded from the San Francisco Giants in early August, but he is still the league's leading hitter at .310 overall. Not having Arraez available next week for the start of the playoffs (if the Phillies qualify) would be a big loss for Philadelphia.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Philadelphia Inquirer - Scott Lauber
Zyhir Hope Appears To Be Future Fantasy Star


Brian Buckey




Sep 25, 2026, 1:46 PM ET
Detroit Tigers new top outfield prospect Zyhir Hope showed off plenty of promise with Double-A Erie following his trade from the Dodgers in the Tarik Skubal deal. Hope was the headline piece coming back to Detroit after dealing away their ace, and he proved his potential with a massive minor-league season at the Double-A level between the Dodgers and Tigers. The 21-year-old left-handed hitter combined to hit .287 with 29 homers and 111 RBI to go with 86 runs scored and 26 stolen bases. Hope has a 50-grade hit tool with 60-grade power and 55-grade speed. The future is bright for Hope, and he could make his debut with the Tigers in 2027. Expect the five-category skills Hope has shown in the minors to translate to the big leagues, making him a great target for fantasy managers as soon as next season.--Brian Buckey - RotoBaller
Source: Minor League Baseball
Caden Hunter Looks Like Future Fantasy Ace


Brian Buckey




Sep 25, 2026, 1:38 PM ET
Baltimore Orioles pitching prospect Caden Hunter turned in a dominant 2026 minor-league season between three levels. Finishing up at Double-A Chesapeake in his age-22 season, Hunter combined to pitch to a 5-3 record with a 2.01 ERA and 1.06 WHIP with 151 strikeouts in 103 innings pitched. In his first professional season out of USC, Hunter dominated to hold opposing hitters to a .171 batting average. The 6-foot-2, 205-pound left-hander is the No. 4 overall prospect of the Orioles and boasts a 60-grade fastball and a 55-grade slider and changeup combination with a 45-grade curveball. Hunter looks like a future fantasy star with the size and skills to be a dominant force on the mound with the Orioles in the future. Look for more of Hunter in the minors in 2027, with the potential to make his MLB debut as soon as next season.--Brian Buckey - RotoBaller
Source: Minor League Baseball
Sep 25, 2026, 1:27 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers pitching prospect Christian Zazueta combined between High-A Great Lakes and Double-A Tulsa to have a stellar age-21 minor-league season in 2026. Zazueta's overall numbers ended up very good, with a combined 6-4 record, 3.65 ERA, and 0.97 WHIP with 144 strikeouts in 103 2/3 innings. The 6-foot-3 right-hander limited opposing batters to a .214 batting average. He is the No. 5 prospect in the Dodgers' system with a 60-grade fastball and changeup combination with a 50-grade secondary pitch in his slider. Zazueta shows very good control and looks to have all the tools to be a future fantasy-relevant pitcher. It could be a few years before Zazueta makes his MLB debut, but he looks like a great dynasty-league addition in the near term.--Brian Buckey - RotoBaller
Source: Minor League Baseball
Connelly Early to Pitch This Weekend


Keith Hernandez




Sep 25, 2026, 1:26 PM ET
Washington Nationals left-hander Connelly Early (elbow) threw 40 pitches across 1 2/3 innings with Triple-A Rochester on Sept. 20 and will come off the 60-day injured list to make one more start this season this weekend against the division-rival New York Mets, according to MLB.com. Early landed on the injured list on July 1 and was moved to the 60-day IL on Aug. 22 due to inflammation in his left elbow. It will be his first start with the Nationals after the team acquired him from the Boston Red Sox at the trade deadline in early August. In his 17 starts (91 2/3 innings pitched) for the BoSox this year in his second season in the big leagues, Early went 7-5 with a 3.44 ERA (4.60 FIP) and 1.25 WHIP with 93 strikeouts and 34 walks. He had a 2.33 ERA and 1.09 WHIP in a smaller sample size of only four starts in his first taste of the big leagues near the end of the 2025 campaign. Early, a fifth-rounder from Virginia in 2023, is one of the more intriguing young lefty arms in baseball, but he will be far too risky in starting fantasy lineups with championships on the line this weekend against New York after his long injury layoff. UPDATE: Early will make his Nationals debut on Saturday.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com
Sep 25, 2026, 1:19 PM ET
Detroit Tigers catcher prospect Josue Briceno overcame wrist surgery and battled a late ankle injury in what was an injury-plagued age 22 minor league season. Briceno combined between four minor-league levels in 2026 to combine for a .250 batting average with nine homers and 29 RBI and 23 runs in 42 total games. Briceno played 15 games at Triple-A Toledo and hit just .196 in a very small sample size. He hit .297 in 17 games at Double-A Erie prior to his call up to Toledo. Briceno is the No. 4 prospect of the Tigers and has a 50-grade hit tool with 60-grade power. The catcher position is in good shape in Detroit with All-Star Dillon Dingler and Eduardo Valencia. Briceno is a power bat with limited speed that could potentially shift to first base or find a spot at DH if needed, but he is still a big part of the future plans for Tigers brass and could make a 2027 debut.--Brian Buckey - RotoBaller
Source: Minor League Baseball
Sep 25, 2026, 1:10 PM ET
Washington Nationals shortstop prospect Devin Fitz-Gerald split his minor-league season between two levels but finished with nice overall numbers in his age-21 season. Between High-A Wilmington and Double-A Harrisburg, Fitz-Gerald combined to hit .251 with 20 homers and 67 RBI, along with 15 stolen bases and 78 runs scored. The switch-hitter was originally drafted by the Texas Rangers and came to the Nationals organization in the MacKenzie Gore trade. Fitz-Gerald is the No. 5 prospect for the Nationals and has a 50-grade hit tool with 50-grade power and 45-grade speed. Fitz-Gerald looks like he could be an impact player for the Nationals, but Washington does have another elite shortstop prospect in Seaver King, so Fitz-Gerald's future could involve another infield position.--Brian Buckey - RotoBaller
Source: Minor League Baseball
Sep 25, 2026, 1:01 PM ET
Tampa Bay Rays first base prospect Xavier Isaac had a good minor league season at age 22 and closed it off well with a good stint at Triple-A Durham. Called up to Durham from Double-A Montgomery on August 25, Isaac played 18 games with the Durham Bulls down the stretch. He finished that stint with three homers and eight RBI in 59 at bats with a .271 batting average and 11 runs scored. Altogether between Montgomery and Durham, Isaac combined to hit .258 with 27 homers and 79 RBI to go with 20 stolen bases and 88 runs scored. Isaac is the No. 18 prospect in the Rays system and looks like he could be ready for a role on the 2027 Rays team. Isaac appears to be a promising talent with 60-grade power, but just a 35-grade hit tool. He could be a good homer and RBI threat but leave something to be desired in the batting average category.--Brian Buckey - RotoBaller
Source: Minor League Baseball
Sep 25, 2026, 11:38 AM ET
Boston Red Sox first baseman Willson Contreras (hand) is out of the starting lineup yet again for Game 1 of a doubleheader on Friday against the visiting Chicago Cubs at Fenway Park, according to MLB.com. On Thursday night, a week after he was hit on the knuckle between the ring finger and pinkie on his right hand, Contreras expressed concern about his availability for the start of the wild-card series in the American League next week. "I mean, it's really concerning," said Contreras. "But at the same time, I'm putting all my effort -- and everything I can do, I'm doing it. I don't know what else to say. I'm working hard with the trainers; the hand is slowly getting better. But I haven't been able to swing the last two days." If the Red Sox do not have Contreras, their best power hitter this season, it will be a big blow to their chances of making a deep postseason run. Before injuries struck this month, Contreras was having a career year in his first season with the team, slashing .276/.387/.518 with 27 home runs and 81 RBI in 129 games played. Andruw Monasterio is starting at first base for Game 1 on Friday and is hitting eighth against Cubs right-hander Clay Holmes.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dylan Cease Gets Good Injury Update Heading into Offseason
item.dc:creator: Brady Farkas
item.description: Unfortunately for the Toronto Blue Jays, the offseason is coming sooner than anyone wants. But at least for Dylan Cease, that offseason will be a relatively normal one. As reported by Arden Zwelling of Sportsnet, Cease will take a few weeks off to let the swelling in his right shoulder settle down, but he anticipates a regular offseason and being fine for spring training in 2027. item.content:encoded:
Unfortunately for the Toronto Blue Jays, the offseason is coming sooner than anyone wants.
But at least for Dylan Cease, that offseason will be a relatively normal one.
As reported by Arden Zwelling of Sportsnet, Cease will take a few weeks off to let the swelling in his right shoulder settle down, but he anticipates a regular offseason and being fine for spring training in 2027.
Cease started eight days ago against the Texas Rangers but went back to Toronto for an MRI following that start. His scheduled start on Wednesday was pushed back and then when the Blue Jays were eliminated from playoff contention, he was shut down and put on the injured list.
The big question
Cease says he plans to be ready for spring training, but of course, the question is: when will spring training actually take place?
With the collective bargaining agreement set to expire on Dec. 2, there's plenty of chatter about a lockout that eats into the 2027 campaign. So, obviously, spring training beginning in mid-February is not a guarantee.
The other thing to note is this: Once Dec. 2 happens, if a lockout does come, players will be prohibited from talking with MLB personnel, including team trainers. So, Cease will have to stay on top of his communication and rehab plan with the training staff prior to that date. I'm sure he will, but it's important to note still.
An incredible year
Signed to a seven-year, $210 million deal last offseason, Cease was everything the Jays could have wanted in a staff ace. He made 29 starts, going 11-6 with a 2.40 ERA. He struck out 239 batters in 169.0 innings, also leading the league in hits/9, homers/9 and strikeouts/9. He's likely to finish second in the American League Cy Young voting to Cam Schlittler of the New York Yankees.
Opponents hit only .180 against him. Cease had started 30 games or more in five straight seasons, a streak that has come to an end.
Looking ahead
With Kevin Gausman out of the rotation, Cease will be the headliner in 2027 and beyond. He figures to pair with Jose Soriano, Trey Yesavage and Cody Ponce in that regard, with the fifth spot up for grabs.
As for the current Blue Jays? They'll finish out the regular season with two more games against the Cincinnati Reds at Rogers Centre. First pitch on Saturday is set for 3:07 p.m. ET as Yesavage takes the mound against Reds righty Rhett Lowder, who is 6-11.

item.content:encoded:
Against the odds, Nolan Arenado is a 30-home run hitter for the Diamondbacks
Arenado joined a short list of third basemen with eight different 30-home run seasons, with the benchmark of 400 for his career within reach next season.
(Photo by Orlando Ramirez/Getty Images)
SAN DIEGO — Nolan Arenado hit 28 home runs combined over the previous two seasons before the Arizona Diamondbacks traded for the third baseman last offseason.
Defense and leadership were the baseline expectations for Arenado in Arizona, and whatever was left in the tank offensively was bonus.
In his age 35 campaign, Arenado has clubbed 30 home runs, punishing a hanging slider from San Diego Padres pitcher Casey Mize on Friday to hit a mark he had not reached since 2022. That year, Arenado was a finalist for the National League MVP with the St. Louis Cardinals.
He has experienced some quieter times since then, suggesting he declined to the point where he could no longer be relied on as an impact bat for a lineup.
The potential future Hall of Famer has reversed time this season for a team that has sorely needed the production.
“It meant a lot,” Arenado told Arizona Sports after hitting his 30th home run. “Just from where I started and just where I’ve been the last couple of years. It hasn’t been easy, but I just thank God that I’ve been healthy. And I owe a lot of credit to the hitting coaches for challenging me and all these guys for challenging me to take chances and work on things.”
Nolan Arenado is on a HEATER!
9 HR in September, 30 HR on the season 😯 pic.twitter.com/1ZcIDpDnmo
— MLB (@MLB) September 26, 2026
Arenado was visibly amped running the bases after the blast that put the D-backs ahead 6-2 in a must-win game they would take 11-4. The Southern California native also did it in front of his parents and brother, who made the hour drive south to watch him play.
“That was really cool,” Arenado said.
This is the eighth time Arenado has hit 30 home runs in a season. 28 players all-time have more such seasons and only two while spending most of their time at third base, per Stathead: Hall of Famers Mike Schmidt (12) and Eddie Mathews (10).
Arenado did so from 2015-19 and picked the streak back up after the shortened 2020 campaign in 2021-22.
This is the outlier outside his prime, especially after he hit 12 home runs last season.
“He has regained a lot of that offensive magic that’s been with him for so long,” manager Torey Lovullo said.
When asked about his offense’s recent success, Diamondbacks general manager Mike Hazen said on Friday, “We’re hitting more home runs. Arenado’s hitting a home run every night.”
Arenado has homered nine times in September, second in Major League Baseball to Baltimore’s Pete Alonso (11). He owns an .889 OPS in the second half of this season. And his four home runs in the past five games have come at a time when the Diamondbacks have had to win to keep their playoff hopes alive.
Arenado joked on the Diamondbacks TV broadcast Friday night that he is probably making Arizona’s hitting coaches work harder than they ever had before. He gave hitting coach Joe Mather a big hug in the dugout after going yard.
Arenado came to Arizona with a reputation of being a maniacal competitor and worker.
He has aimed to challenge himself during his preparation before games to get his body up to speed at this age, not totally dissimilar to Eugenio Suarez when he turned around his 2024 season in Arizona. The veteran has said lately he has cooled off the pregame physical work to maintain his body this late in the season, which has paid off.
Health has also been a factor, as Arenado dealt with shoulder issues at the end of his St. Louis tenure that he felt hampered him. He has been banged up in the second half of this season (intercostal, thumb) but has managed to limit his time off the field.
Before Friday’s game, Arenado stood in the batter’s box with his headphones and a bat, practicing his load and stride. Nobody was throwing batting practice yet, and there were still tamps and other grounds-keeping equipment on the field. Perhaps he was visualizing what soon became reality when he shot a ball into the Western Metal Supply Co. building.
Lars Nootbaar has had a front-row seat to Arenado’s career since he came up with the Cardinals in 2021, reuniting with the veteran at this past trade deadline.
“I just think that if anybody saw what he does and what he goes through on a daily basis and to try to get himself in a good position and be as obsessive as he is and be as passionate as he is, to get rewarded in this game and to be able to hit 30 in front of his family, that’s really cool from a baseball fan perspective and friend,” Nootbaar said.
Geraldo Perdomo predicted this re-breakout season back in spring training, and he claims to have called Arenado going for 30 home runs a couple weeks ago.
“I’m happy for him,” Perdomo said. “He’s the type of player who works every day hard in the cages with the hitting coaches to get better.”
Arenado enters Saturday second among qualified D-backs hitters with an .803 OPS, ahead of Corbin Carroll and Ketel Marte and trailing Gabriel Moreno.
He has previously been candid about wishing he has had more success this year with runners in scoring position, a shortcoming for large chunks of the season both individually and team-wide. He is batting .228 in those spots, although the OPS has climbed to .745.
This is not quite the MVP-candidate version of Arenado’s prime, but there is no doubt that the Diamondbacks acquiring him from St. Louis without having to pay the majority of his contract was a steal. It is arguably the biggest win of Hazen’s offseason.
Arenado is up to 383 career home runs, as the celebrated 400 benchmark is within grasp in 2027. MLB also revealed the 20 top-selling jerseys for the 2026 season, and Arenado was 19th on the list, the highest Diamondback.
For now and most importantly, with the D-backs trailing the final NL Wild Card spot by one game with two to play, can Arenado push this hot streak a couple games further?

item.content:encoded:
El cerrador mexicano Andrés Muñoz sufrió un amargo cierre en la Temporada 2026 de las Grandes Ligas de Béisbol (MLB) después de que, al sufrir una inflamación en la rodilla derecha, los Mariners lo colocaron en la lista de lesionados y se perderá los últimos juegos del calendario regular.
La salida del taponero mexicano es un movimiento preventivo para los Mariners que ya fueron eliminados de la pelea por un boleto a los playoffs el jueves pasado.
Se acabó la temporada para Andrés Muñoz
Muñoz, colocado en la lista de lesionados por 15 días, comenzó a sentir molestias desde una semana antes en la gira del equipo por Colorado. El domingo anterior comenzó a sentir ciertas molestias en la rodilla y abandonó el juego después de un breve intercambio con el manager Dan Wilson y el preparador físico Kevin Orloski.
El Plebe fue sometido a diversos exámenes cuando el club regresó a Seattle, cuyos resultados revelaron que no se trataba de “nada serio, nada preocupante desde el punto de vista estructural”, aseguró en su momento el gerente general Justin Hollander.
Roster moves:
???? Troy Taylor, RHP, recalled from Triple-A Tacoma.
???? Andrés Muñoz, RHP, placed on the 15-day Injured List (right knee inflammation).
????: https://t.co/CSdqzDzEP5 pic.twitter.com/zLeQkUf7pb
Andrés estuvo fuera de acción los siguientes tres juegos, incluso el miércoles cuando los Mariners ganaron un juego de 10 entradas a los Astros, cuando hubo situaciones de alto calibre en las que pudo haber ingresado.
“Siguió sintiendo molestias al llegar a casa”, dijo el manager Dan Wilson luego del juego del viernes. “Y, dada la etapa de la temporada en la que nos encontramos, tenía mucho sentido enviarlo a la lista de lesionados en este momento. No hay razón para forzarlo a estas alturas de la campaña; por mucho que queramos contar con él, si no está en condiciones de jugar, hay que pensárselo dos veces”.
Amargo final para el cerrador mexicano
El movimiento pone fin a una temporada llena de altas y bajas para el mochitense. En su lugar, Troy Taylor fue ascendido por el equipo desde su filial Triple-A.
Andres Muñoz has been placed on the 15 day IL, per @DKramer_
Troy Taylor has been called up subsequently#TridentsUp pic.twitter.com/qOkxWpl9hK
Andrés terminó la temporada con una efectividad de 4.24 y 10 salvamentos fallados, la cifra más alta en todas las Grandes Ligas junto a Kyle Finnegan, de los Nationals. La temporada se quedó lejos de los resultados que obtuvo durante los dos años anteriores, cuando fue llamado al Juego de Estrellas.

item.content:encoded:
이런 더블 히트(두 번 맞추는 안타)를 본 적이 있으십니까?
제대로 배트 중심에 맞았다고 말할 수 있는 순간이었습니다.
토론토 블루제이스의 1루수 블라디미르 게레로 주니어는 25일(미국 현지시간) 로저스 센터에서 열린 신시내티 레즈와의 경기에서 6-5 승리를 거둔 7회초에 기술적으로 타점 적시타를 만들어냈지만, 그 과정은 꽤나 특이했습니다.
신시내티의 불펜 투수 루이스 메이의 0-2 카운트 싱커를 상대로, 게레로는 가운데 방향으로 땅볼을 쳐냈고 그 과정에서 배트가 두 토막으로 부러졌습니다. 그러자 순수한 야구의 마법이 펼쳐졌습니다.
슬로모션 리플레이는 정확히 무슨 일이 일어났는지 보여주었습니다. 게레로의 부러진 배트 동체 조각이 홈플레이트 전방 수 피트 앞에서 야구공과 다시 부딪히며 공의 진로를 내야 오른쪽 방향으로 꺾어놓았습니다. 공은 레즈 수비진의 빈틈을 굴러 우익수 앞 안타가 되었고, 2루에 있던 안드레스 히메네스를 홈으로 불러들였습니다.
토론토에 리드를 안기고 결국 승리로 이어진 결정적인 7회 4득점 빅이닝의 첫 득점을 만들어낸 게레로의 이 안타는 선수가 공을 두 번 치는 일이 발생한 최초의 안타가 결코 아니었습니다. 사실, 하루에만 두 번 나온 사례를 포함하여 이번 시즌에만 적어도 여섯 번째로 발생한 일입니다.
게레로가 머릿속으로 그리던 완벽한 정타는 분명 아니었지만, 금요일에 나온 이 더블 히트는 진정 기발한 방식으로 "수비가 없는 곳으로 타구를 보내는" 결과를 만들어냈습니다.

item.title: [bolavip.com] Blue Jays’ Vladimir Guerrero Jr. regrets past comments, discusses contract extension
item.dc:creator: Santiago Tovar
item.description: Fresh off a run as the AL pennant runners-up last season, the Toronto Blue Jays have officially been eliminated from 2026 postseason contention. Toronto has turned its focus toward next year—and to expecting a return to form from star slugger Vladimir Guerrero Jr., who signed a massive contract extension with the club. However, recent comments from Guerrero Jr. sparked a firestorm among the fan base over the week. On Friday, the first baseman spoke to the media alongside his Hall of Fame father
item.content:encoded:
Fresh off a run as the AL pennant runners-up last season, the Toronto Blue Jays have officially been eliminated from 2026 postseason contention. Toronto has turned its focus toward next year—and to expecting a return to form from star slugger Vladimir Guerrero Jr., who signed a massive contract extension with the club.
However, recent comments from Guerrero Jr. sparked a firestorm among the fan base over the week. On Friday, the first baseman spoke to the media alongside his Hall of Fame father to address the controversy and express regret over his statement. “I feel like the comments I made the other day didn’t accurately reflect what I really wanted to say. Everyone deserves an apology from me,” Guerrero Jr. told reporters.
Guerrero ignited a wave of backlash across social media after an interview posted by content creator Masterflip, during which the slugger remarked that the Blue Jays “didn’t pay me to hit 40 [home runs] every year.”
While other MLB contenders scratch and claw for a postseason berth—such as the Philadelphia Phillies, who missed an opportunity to lock up their spot heading into October—the Blue Jays find themselves navigating internal turbulence surrounding the face of their franchise.
Vladimir Guerrero Jr. #27 of the Toronto Blue Jays.
Vladdy’s struggles this season
Following a dominant 2025 campaign, Guerrero Jr. has endured a surprisingly down year. His lingering struggles at the plate are reflected in his numbers: just nine home runs and 56 RBIs through 142 games.
Guerrero has been hampered by various nagging injuries throughout the year, missing around 17 games. Playing through constant physical discomfort has prevented him from finding a rhythm or establishing consistent timing in the batter’s box.
MLB legend weighs in on Guerrero Jr.’s comments
Addressing the noise surrounding the Toronto star, MLB legend Pedro Martinez stepped up to defend Guerrero Jr.’s intent. “He was misinterpreted. What he meant is that contract came from what he’s already done and what he can still do,” Martinez said to El Emergente’s Marcos Grunfeld. “That’s a young man talking—he just didn’t explain himself the right way.”
Despite the current turmoil, Vladdy still has plenty of time to prove that his long-term contract extension was well-earned. If he can turn things around next spring, he remains positioned to re-establish himself as one of the premier hitters in Major League Baseball.
Key takeaways
- Vladimir Guerrero Jr. apologized for recent comments that sparked backlash among fans.
- MLB legend Pedro Martinez defended the slugger, stating his comments were misinterpreted.
- The Toronto Blue Jays have been officially eliminated from 2026 postseason contention.

item.title: [The Times of India] Juan Soto’s $765 million New York Mets contract made MLB history: The numbers, salary structure, bonuses and clauses behind baseball’s biggest superstar deal
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk
item.description: Juan Soto’s trade to the New York Mets was one of the biggest money moments in Major League Baseball history. The four-time All-Star agreed to a 15-year, $765 million deal after the 2024 season, topping Shohei Ohtani’s previous record $700 million deal with the Los Angeles Dodgers in total contract value. When the deal was finalised in December 2024, MLB dubbed the contract the largest in league history. But that headline figure is only part of the story. Soto’s deal features a $75 million signi
item.content:encoded:
Juan Soto’s trade to the New York Mets was one of the biggest money moments in Major League Baseball history. The four-time All-Star agreed to a 15-year, $765 million deal after the 2024 season, topping Shohei Ohtani’s previous record $700 million deal with the Los Angeles Dodgers in total contract value. When the deal was finalised in December 2024, MLB dubbed the contract the largest in league history.
But that headline figure is only part of the story. Soto’s deal features a $75 million signing bonus and no deferred money, along with an opt-out after the 2029 season. The New York Mets have a provision that can eliminate that opt-out by increasing the annual value of the last 10 seasons, possibly moving the deal from $765 million to $805 million.
Juan Soto’s Mets contract remains MLB’s defining blockbuster after historic $765 million agreement
The original $765 million agreement for Juan Soto with the New York Mets is a 15-year deal from 2025-39 with an average annual value of $51 million.
When finished, it was the biggest and longest deal in MLB history and raised the bar for what free agents could get paid.
The deal came after Soto had finished the 2024 season with the New York Yankees. In his only season in the Bronx, Soto hit .288 with a .419 on-base percentage and .569 slugging percentage, belting 41 homers and scoring 109 runs in 157 games.
He was also third in MVP voting in the American League.
| Contract detail | Juan Soto |
| Team | New York Mets |
| Contract length | 15 years |
| Total value | $765 million |
| Average annual value | $51 million |
| Signing bonus | $75 million |
| Contract period | 2025–2039 |
| Deferred compensation | None |
| Player opt-out | After 2029 season |
| Potential maximum value | $805 million |
The $765 million headline immediately established a new standard for MLB free-agent contracts. Juan Soto surpassed Shohei Ohtani’s $700 million deal with the Los Angeles Dodgers that was signed after the 2023 season. MLB called Soto’s contract the largest free agent deal in league history in total value.
The comparison is further complicated by the timing of payment and the average annual value. Soto’s original deal has an AAV of $51 million, and Ohtani’s $700 million contract has an AAV of $70 million on paper. But Ohtani’s deal has a lot of deferred compensation, so the timing of payments is fundamentally different from Soto’s contract.
Juan Soto and New York Mets built-in contract protections
One of the more unusual aspects of Juan Soto’s deal is the opt-out after the 2029 season. Soto can invoke the clause after five seasons with the New York Mets, and potentially hit the free-agent market at age 31.
But the Mets have a contractual mechanism to prevent the opt-out. The opt-out can be voided if the club increases the average annual value of the final 10 years from $51 million to $55 million. That would push the total contract value to $805 million and the effective AAV over the life of the full deal to roughly $53.67 million.
Another key part of the deal is the $75 million signing bonus. Combined with the salary structure, it adds to the overall value of the deal and makes the contract very different from a simple 15-year salary deal. MLB reported the signing bonus along with the lack of deferred money when describing the deal.
There are financial incentives in Juan Soto’s contract based on performance on top of the guaranteed money. Reportedly includes bonuses tied to National League MVP voting, which adds another layer to the financial structure.
Reported incentives include $500,000 for Soto's first National League MVP award, with bigger bonuses for subsequent MVP wins. There are also bonus payments to high finishers in the voting, including a reported $350,000 for second and $150,000 for a third through fifth place finish.
Juan Soto’s deal compared with Shohei Ohtani’s record
Juan Soto’s New York Mets contract and Shohei Ohtani’s Los Angeles Dodgers deal are two different takes on baseball’s new mega-contracts. The total value of Soto’s deal is bigger, but Ohtani’s contract has a higher stated AAV.
| Financial comparison | Juan Soto | Shohei Ohtani |
| Team | New York Mets | Los Angeles Dodgers |
| Contract length | 15 years | 10 years |
| Total value | $765 million | $700 million |
| Stated AAV | $51 million | $70 million |
| Deferred compensation | None | Significant deferrals |
| Signing year | 2024 | 2023 |
Soto’s 15-year, $765 million contract is higher in total value than Ohtani’s 10-year, $700 million deal, according to MLB’s historical contract records. Soto also set a new record for the longest MLB contract, and Ohtani's deal remains one of the most financially unique because of its extensive deferral structure.
The difference in length of the contract is very important. Soto is signed through 2039, meaning the New York Mets get a long-term commitment for one of the best hitters in baseball. Ohtani’s Dodgers contract is for 10 years, through 2033, but it’s structured to push most of the money into the future.
Juan Soto’s New York Mets contract sets a new benchmark
Soto’s deal also fits into a larger trend of ever-growing MLB contracts. Aaron Judge’s nine-year, $360 million deal with the New York Yankees had set the free-agent standard after the 2022 season, before Ohtani signed his $700 million deal. Soto then added $65 million in total guaranteed value to the ceiling.
Soto’s deal is notable for reasons beyond the record-shattering headline and its contract structure. It’s a 15-year deal with a $75 million signing bonus, no deferred money, an opt-out provision and a possible $805 million escalator, all of which combine to make it a contract unlike the typical long-term MLB contract.
The pact binds the New York Mets deep into the next decade. For Juan Soto, it provides a huge guaranteed money platform with a possible decision point after the 2029 season. That’s why the financial specifics of the deal have been a hot topic throughout MLB, blending long-term security with contractual flexibility.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Where has Kyle Schwarber gone?
item.dc:creator: Ethan Witte
item.description: We are all aware of the reputation Philadelphia has when it comes to underperforming athletes in this city. There are "boo birds" out en masse if a player does something that the city thinks isn't up to their standards. Last night, against Tampa Bay, the fans were restless as scoring chance after scoring chance went wasted, frittered away by an offense that is so clearly pressing it's barely funny. When that ire is thrown from the stands, the suspects are usually the ones that have underperforme
item.content:encoded:
We are all aware of the reputation Philadelphia has when it comes to underperforming athletes in this city. There are "boo birds" out en masse if a player does something that the city thinks isn't up to their standards. Last night, against Tampa Bay, the fans were restless as scoring chance after scoring chance went wasted, frittered away by an offense that is so clearly pressing it's barely funny.
When that ire is thrown from the stands, the suspects are usually the ones that have underperformed seemingly since the day they arrived. Trea Turner has been the subject of many a negative comment both in these parts and at the stadium in person. Alec Bohm frequently hears from the people when one of his cold streak appears out of nowhere. Much people's current distaste has been directed at the currently 0 for his last 32 J.T. Realmuto, all of that completely justified.
However, there needs to be some criticism lobbed at the leadoff hitter. Kyle Schwarber has not just been ineffective lately, he's been pretty ineffective for a while now.
The supposed fulcrum of the Phillies offense has been off for not just a little bit now. If we're looking at recent runs, Schwarber's last 14 days has seen him hit .143/.345/.262 with one home run. Stretch that back even 28 days and the line doesn't really get all that much better (.185/.333/.380). His basing his entire offensive profile on hitting home runs is great and worth all the accolades he has been given in the past, but his dry spell is costing the team dearly.
Now, the entirety of the offense is currently to blame for their predicament. Meant to clinch a playoff spot earlier this week, they have found themselves in the position where missing the playoffs entirely is truly on the table and the cluster of the roster to blame is the offense. They have simply disappeared. When an All-Star starter disappears from the planet as far as production at the plate (Brandon Marsh's wRC+ since 7/1 is 33), that is going to have an effect on the offense. When the catcher joins him in offensive ineptitude (Realmuto's during that same time is a very not nice 69), that's two hitters of nine that are just anchors on a lineup and what they can do.
But having a leadoff hitter that doesn't do what he's supposed to do is also a weight that is hard to ignore. Schwarber since 7/1 has hit .205/.336/.413, a paltry amount compared to what we have seen from him in the past. He's hit 15 home runs in that time frame, which is great since the rest of the lineups has seen little power outside of him, but again, it's not up to his standard.
And there are the strikeouts.
Holy cow, the strikeouts. He's not nearly as strikeout prone as someone like Colson Montgomery, the young White Sox slugger that just whiffed his way to the MLB strikeout record for a season. But Schwarber truly looks lost at times at the plate, that he's just unable to make contact when it is needed most. Two things that have been noticeable is that he's not squaring the ball up
and he's hitting the ball on the ground a lot more often.
It's enough to make one wonder if there is something deeper at play, some kind of injury that he has been hiding that will require something done in the offseason.
There could be a few changes in mind to help with the malaise of the offense as a whole. Batting order changes, substitutions, something that can be used to shake up what looks to be a dormant group of hitters. Something in these final two games that maybe kickstart something drastic. Panicking? Maybe, but panic mode is probably in order right now.
What would really help is a leadoff hitter that was doing his job and right now, Kyle Schwarber is not doing that.

item.content:encoded:
Work with me here.
Imagine that this was Shohei Ohtani’s first MLB season. Thus, this was the first time you regularly saw the same human start 14 games with a 1.79 ERA and produce the fifth-best OPS in the majors.
The attempt is to erase from your mental database familiarity. So you see this fresh and, thus, remove fatigue or boredom or Dodgers hatred or whatever might come when the baseball miraculous is done too often in front of you, rendering it mundane.
If you can attain that state where you see it all anew, let me ask you this: Would you vote for Ohtani as National League MVP?

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Phillies' Luis Arraez gets nightmare injury update as playoff hopes come to a halt amid struggles
item.dc:creator: Hunter Cookston
item.description: Phillies' Luis Arraez gets nightmare injury update as playoff hopes come to a halt amid struggles originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here. The Philadelphia Phillies are trying to make it to their fifth straight playoff appearance, but they are not doing themselves any favors. Over the last two weeks, the team has lost nine of its last 14 games. This is not the type of stretch the Phillies want to be on with the playoffs set to begin
item.content:encoded:
Phillies' Luis Arraez gets nightmare injury update as playoff hopes come to a halt amid struggles originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Philadelphia Phillies are trying to make it to their fifth straight playoff appearance, but they are not doing themselves any favors. Over the last two weeks, the team has lost nine of its last 14 games.
This is not the type of stretch the Phillies want to be on with the playoffs set to begin Tuesday. In fact, the team has allowed the Arizona Diamondbacks back into the picture after losing to the Tampa Bay Rays on Friday.
"The Phillies entered leading Arizona by two games for an NL wild card with three to play. The Phillies would have clinched their fifth straight playoff berth with a win against the Rays and an Arizona loss to San Diego. The Phillies instead lost their third straight and delayed a potential clincher at least until Saturday when they will throw a bullpen game against the Rays," ESPN wrote.
Earlier in the week, things got even bleaker for the Phillies as their trade deadline acquisition, Luis Arraez, left the game with an injury.
"Arraez was injured after he tried to avoid a tag at first base in the Phillies' loss to Milwaukee on Thursday night. Obtained from San Francisco at the trade deadline, Arraez stayed down for a while as trainers tended to him. He eventually hobbled off the field with assistance," ESPN wrote.
On Friday, interim manager Don Mattingly provided an injury update, and it was not one Phillies fans wanted to hear.
"Don Mattingly said update on Luis Arraez was "kind of not a great one." Sounds like they hope he might improve enough to pinch-hit at some point. IL could be possible if he doesn't improve," MLB.com's Todd Zelecki wrote.
With the playoffs starting Tuesday, the timing of this injury could not be worse. Arraez is a tough player who wants to be in the lineup every day, so if he is missing games, the injury is clearly something to monitor.
There is still no guarantee that Philadelphia makes the playoffs, as the Arizona Diamondbacks are only one game behind. If the Phillies can punch their ticket to the postseason, it is not looking like Arraez will be available, at least as a starter.

item.title: [Field Level Media] Cal Raleigh honors Mariners announcer in final series vs. Angels
item.description: Cal Raleigh made his way up to the press box before a recent game at T-Mobile Park, lugging a large box with him. The Seattle Mariners catcher poked his head into the home radio booth, where announcer Rick Rizzs was preparing for one of the final games of his 41-year career with the franchise. Raleigh opened the box to unveil a custom chest protector with a collage of photos of Rizzs, one with Ken Griffey Jr. and another with late broadcast partner Dave Niehaus, with the words “Holy Smokes,” Riz
item.content:encoded:
Cal Raleigh made his way up to the press box before a recent game at T-Mobile Park, lugging a large box with him.
The Seattle Mariners catcher poked his head into the home radio booth, where announcer Rick Rizzs was preparing for one of the final games of his 41-year career with the franchise.
Raleigh opened the box to unveil a custom chest protector with a collage of photos of Rizzs, one with Ken Griffey Jr. and another with late broadcast partner Dave Niehaus, with the words “Holy Smokes,” Rizzs’ catchphrase.
Raleigh told Rizzs he plans to wear the equipment this weekend against the Los Angeles Angels in the final games of the season.
“Oh, my gosh,” Rizzs said, covering his mouth.
It was one of few times Rizzs has been at a loss for words.
“After I’m done wearing it you get to keep it,” Raleigh told Rizzs in a video the Mariners shared on social media.
The clip ended with Rizzs hugging Raleigh and telling him, “You’re the best.”
After falling one game short of their first World Series appearance last season, the Mariners had high hopes in their 50th anniversary season to send Rizzs out with a bang.
It won’t happen, as the Mariners (74-86) were eliminated from playoff contention in the American League West on Thursday.
So Rizzs, 72, will call his final game Sunday afternoon. Just the thought of it makes him tear up.
“I’m a crybaby,” he admitted. “I cry at Hallmark commercials.”
The Angels (62-98) have won the first two games of the series and need one more victory this weekend to avoid the first 100-loss season in franchise history, which dates to 1961.
Reid Detmers pitched six scoreless innings and Christian Moore and Zach Neto homered in Friday’s 7-5 victory.
“That was a good way to end it,” said Detmers, who returned to the rotation this season. “There’s a lot of good to look back on. And to do it against a pretty good team in their home ballpark. It’s a good feeling.”
Detmers finished 7-8 with a 3.36 ERA and 211 strikeouts, the first Angels left-hander to fan more than 200 since Chuck Finley in 1999.
“We talked about his journey,” Angels manager Kurt Suzuki said. “Being such a good starter early in his career, having struggles and then moving to the bullpen last year. And now, becoming one of the best starters in the game. It’s a credit to him and his work ethic.”
Saturday’s pitching matchup will feature Angels right-hander Ryan Johnson (5-9, 4.93 ERA) against Mariners rookie lefty Kade Anderson (2-2, 4.18).
Johnson is coming off an 8-0 loss to visiting Minnesota on Sunday, when he allowed three runs on seven hits over 4 2/3 innings. In his start before that, he beat the visiting Mariners 2-1 by giving up one run in six innings. Johnson is 1-1 with a 2.25 ERA in three career appearances against Seattle, with two starts.
Anderson pitched seven scoreless innings Sunday in a 2-1 victory at Colorado, when he gave up three hits with no walks and seven strikeouts. He lost 6-4 at Anaheim on Sept. 14 when he was battered for five runs on seven hits in 4 1/3 innings.
–Field Level Media
