item.content:encoded:
Las Grandes Ligas de Béisbol (MLB, por sus siglas en inglés) revelaron las 20 camisetas de peloteros más vendidas de la temporada 2026.
En la lista figura un solo pelotero venezolano: Ronald Acuña Jr., de los Bravos de Atlanta, quien ocupa la cuarta posición. En 2025, Acuña Jr. también figuró en este listado, pero en el puesto 11.
La publicación, difundida por la MLB en su cuenta de Instagram, reveló que el japonés Shohei Ohtani, de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles, encabeza la lista de las camisetas más vendidas.
En cuanto a los equipos, los Dodgers de Los Ángeles son los que cuentan con más jugadores en la lista, con cuatro: Ohtani, Freddie Freeman, Mookie Betts y Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
¿Quiénes son los 20 peloteros con las camisetas más vendidas en 2026?
De acuerdo con la lista difundida por la MLB, estas son las 20 camisetas más vendidas de la temporada 2026:
- Shohei Ohtani, Dodgers de Los Ángeles.
- Aaron Judge, Yankees de Nueva York.
- Pete Crow-Armstrong, Cachorros de Chicago.
- Ronald Acuña Jr., Bravos de Atlanta.
- Fernando Tatis Jr., Padres de San Diego.
- Freddie Freeman, Dodgers de Los Ángeles.
- Bryce Harper, Filis de Filadelfia.
- Mookie Betts, Dodgers de Los Ángeles.
- Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers de Los Ángeles.
- Juan Soto, Mets de Nueva York.
- Corey Seager, Texas Rangers.
- Vladimir Guerrero Jr., Toronto Blue Jays.
- Adley Rutschman, Medias Rojas de Boston.
- Kyle Schwarber, Filis de Filadelfia.
- Paul Skenes, Piratas de Pittsburgh.
- Cal Raleigh, Marineros de Seattle.
- Elly De La Cruz, Rojos de Cincinnati.
- Jackson Merrill, Padres de San Diego.
- Nolan Arenado, Arizona Diamondbacks.
- Munetaka Murakami, Chicago White Sox.
Shohei Ohtani encabeza por cuarto año consecutivo
El japonés Shohei Ohtani, de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles, volvió a ser el jugador con la camiseta más vendida de las Grandes Ligas, una posición que ocupa por cuarto año consecutivo.
Ohtani se convirtió así en el primer jugador en encadenar cuatro temporadas como líder en ventas de camisetas desde que MLB comenzó a registrar este dato en 2010, reseñó la agencia de noticias EFE este viernes 25 de septiembre.
Desde 2023, los aficionados han comprado la camiseta Nike de Ohtani más que cualquier otra en Estados Unidos, Japón y el resto del mundo, consolidando al jugador japonés como la figura con mayor demanda comercial entre los peloteros de las Grandes Ligas.
El listado, elaborado a partir de las ventas de camisetas Nike realizadas a través de Fanatics, incluido MLBShop.com, desde el Día Inaugural de la temporada 2026, sitúa al capitán de los Yankees de Nueva York, Aaron Judge, en el segundo puesto y al jardinero de los Cachorros de Chicago Pete Crow-Armstrong en el tercero.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Alonso hits two more HRs in 10-2 Orioles win over Yanks
item.dc:creator: Paul Folkemer
item.description: This just in, ladies and gentlemen: Pete Alonso is really good at baseball. The Most Valuable Oriole continued to be the best thing to happen to this franchise in a long time, adding two more homers to his league-leading total in a 10-2 blowout win to open a doubleheader against the Yankees. Whatever other things have gone wrong for the Orioles this year — and oh boy, are there many — Pete Alonso has been worth the price of admission all by himself. Tonight, even in a game that had no meaning fo
item.content:encoded:
This just in, ladies and gentlemen: Pete Alonso is really good at baseball.
The Most Valuable Oriole continued to be the best thing to happen to this franchise in a long time, adding two more homers to his league-leading total in a 10-2 blowout win to open a doubleheader against the Yankees.
Whatever other things have gone wrong for the Orioles this year — and oh boy, are there many — Pete Alonso has been worth the price of admission all by himself. Tonight, even in a game that had no meaning for either team, he proved why.
Alonso stepped to the plate with a man aboard in the third against Yankees starter Brendan Beck, who'd begun the game with two scoreless innings. Pete put an end to that real quick. He drove a 407-foot dinger into the left-field seats, his 42nd of the year. At that point, Alonso's last seven hits had all been dingers. Did I mention this guy is good at baseball?
The Orioles turned the game into a laugher in the fourth even without Pete being prominently involved (though he did get a single). The O's loaded the bases with nobody out for the soft underbelly of the lineup, including Christian Franklin and Carlos Narváez, who entered the game with a combined zero RBIs in 132 plate appearances with the Orioles. That's Caleb Joseph territory right there. Franklin managed to get off the schneid with a sharp single to right, collecting his first major league RBI, but Narváez remained in his drought by hitting into a force at the plate.
It shouldn't be that hard to get one measly RBI, Carlos. Just watch as Dylan Beavers gets four of them in one at-bat! The O's right fielder jumped on a hanging curveball from Beck and clobbered it into the right-field seats for his first career grand slam. Beavers! With one mighty swing, the Orioles had an insurmountable 7-0 lead.
The Birds' victory was all but assured, but that doesn't mean they couldn't have some more fun along the way. In the top of the sixth, Jeremiah Jackson lofted a fly ball to deep center field. Spencer Jones loped back at an ambling pace, as if he had the ball tracked all the way, but when he reached up to make the catch, it glanced off his glove and deflected to the wall. The ball trickled along the warning track for so long that Jackson just kept circling the bases, and by the time the Yankees got the ball into the infield, Jackson had slid in safely with an inside-the-park home run.
Look at the wheels on Jeremiah! If you'd told me that the Orioles would have two inside-the-parkers this season and they'd be hit by Coby Mayo and Jeremiah Jackson, I'm not sure I would've believed you. This has been a strange season, occasionally in good ways.
You know what's not strange? Pete Alonso being awesome. It's just what he does, and always has. Alonso led off the seventh against reliever Yerry de los Santos and absolutely demolished a baseball. Holy smokes, was it tattooed, a mammoth blast the landed high into the left-field bleacher seats.
Pete, that baseball had a family! The blast was his second of the game and AL-leading 43rd of the year, and extended his AL-leading RBI count to 112. In all likelihood, Pete is going to take two of the three Triple Crown categories. He won't win AL MVP, and I'm not saying he should, but…is there any player in the American League who's really that much better than him? I'd put him in my top five for sure.
This game was all Orioles, but if there was one disappointing aspect, it's that Trevor Rogers didn't get the chance to earn the win in what may well have been his final start as an Oriole. Rogers pitched brilliantly tonight as always, but the Orioles, in an apparently pre-planned move, removed him from the game after four innings and 55 pitches.
I mean…why? Rogers was showing no signs of fatigue. He mowed down the Yankees in the first four frames, throwing 41 strikes and just 14 balls. He allowed only one run, on an Amed Rosario RBI single in the fourth, and the O's had a comfortable six-run lead when he left. Was his arm really going to fall off if he threw more than 55 pitches in his final start of the season?
I will grant that he'd already thrown a career-high 169.2 innings this season, and perhaps the Orioles saw no reason to push him in a meaningless game, but I would've let him at least pitch one more inning to get a W next to his name. Mostly I just don't want to accept that this might've been the last time we see Rogers in an Orioles uniform.
The Orioles hit double digits in runs on Gunnar Henderson's RBI single in the eighth that deflected off the second baseman, and the bullpen took it from there. Albert Suárez, now in his sixth stint with the Orioles this year, did his usual quality work in long relief. He tossed four scoreless innings and struck out five, even despite a nosebleed that afflicted him in the eighth. Suárez has been an unsung hero of the O's bullpen, constantly eating up innings without complaint even when he knows he'll probably get DFA'd the next day, then inevitably returning to the roster to do it all over again.
Alex Hoppe's ninth inning was a mess — 22 pitches, two walks, and a run — but a nine-run lead gives you plenty of wiggle room, and he eventually finished it with a called strikeout of Ben Rice. Orioles win, 10-2. Not a bad way to start the weekend.

item.title: [Bozeman Daily Chronicle] Pete Alonso homers twice to take over AL lead as Orioles rout Yanks 10-2 in doubleheader opener
item.dc:creator: LARRY FLEISHER
item.description: NEW YORK (AP) — Pete Alonso homered twice to take over the American League lead with 43, including a 471-foot drive deep into the left field bleachers, and the Baltimore Orioles routed the New York Yankees 10-2 in a doubleheader opener on Friday. Dylan Beavers had his first career grand slam in a five-run fourth and Jeremiah Jackson added an inside-the-park homer in the sixth. Alonso hit rookie Brendan Beck's first-pitch slider in the third inning, becoming the first Oriole since Mark Trumbo in
item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK (AP) — Pete Alonso homered twice to take over the American League lead with 43, including a 471-foot drive deep into the left field bleachers, and the Baltimore Orioles routed the New York Yankees 10-2 in a doubleheader opener on Friday.
Dylan Beavers had his first career grand slam in a five-run fourth and Jeremiah Jackson added an inside-the-park homer in the sixth.
Alonso hit rookie Brendan Beck's first-pitch slider in the third inning, becoming the first Oriole since Mark Trumbo in 2016 with seven straight hits that were homers.
Alonso singled in the fourth and three innings later hit a changeup at least halfway up the left field bleachers for a 9-1 lead, the fourth-longest homer in the major leagues this year.
Alonso moved out of a four-way tie for the AL home run lead. His 113 RBIs tied St. Louis' Alec Burleson for the big league high and the most by an Oriole since Chris Davis' 117 in 2015.
It was Alonso's 29th multi-homer game and third this year.
Beavers hit Baltimore's sixth grand slam this season, a drive into the right-field seats for a 7-0 lead.
Jackson added Baltimore’s second inside-the-park homer this year when he hit a fly ball that went over center fielder Spencer Jones’ glove at the warning track in front of New York’s bullpen. The ball caromed in front of the fence and Jackson crossed the plate ahead of right fielder Amed Rosario's throw.
Baltimore starter Trevor Rogers allowed one run and five hits in four innings. Albert Suárez (3-0) pitched four innings for the win.
Rosario had an RBI single for the Yankees, who honored Hall of Fame pitcher CC Sabathia by retiring his No. 52 and giving him a plaque in Monument Park in a pregame ceremony.
Anthony Volpe debuted at third base for the Yankees and had a double by Christian Encarnacion-Strand hit the bag go over his head in the ninth.
Beck (0-2) allowed seven runs and six hits in five innings.
Up Next
RHP Brandon Young (9-5, 3.62 ERA) starts for Baltimore in Game 2.

item.content:encoded:
【カブス3-4レッドソックス】ボストン／フェンウェイパーク、9月25日（日本時間26日）
レッドソックスは本拠地フェンウェイパークで行われたカブスとのダブルヘッダー第1試合に4-3で逆転勝利。ア・リーグの第5シードに入ることが確定し、ワイルドカードシリーズでは同地区の宿敵ヤンキースと対戦することになった。カブスの鈴木誠也は「2番・右翼」でスタメン出場し、初回の第1打席で四球を選んで先制のホームイン。しかし、その後はピッチャーゴロ、空振り三振、ショートゴロ、空振り三振と快音響かず、4打数無安打1四球で今季の打撃成績は打率.268、OPS.837となった。 レッドソックス先発のアレック・ガンボアは初回、1死から鈴木に四球を与え、2死後にタイロン・テイラーにレフトへのタイムリー二塁打を浴びて先制点を献上。二回は1死一、二塁の場面でミゲル・アマヤに2点タイムリー二塁打を浴び、2回4安打3失点で降板した。 しかし、ガンボア降板後、レッドソックス投手陣がカブス打線を封じた。2番手のジェイク・ベネットは3回2/3を3安打無失点に抑え、六回2死一塁の場面で登板した3番手のグレッグ・ワイサートも1回1/3を無失点。八回と九回は4番手のレイモンド・バーゴスが打者6人をパーフェクトに抑える好投を見せた。 レッドソックス打線は二回までカブス先発のクレイ・ホームズに無得点に抑えられていたが、三回にエラー絡みで1点を返すと、五回には1死二、三塁のチャンスを作り、ホームズを降板に追い込んだ。このあと、2番手のケイレブ・シールバーからアドリー・ラッチマンが2点タイムリーを放ち、3-3の同点に。リリーフ陣の奮闘に打線が応え、試合を振り出しに戻した。 2死満塁のピンチを切り抜けた直後の七回には勝ち越しのチャンスが到来。ロマン・アンソニーがライトへの三塁打を放ち、1死三塁となった。ここでコナー・ウォンがタイムリー二塁打を放ち、4-3と勝ち越しに成功。この1点を守り切って今季86勝目を挙げ、ア・リーグの第5シードを確定させた。 なお、カブスとレッドソックスは3連戦の最終戦を今日にスライドしてダブルヘッダーを開催し、明日がシーズン最終戦となる予定だったが、ボストンの天気が悪いため、明日の試合をレギュラーシーズン最終日となる27日（同28日）にスライドして開催地をレイズの本拠地であるトロピカーナフィールドに変更。確実に試合を消化できる日程が組まれることになった。

item.title: [MLB.com] Doc Emrick talks Pirates fandom, Paul Skenes and what makes Pittsburgh great
item.dc:creator: Jason Mackey

item.content:encoded:
DETROIT — Doc Emrick is most famous for his work as a Hall of Fame hockey broadcaster, but he’s always been a baseball fan at heart, especially when it comes to his beloved Pirates.
In fact, Emrick can pinpoint the exact day his Pirates fandom was solidified, which would surprise absolutely no one who’s ever listened to him call a hockey game.
The day was Aug. 9, 1959. The Pirates beat the Cubs at Wrigley Field in 10 innings, and Elroy Face earned the win. Emrick, who grew up in Fontaine, Ind. was there to witness it.
Initially intrigued by hearing Bob Prince call Pirates games on the radio, Emrick passed the point of no return when he saw the team win in person.
“I was hooked,” Emrick said Friday before the Pirates played the Tigers at Comerica Park. Emrick lives in St. Clair, Mich., about an hour north.
“I got to see three World Series championships, and the last guy who was on the mound when they won a World Series was Kent Tekulve. I’m proud to know him and have been around him down at fantasy camp.”
Emrick said it’s been about five years since he attended a Major League game but was thrilled to be around it live again. He watches every Pirates game back home and will join the SportsNet Pittsburgh broadcast alongside Greg Brown and John Wehner.
Predictably, Emrick was all smiles pregame while meeting with manager Don Kelly and saying hello to a few players, including noted hockey fan Spencer Horwitz.
“This is a special treat for me,” Emrick said. “The fact that I can see the Rock and Brownie and actually sit in with them [Friday], that’s special to me.”
Emrick participated in Pirates fantasy camp back in 2012 and encouraged anyone on the fence about doing it to take the plunge.
Starting with their Opening Day homers, Brandon Lowe and Ryan O’Hearn have been two of Emrick’s favorite players to watch this season, for how they seem to come through at important times.
On the pitching side, Emrick obviously enjoys watching Paul Skenes. But Mason Montgomery’s ascent this season has also been a pleasant surprise, leading Emrick to drop an obscure Ryne Duren (Google it) reference that’s very uniquely him.
“I like to see pitches thrown 100 or 101 miles per hour, because I could only imagine that when I was watching back in an earlier era,” Emrick said. “There was a pitcher for the New York Yankees that had Coke bottle glasses named Ryne Durne, and Yogi Berra felt that he probably pitched 90 miles an hour.
“Nobody wanted to bat against him, especially on a cold day. That was 90 [mph] and considered to be off the charts back then. The standard now is so much different.
“But to have confidence in a closer that comes out of the bullpen and you realize he’s probably got this thing, that’s really, really good. … I wish he could pitch every game. But you can’t expect that with that kind of velocity, for somebody to pitch every game.”
As for Skenes, Emrick enjoys how much attention he generates around MLB, basically as a point of pride for Pittsburgh. Emrick also isn’t upset that Skenes’ 2026 performance failed to meet previous standards set. In Emrick’s mind, that would’ve been darn near impossible.
“The first couple of years, the standard was so high,” Emrick said. “How is a human being going to rise above that for a third year in a row? Some of these recent outings that he’s had have been spectacular. It’s something to look forward to for the future.”
Emrick retired in October 2020 after 47 years of broadcasting hockey, which included the Stanley Cup Final 22 times. Given the Penguins’ success, Emrick was a regular presence in Pittsburgh and typically tried to work Pirates references into his hockey broadcasts.
There are also Pittsburgh ties with Emrick having taught speech and broadcasting at Geneva College, which basically makes him an honorary Yinzer.
Emrick said he appreciates Pittsburgh being so welcoming, along with the athletic success the city has enjoyed over the years.
“I’m just glad to be around you folks and travel into Pittsburgh now and then,” Emrick said. “I was thinking the other day, the city of Pittsburgh has had so many wonderful athletes in football, baseball and hockey. It’s easy to get spoiled. Not every city has that many that have been that prominent. And they tend to stay around there, don’t they?
“There’s not an edge to people in Pittsburgh. There’s just a general feeling that’s good.”

item.content:encoded:
Luis Arráez encendió las alarmas de Philadelphia durante la derrota 5-1 ante Milwaukee Brewers. El venezolano conectó un rodado en la sexta entrada y se torció el tobillo izquierdo cuando intentó evitar el toque del primera base Jake Bauers.
El infielder permaneció varios minutos en el terreno y necesitó ayuda del personal médico para caminar hasta el dugout. Los Phillies confirmaron posteriormente un esguince, aunque las radiografías descartaron una fractura.
- LEER MÁS: Los venezolanos que están marcando el cierre de MLB 2026
- LEER MÁS: Fernando Valenzuela: cómo la “Fernandomanía” transformó a la MLB
Todavía no existe una incapacidad oficial ni una fecha establecida para su regreso. El mánager interino Don Mattingly aseguró que espera poder utilizarlo nuevamente, pero su disponibilidad dependerá de la inflamación, el dolor y las evaluaciones realizadas durante el fin de semana.
El momento de la lesión aumenta la preocupación. Philadelphia posee marca de 87-72, ocupa el último comodín de la Liga Nacional y mantiene solamente dos juegos de ventaja sobre Arizona Diamondbacks cuando restan tres compromisos contra Tampa Bay Rays.
Suscríbete al Newsletter de Unanimo y recibe gratis las últimas noticias. Dale click aquí
Arráez se había convertido en una pieza importante desde su llegada procedente de San Francisco. En 45 partidos con los Phillies batea para .283, con dos jonrones, 21 carreras impulsadas y OPS de .690, generalmente como cuarto bate detrás de Bryce Harper.
Su ausencia también obligaría a modificar varias posiciones. Edmundo Sosa podría encargarse de la segunda base, mientras otra alternativa sería devolver a Harper a la inicial y reorganizar el outfield. Bryson Stott y Alec Bohm también podrían cambiar nuevamente de posición.
Luis Arráez went down in pain after running to 1st base on this play. He has left the game. pic.twitter.com/nbKPlGanAg
— FOX Sports: MLB (@MLBONFOX) September 24, 2026
Philadelphia ya enfrenta otras dudas antes de octubre. Jesús Luzardo se encuentra en la lista de lesionados por una inflamación en el hombro izquierdo y el equipo acumula dos derrotas consecutivas, por lo que perder otro titular reduciría todavía más su margen de error.
Arráez no está descartado para los playoffs y las radiografías negativas representan la mejor noticia posible. Sin embargo, la Serie del Comodín comienza el martes y cualquier recuperación superior a cuatro días podría impedir que el venezolano participe desde el inicio.

item.title: [heavy.com] Milwaukee Brewers Announce Christian Yelich Decision Before Cardinals Series
item.dc:creator: Cole Sullivan
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers are coming off a series victory over the Philadelphia Phillies that they wrapped up Thursday with a 5-1 victory. Now, they’re back home Friday night. And continue to inch closer to clinching the No. 1 overall seed in the National League as they begin their final series of the regular season against the St. Louis Cardinals. item.content:encoded:
The Milwaukee Brewers are coming off a series victory over the Philadelphia Phillies that they wrapped up Thursday with a 5-1 victory.
Now, they’re back home Friday night. And continue to inch closer to clinching the No. 1 overall seed in the National League as they begin their final series of the regular season against the St. Louis Cardinals.
On Friday night, Milwaukee will have right-handed pitcher Robert Gasser on the mound against Cardinals righty Michael McGreevy.
Ahead of the matchup, Brewers manager Pat Murphy made a notable change to the starting lineup involving veteran slugger Christian Yelich.
Brewers Announce Yelich Decision
After sitting Thursday in the series finale against Philly and making no pinch-hit appearances, Yelich is back in the order for Friday’s matchup.
Yelich will bat fifth in the order and serve as the team’s designated hitter, a usual spot for him this year as he’s entered more of a platoon role in his 14th MLB season.
Here’s the full Brewers lineup:
Via Underdog MLB: “Brewers 9/25 G. Mitchell CF B. Turang 2B W. Contreras C J. Bauers 1B C. Yelich DH J. Ortiz SS L. Lara RF S. Frelick LF D. Hamilton 3B R. Gasser SP.”
Brewers 9/25
G. Mitchell CF
B. Turang 2B
W. Contreras C
J. Bauers 1B
C. Yelich DH
J. Ortiz SS
L. Lara RF
S. Frelick LF
D. Hamilton 3B
R. Gasser SP
— Underdog MLB (@UnderdogMLB) September 25, 2026
Looking at Yelich’s 2026 Season
While Yelich no longer plays every day or spends much time in the field. He remains an extremely productive player for a 100-win Brewers team that owns the best record in baseball.
Yelich has appeared in 115 games this season and logged 433 at-bats, recording 68 runs, 102 hits, 12 home runs, and 58 RBIs while hitting .236 and slugging .381 with a .695 OPS.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Red Sox Star Sonny Gray Gets Big Free Agency Prediction Just Before Playoffs
item.dc:creator: Matt Levine
item.description: The Boston Red Sox are getting ready for the final few games of the regular season, with the postseason starting up next week. Boston has clinched a playoff spot, and they will be a wild-card team this season. The Red Sox battled back from a very slow start to the season, putting together a massive rally in the middle of the year. item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox are getting ready for the final few games of the regular season, with the postseason starting up next week.
Boston has clinched a playoff spot, and they will be a wild-card team this season. The Red Sox battled back from a very slow start to the season, putting together a massive rally in the middle of the year.
The goal is to win a World Series title, and they seem to have a decent shot at getting it done. But while the players are focused on the play on the field, the front office also has its sights set on the upcoming offseason.
Even with the impending lockout likely coming to baseball, teams all over the league could try to maneuver rosters before it happens. For the Red Sox, they do have a key free agent hitting the market in ace Sonny Gray.
The veteran right-hander has been excellent for the Red Sox this year, firing a 2.79 ERA over 29 innings. Gray has helped establish the Red Sox rotation as one of the best in baseball, and he has been a major reason why the team has made the playoffs.
The right-hander has a mutual option for next season, but there has also been some retirement talk. However, given how strong of a year he has seen, the right-hander may postpone that idea, looking to land one last big contract.
Boston would surely want him back, but that all remains to be seen. But his free agency will be something to watch for the Red Sox and other potentially interested teams out there.
Sonny Gray Gets Major Free Agency Prediction
analyst Zach Buckley of Bleacher Report looked ahead to some of the bigger stars hitting the free-agent market this winter, predicting some of the outcomes. In this, Buckley has predicted that Gray will indeed return to the Red Sox following a strong season.
"It sounds like everything is on the table for the 36-year-old. Per Mass Live's Chris Cotillo, Gray could fetch a similar deal to the three-year, $75 million deal Nathan Eovaldi inked with the Texas Rangers two years back. But Cotillo also noted that Gray relayed in a recent interview with The Boston Globe he would retire "in a heartbeat" if his family indicated any desire for him to do so.
"Only Gray knows what he's thinking, and since he doesn't need to make a decision right now, it's very possible even if he isn't sure. If he wants to keep playing, though, he has clearly set himself up to strike it rich in free agency," Buckley wrote.
Should Red Sox Resign Sonny Gray?
Given how dominant Gray has been, the Red Sox should try to sign him to a new deal. Even if this would be just for another year or two, having Gray around would help Boston heading into next season.
Gray has seen a lot of success with the Red Sox, and the team is a contender, so the two sides may come together. But for now, the focus will be on trying to win the World Series, with free agency in the back of everyone's mind.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Red Sox Star Sonny Gray Gets Big Free Agency Prediction Just Before Playoffs appeared first on HEAVY.

item.title: [CBS Sports] Vladimir Guerrero Jr. apologizes for controversial comments about his $500 million contract
item.dc:creator: Dayn Perry
item.description: Toronto Blue Jays first baseman Vladimir Guerrero Jr. has apologized days after saying his $500 million contract extension rather than a reflection of his value moving forward. Guerrero Jr. on Friday, ahead of his team's season-ending home series against the Cincinnati Reds, issued the following statement, via MLB.com: "I want to tell everyone that I'm going to continue to keep working hard to make my contract a great one. … "I feel that the comments I made the other day is not what I really wan
item.content:encoded:
Toronto Blue Jays first baseman Vladimir Guerrero Jr. has apologized days after saying his $500 million contract extension rather than a reflection of his value moving forward.
Guerrero Jr. on Friday, ahead of his team's season-ending home series against the Cincinnati Reds, issued the following statement, via MLB.com:
"I want to tell everyone that I'm going to continue to keep working hard to make my contract a great one.
…
"I feel that the comments I made the other day is not what I really wanted to say. Everyone deserves an apology from me."
Guerrero Jr. said he regretted his comments and felt like he owed an apology to the fans and his teammates.
Vladdy starts his availability with a statement, through interpreter:
“The reason I'm here because I regret my comments the other day … I feel from my heart, my fans, my teammates, they needed an apology from me, and that's why I'm here for.”#BlueJays
Additionally, Guerrero Jr. said he decided to apologize after speaking with his father, Hall of Famer Vladimir Guerrero Sr.
The controversy stemmed from what the 27-year-old first baseman recently told Telemicro News, as translated by Héctor Gómez:
"The contract I got was based on what I did, not necessarily for what I'm going to do. I understand why the fans believe it's the other way around. Sometimes I think that way too, like 'oh they give me this money and I'm not doing enough', but you know I try my best and I'm working hard.
"The fans I know how they are, when you are doing great they are 100% behind you but when you are not at your best not everybody is behind you, almost nobody supports you. Those are my real fans, the ones that are supporting me all the time."
Guerrero Jr.'s original comments were ill-timed, as the reigning American League champion Blue Jays have been eliminated from playoff contention, and Guerrero Jr. himself has endured a highly disappointing season:
The above comes to an OPS+ of just 92, or a park-adjusted OPS that's 8% worse than the league average. Coming into 2026, he had a career OPS+ of 136. This season, Guerrero Jr. has hit just nine home runs and only one at home. He's slugged just .360, and his WAR has dropped from 4.6 a season ago to 1.3 in 2026. This decline in production has come in the first year of that $500 million extension, which will run through the 2039 season.
The only way Guerrero Jr. can truly put those struggles behind him is with a strong 2027, and his words on Friday suggest he's dedicated to making that happen.
The last-place Blue Jays enter the final weekend of the regular season with a record of 77-82, which means they've ensured a losing season for the second time in the last three years.

item.content:encoded:
Anyone who watched the 2026 Mariners could easily point to areas where the team failed, but Cal Raleigh, meeting with the media on Thursday, was unflinching in his assessment of what went wrong this season.
"I think there's a lot of areas you can point to. I think ultimately, I think it was a lack of focus, a lack of execution, a lack energy at times. Defense was not good all year, controlling the running game was not good all year. Playing bad on the road all year, hitting with runners in scoring position was definitely not good. I'd say those were some key points that I kind of look at."
Other than that, Mrs. Lincoln, how was the baseball season?
One thing Raleigh is steadfast in is not blaming injuries for the team's poor performance, shutting down that line of questioning immediately.
"Every team deals with that. Guys are going to go through aches, pains, injuries. So it's silly to use that as an excuse. 29 other different ball clubs are dealing with the same thing that we are, and you can't use that as an excuse. And we're definitely not going to. It came down to play on the field, and it was not executed."
But fans were there. They saw the lack of execution. They are less interested in the why, and more in how it's going to get better. Unfortunately, in order to get to the second part – knowing how to fix it – it is necessary to first understand what went wrong, and why. But that's a more complex discussion that first involves figuring out where to assign blame, and how much of it goes where. It's not a one-size-fits-all answer, notes Raleigh.
"I don't think it was one thing," said Raleigh. "I think we could point to a lot of things that that went wrong, but I
don't think it was one thing. I don't think it was one person. I don't think it was one department that
failed this year. I think it was a collective failure, unfortunately."
"Ultimately, yeah, the players are the ones playing every single day, 162. I think if you ask everybody, typically it's going to fall on the players. But like I said, I think there's not one person or one group that it falls under. I think it's a collective effort. I think it's all the way from the top, to all the way to the bottom, and that's a tough pill to swallow."
While the players are, as Cal points out, ultimately the ones on the field, it's clear from his comments they aren't the only ones in charge of turning around this miserable season next year. Deficiencies that showed up early in the season as far as the roster went were only exacerbated by injuries and ineffectiveness, especially in the pitching staff, which suffered the biggest drop in WAR from the first to the second half as starters stuttered and bullpens imploded.
"We need more depth in the bullpen," said Raleigh. "I mean, we honestly do. We need to get some more whiff. We need to get some more guys that can punch some tickets here and there."
But beyond adding pieces, Raleigh says the core of pitchers who make up the rotation need to return to form or maybe change tactics. He seems to feel other teams have figured out the Mariners pitchers plan of attack, and the focus now needs to be on counter-attacking aggressive hitters rather than allowing them to ambush first pitches.
"The starters, they got to continue to get better. They've been one of the best rotations in all of baseball for the last few years, and and like I said, you can talk to all of them, and they're probably disappointed with how they did. When I when I'm watching the game back there, I'm seeing a lot of very aggressive teams, very aggressive teams, even teams that aren't [usually] aggressive. And when I look at that, it's going to come down to execution. It's not not necessarily all the time about winning your 0-0s, your 1-1s. It's about executing a pitch and how can we get this guy out."
"I saw a lot of very aggressive hitters and guys that were were ready to go from you know pitch one because that's kind of in our DNA. We've got to continue finding ways to combat that. I think we've done a great job of that, and creating pitchers [who attack the zone] and having guys that are really good at doing that. But at the end of the day, it's about wins, it's about execution. It's not about chasing a stat or, or doing anything like that. So it's just about getting better, and I don't know if maybe we were complacent in that fact. Maybe we were. Maybe we
weren't. Maybe it was just unlucky. Maybe it wasn't. But it's finding a way to, 'how can we get better? How can we combat those things that other teams are doing to us?'"
Beyond just the core of pitchers, Raleigh said the core of players as a whole has to do better. Yes, injuries decimated the bullpen and that depth has to be rebuilt, and every team always wants to get better, but the core members of the team as a whole have to play better.
"I said it right at the right at the deadline. The core is here. The core is here, and this core got us where we were last year. But ultimately, that core has to get better as well. It's not always bringing in extra pieces that are gonna help. Do we need to bring in more people in certain areas of the game? Yes, 100%. We need to get better, and that's always gonna help. But at the same time, when you look at the core guys, I think you can look at most of the guys, and they will tell you that they did not have the season they wanted, and team-wise, we didn't have the season we wanted. Ultimately we failed. That's the easiest way to put it."
What caused this team-wide failure across the core? Raleigh noted there might have been times where the team stagnated when they needed to take a step forward, failing to make adjustments and finding the kind of edges that great teams do.
"Every facet can be better," he said bluntly. "I think we—myself included—we could have done a better job of of preparing and continuing to get better throughout the year. I think sometimes in the game you can get a little stagnant at times, like, 'I got to rest my body' or 'I got to make sure I'm ready for the game at 7 o'clock,' which is ultimately, what you want to do."
"But you also have to continue to get better and continue to get stronger as the year goes on, and we just never did. We never made those adjustments we had to make. We didn't get better in the areas that we were deficient in, and we just kind of stayed stagnant the whole time. We were relying more on catching a lucky streak rather than to keep preparing better, to keep getting better, keep finding those those edges to to find ways to to win ball games, whether it was defensively holding runners, hitting with runners in scoring position, finding a way to get through six innings instead of five from the starters…there's lots of different things. Taking an extra bag here and here, things like that. And and it just never got there. Never got there."
Raleigh is an admirer of Seahawks coach Mike McDonald, and has clearly absorbed McDonald's message of "chasing edges", or finding small ways to edge out an opponent. Again, his comments reflect some frustration with the status quo and a lack of innovation, as well as a lack of execution.
"You can't rely on the bullpen or you can't rely on the big home run every single time. We have to be able to win in different fashions, win in different ways. Find a way to sneak out those one-run ball games. I don't think we were very good in one-run ball games this year. I think it was right around .500. Like I said before, the road record was poor, we got swept too many times. It's finding a way to edge out those games. It's—I heard this phrase the other day, 'chasing edges.' How can we win one game here and there, one extra game a month? That's six, seven extra wins. Now we're tied for first, or we're we're in first place. It's cliché to say it's the little things, but those are what win you ball games, and those are things we did not do this year."
Raleigh's biggest takeaway is not letting this become a habit, pointing out that it if happens once, it's an unfortunate event; if it happens twice, it's a habit.
"We've got to figure out why why that happened, and and there's going to be lots of talks, lots of discussions throughout the off season to make sure that doesn't come back next season. Every single aspect needs to be geared towards how can we win this ball game today. Not taking days off, not letting one thing slip through the cracks. Because once that happens, it's a domino effect, right? Like you let one thing slide, then you let another thing slide. The next thing you know, you don't know what's going on. There's no standards. There's no accountability. There's no dynamic of who we are and what we do, and and I think that's what's going to be looked at this off-season."
The 2026 season was certainly a slide for the Mariners. Now Cal Raleigh, his teammates, and the rest of the organization – top to bottom – have to reset those dominoes and figure out how to not let them fall again. Raleigh seems to have a vision: chasing edges every day, stopping slides before they start, being less predictable as a pitching staff, cleaning up sloppy play on the field. Now, he has an off-season to implement it.

item.title: [MLB.com] Alonso says 'unacceptable' for O's to miss postseason: 'That's not the standard here'
item.dc:creator: Jake Rill
item.description: NEW YORK -- When the Orioles arrived at Yankee Stadium early Friday afternoon, it was the first time the team had convened since being eliminated from postseason contention. Baltimore’s playoff aspirations ended during Thursday’s off-day, when a White Sox win at Kansas City dropped the O’s postseason odds to 0%. Manager Craig Albernaz addressed his players inside the visitors’ clubhouse prior to the start of the final three-game series vs. the Yankees -- one that doesn’t have any stakes. “Obviou
item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK -- When the Orioles arrived at Yankee Stadium early Friday afternoon, it was the first time the team had convened since being eliminated from postseason contention. Baltimore’s playoff aspirations ended during Thursday’s off-day, when a White Sox win at Kansas City dropped the O’s postseason odds to 0%.
Manager Craig Albernaz addressed his players inside the visitors’ clubhouse prior to the start of the final three-game series vs. the Yankees -- one that doesn’t have any stakes.
“Obviously, we’re eliminated, and it’s not a place where we wanted to be. But we’re here, and it sucks. It’s something for myself, and also the rest of the team, we don’t want to have this feeling again,” Albernaz said. “I just challenged the guys that, first and foremost, I can be better for them. I’ve got to make adjustments and help us in the win column as much as I can, but also challenge them that each player do some self-reflection and figure out the little margins where they can get better as well and attack them this offseason.
“Us as a group, if we all attack those margins and you look up, next year, hopefully, we’ll be in a better spot.”
That was the general consensus among the Orioles. Everybody is disappointed about entering Friday with a 78-81 record and knowing their season won’t extend beyond Sunday. But there’s a belief that it won’t be like this again in 2027.
Pete Alonso has been Baltimore’s leader all season. After signing a five-year, $155 million deal last December, the 31-year-old slugger has not only been the team’s best player on the field, but he has become a strong presence with a loud voice inside the clubhouse.
And Alonso didn’t mince words when asked about Thursday’s elimination.
“That’s not the expectation. As a club, we failed to perform and do what we were supposed to do. We had great moments, great individual performances, but as a whole, that’s not the standard here. And that’s unacceptable for us,” Alonso said. “The standard for us is to not only make the postseason, but make a run and have a legitimate shot to hold up a trophy at the end of the year, and we didn’t even give ourselves an opportunity to enter the dance in October.”
After making consecutive postseason appearances in 2023 and ‘24, the O’s have missed the playoffs in both ‘25 and ‘26. There had been optimism for this season to be a bounce-back year, and instead, Baltimore never quite played up to expectations.
The Orioles never had a record above .500 after falling to 9-9 on April 15. They spent nearly the entire season with a losing record, then returned to .500 when they improved to 69-69 on Aug. 31. However, Baltimore opened September with six straight losses.
With the race for the third American League Wild Card wide open for the final few weeks of the season, the O’s stayed alive for longer than they likely would have in most years.
“I think if you ask anyone in this clubhouse, it didn’t really feel like we played our best baseball over a collective period of time -- pretty much the whole year,” outfielder Colton Cowser said. “It kind of sucks, because it did feel like it was somewhat of a down year in the AL. ... So I think when you reflect upon it like that, it feels like we probably didn’t take advantage of a year where we probably could have made the playoffs.”
So, where do the Orioles go from here?
They still have to wrap up the season in New York. Then, the players will head their separate ways and take some time to unwind and debrief early in the offseason.
There will be transactions made, whether that’s in free agency or via trades. The O’s will surely look at least slightly different when they begin play in the 2027 season.
But Baltimore still has confidence in the potential for a successful long-term future.
“I think this team can be in a really good spot next year,” Cowser said.
“Next year, whatever needs to happen, we need to do a better job. We need to do a better job as players, because that’s what it boils down to,” Alonso added. “The expectation is to be a great team.”

item.content:encoded:
The Diamondbacks placed Burnes on the 15-day injured list Friday with right shoulder inflammation.
Burnes showed diminished velocity in his last start versus the Yankees, serving up three home runs during a four-batter span at one point. The veteran righty had a setback in his recovery from Tommy John surgery earlier this season when he suffered a teres major strain, though there's no indication at this point that the new injury is related. It's unclear whether Burnes has a chance to pitch at some point in the postseason, should the Diamondbacks qualify. Burnes had been slated to start Saturday's game in San Diego, but that assignment could now go to Ryne Nelson.

item.dc:creator: Gray Louisiana

item.content:encoded:
PITTSBURGH (WAFB) - Former LSU star Paul Skenes ended his season by making Pittsburgh Pirates history.
Then Livvy Dunne made sure one online critic knew about it.
Skenes recorded his 200th strikeout of the season Thursday in his final start of 2026, becoming the first Pirates starter with consecutive 200-strikeout seasons since Bob Veale accomplished the feat from 1964 through 1966.
The right-hander entered the seventh inning against the St. Louis Cardinals sitting at 199 strikeouts.
Skenes struck out Leo Bernal for No. 200 before being removed from the game.
He finished the afternoon allowing one run on three hits and two walks while striking out eight over 6 1/3 innings. Pittsburgh went on to win 2-1.
Skenes finished the season with a 3.82 ERA and exactly 200 strikeouts across 32 starts.
“It was a grind. It was definitely a grind,” Skenes said after the game.
The former LSU national champion acknowledged that his 2026 season did not match the standard of his previous two years but said he believes his best baseball is still ahead.
Livvy Dunne responds to Skenes critic
Former LSU gymnast and social media personality Livvy Dunne later shared photos highlighting moments from Skenes’ season.
One commenter responded, “Tell Paul to lock in.”
Dunne kept her answer short.
“200ks btw,” she replied.
The response came hours after Skenes reached the milestone in Pittsburgh’s final home game of the season.
Skenes and Dunne both became stars while competing at LSU.
Skenes helped lead LSU baseball to the 2023 national championship before the Pirates selected him with the No. 1 overall pick in the MLB Draft. Dunne competed for LSU gymnastics and was part of the program’s 2024 national championship team.
Skenes won the National League Rookie of the Year award after his first major league season and followed it by winning the NL Cy Young Award in 2025.
Despite a more difficult 2026 season, Skenes ended it with a milestone few pitchers in Pirates history have matched.
“I think my best baseball is ahead of me and I think our best baseball is ahead of us,” Skenes said.

item.content:encoded:
El japonés Shohei Ohtani, estrella de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles, volvió a ser el jugador con la camiseta más vendida de las Grandes Ligas, una posición que ocupa por cuarto año consecutivo, según la lista publicada este viernes por MLB y MLB Players, Inc. (Mlbpi).
Ohtani se convirtió así en el primer jugador desde que MLB comenzó a registrar las ventas en 2010, que encadena cuatro temporadas como líder en comercialización de camisetas.
Desde 2023, los aficionados han comprado la camiseta Nike de Ohtani más que cualquier otra en Estados Unidos, Japón y el resto del mundo, consolidando al jugador japonés como la figura con mayor demanda comercial entre los peloteros de las Grandes Ligas.
El listado, elaborado a partir de las ventas de camisetas Nike realizadas a través de Fanatics, incluido MLBShop.com, desde el Día Inaugural de la temporada 2026, sitúa al capitán de los Yankees de Nueva York, Aaron Judge, en el segundo puesto y al jardinero de los Cachorros de Chicago Pete Crow-Armstrong en el tercero.
Crow-Armstrong, quien esta temporada se convirtió en el séptimo jugador en la historia de las Mayores y el primero de los Cachorros en conectar al menos 40 jonrones y robar 40 bases, alcanzó el mejor puesto para un jugador de Chicago desde que el puertorriqueño Javier Báez fue tercero en 2018.
El listado también refleja la presencia de otras figuras de alcance internacional. El venezolano Ronald Acuña Jr., de los Bravos de Atlanta, ocupa el cuarto lugar, seguido por el dominicano Fernando Tatis Jr., de los Padres de San Diego.
Los Dodgers colocaron a tres jugadores entre los diez primeros, con Ohtani al frente, Freddie Freeman en el sexto puesto y Mookie Betts en el octavo. El japonés Yoshinobu Yamamoto, también de Los Ángeles, aparece noveno.
La temporada 2026 marcó además un registro inédito para los jugadores japoneses, con tres de ellos entre los 20 primeros de la clasificación, después de que el toletero Munetaka Murakami, de los Medias Blancas de Chicago, debutara en el vigésimo puesto.
Yamamoto, por su parte, ocupa el noveno lugar, mientras que Ohtani mantiene el liderazgo de una clasificación que vuelve a poner de manifiesto su dimensión dentro y fuera del terreno de juego.
La lista se conoce antes del inicio de las Series de Comodines de ambas ligas, que comenzarán el próximo martes 29 de septiembre, con Ohtani, Judge y Crow-Armstrong entre las principales figuras de unos equipos que ya tienen asegurado su boleto a la Postemporada.

item.dc:creator: Aaliyan Mohammed

The Cubs once again fell short of winning the National League Central, watching the Brewers' four-peat for the first time in the division's history. item.content:encoded:
Pete Crow-Armstrong is the favorite to win the National League MVP Award, and even his rivals have nothing but great things to say about him.
The Cubs once again fell short of winning the National League Central, watching the Brewers' four-peat for the first time in the division's history. The Brewers have their own MVP Award winner in Christian Yelich. Yelich won MVP in 2018 and was the favorite to win a second MVP Award in 2019 before a knee injury in the final month of the regular season.
It's been a while since Yelich won MVP, but at his peak he was a dynamic power-speed threat, just like Crow-Armstrong. Yelich didn't have the advantage that Crow-Armstrong does on the bases with all of the new rules, but he was still able to make a difference at the plate with his power and with his legs on the basepaths. Yelich acknowledged how good a hitter Crow-Armstrong has been this year, despite playing for his rival team.
"He's probably the best defender in the game right now, and it'd be hard to find another hitter that's going as good as he is," Yelich said, per ESPN's Jesse Rogers. "He's had a great year and a special year for him."
Yelich's MVP season was great, but it did not feature Platinum Glove defense.
"Yes, without the defense," Yelich said when asked if he sees similarities between his MVP season and Crow-Armstrong's. "That's what makes him really, really special -- is being able to combine the two."
Crow-Armstrong should win the Platinum Glove this year, and there's a good chance his Cubs and Yelich's Brewers meet in the postseason.
More MLB: Cubs' Jed Hoyer Has Unbelievably High Praise For Pete Crow-Armstrong's Season

item.content:encoded:
The Atlanta Braves will be the No. 3 seed in the National League playoffs this year, locking in their seeding on Thursday night.
Atlanta is coming off a tough series against the Cincinnati Reds that saw them drop two of three games, resulting in their playoff positioning. But the Braves aren’t going to let this get them down, and they will enter the final few games of the season ready to make a statement.
The Braves will be taking on the Miami Marlins for a three-game series, with the team trying to get some momentum heading into the playoffs next week. Atlanta will host the final wild-card team in the first round of the playoffs, but this group has to get through the Marlins first.
Ronald Acuña Jr. Decision Announced by Braves
Ahead of the series with Miami, the Braves have dropped the lineup for the opener. Within this lineup, Atlanta will be hitting star outfielder Ronald Acuña Jr. in the number two spot.
Acuña will be playing in right field for this game against the Marlins.
Braves 9/25
D. Baldwin DH
R. Acuña Jr. RF
M. Olson 1B
M. Harris II CF
M. Dubón SS
O. Albies 2B
M. Yastrzemski LF
A. Riley 3B
S. Murphy C
R. Kerr SP
— Underdog MLB (@UnderdogMLB) September 25, 2026
Acuña has done everything and more for the Braves this season, helping the organization turn things around after missing the playoffs last year. Overall, Acuña has hit .261 with 20 home runs and 55 RBIs, while posting an OPS of .813.
The Braves understand how important Acuña is to their overall success, and he has put together a strong season for the team. Atlanta manager Walt Weiss weighed in on his star outfielder, giving much praise to the veteran.
If the Braves are going to go on a run this year, Acuña will be a key piece to everything. His teammates also understand how important he is, and many of them look up to him on the field.
“When he is healthy and he gets on one of these streaks, he’s one of the best players in baseball,” Braves second baseman Ozzie Albies said. “There’s nothing else to say about that.”
Ronald Acuña Injury Update
Acuña did recently give the Braves a scare when he fouled a ball off his leg, gingerly walking away from the plate. But he seems to be okay for Atlanta with the playoffs starting next week.

item.title: [Reviewing the Brew] Brewers’ Jacob Misiorowski chasing rare franchise history in addition to Cy Young pursuit
item.dc:creator: Evan Frederiksen
item.description: Just one regular-season series against their division rivals, the St. Louis Cardinals, remains in what has been the most successful regular season in Milwaukee Brewers history. A team that many experts picked to finish with 80-85 wins has already reached the 100-win mark with three games left to play in the regular season. With a first-round bye, the top seed in the National League, and home-field advantage throughout the postseason, the Brewers have set themselves up for success for in the play
item.content:encoded:
Just one regular-season series against their division rivals, the St. Louis Cardinals, remains in what has been the most successful regular season in Milwaukee Brewers history. A team that many experts picked to finish with 80-85 wins has already reached the 100-win mark with three games left to play in the regular season. With a first-round bye, the top seed in the National League, and home-field advantage throughout the postseason, the Brewers have set themselves up for success for in the playoffs just as they did a season ago.
However, while the 2025 and 2026 Brewers both achieved the best regular season record in MLB, there's a key difference between the two teams that should have fans feeling more confident in this year's club: The 2026 squad will be led by the best pitcher in baseball, Jacob Misiorowski. Yes, the 2025 team had an ace in Freddy Peralta, who put together the best season of his career last year, but there's no denying that Misiorowski is in a different tier.
Thanks to a sophomore season breakout, the 24-year-old flame-throwing Misiorowski is the clear front-runner for the 2026 NL Cy Young Award. Just one year ago, when the Brewers were deciding whether or not to include Misiorowski on their postseason roster due to his late-season command issues and concerning inconsistency, the thought of Miz running away with the Cy Young in 2026 seemed far-fetched. The dominant right-hander, however, has reached his ceiling far quicker than anyone expected him to, and, as a result, is just weeks away from adding a Cy Young Award to a resume that already includes two All-Star Game appearances.
In pursuit of the National League's top pitcher honor, Misiorowski is unsurprisingly on the verge of etching his name in the franchise record books as well. One impressive franchise record looks all but certain after Miz's memorable 2026 campaign.
Jacob Misiorowski on the verge of setting a new single-season franchise record for the lowest ERA by a starting pitcher
Misiorowski is scheduled to make one more start before the end of the season in Sunday afternoon's season finale against the St. Louis Cardinals. While Miz's most recent start, which came against the Baltimore Orioles, lasted just three innings by design, it's possible the Brewers let their ace go a little deeper on Sunday, as he prepares for his expected start in Game 1 of the NLDS on the following Saturday.
His preparation for the postseason is undoubtedly the most important aspect for Miz in his final start of the regular season, but as the flame-thrower's attention remains locked in on the playoffs, Brewers fans may witness some incredible franchise history. Misiorowski currently sports an otherworldly 1.86 ERA, which is best in baseball this year -- New York Yankee's right-hander Cam Schlittler is in second with a 1.96. However, it's not just the best ERA in baseball that Miz is vying for, which would make him the second Brewer to win an ERA title (Corbin Burnes, 2021); Misiorowski also has a good chance to post the lowest season-long ERA by a qualified starter in franchise history.
The current leader for the lowest single-season ERA in franchise history is Mike Caldwell, whose 2.36 ERA during his incredible 1978 season barely tops the 2.43 mark Burnes posted in 2021. Assuming Miz covers five innings on Sunday, the Brewers' ace would have to allow 11 earned runs to fall behind Caldwell's franchise record.
To make matters even more impressive, given the command troubles that plagued Misiorowski a season ago, the flame-thrower has a chance to set a new franchise record for the lowest WHIP (walks + hits per inning pitched) in a single season. Miz's 2026 WHIP with one start to go is 0.803, and the lowest to this point in franchise history is the 0.940 WHIP Burnes posted in 2021. Pair that with the fact that Misiorowski looks all but certain to set a new franchise mark for strikeouts per nine innings pitched, and it becomes even clearer just how dominant Miz's 2026 campaign truly has been.
For Misiorowski, the 2026 season has been the result of his growth as a pitcher. His one-of-a-kind velocity is certainly the driving factor that catches everyone's attention, but his improved secondary offerings and far better command are why hitters just haven’t been able to come up with any answers. With a chance to make rare baseball and Brewers history, Misiorowski will have one final opportunity to put the cherry on top of what has been a remarkable season for both himself and the Brewers.

item.title: [Claro Sports] Parte médico de Luis Arráez: la lesión que podría condicionar los playoffs de Philadelphia
item.dc:creator: Julian Castillo

item.content:encoded:
Luis Arráez sufrió un esguince en el tobillo izquierdo y los Phillies esperan conocer su disponibilidad para el resto de la campaña.
Las alarmas están encendidas en los Philadelphia Phillies en uno de los tramos más complicados del calendario. El segunda base venezolano, Luis Arráez, abandonó el terreno de juego este jueves ante los Milwaukee Brewers tras sufrir un esguince en el tobillo izquierdo, una lesión que llega cuando el equipo pelea por asegurar su lugar en los playoffs.
No se trata de una ausencia menor. Arráez lidera la Liga Nacional con promedio de .310 y representa una pieza central en una ofensiva que necesita contacto, turnos largos y presencia constante en circulación. Su estatus para los últimos juegos de la temporada regular y una eventual Serie de Comodines todavía no está definido.
El primer parte médico del equipo es un tanto alentador. Las radiografías descartaron una posible fractura, pero el equipo aún debe determinar el grado del esguince y cuánto puede limitarlo al correr, defender la segunda base y ejecutar su juego de contacto.
MÁS INFORMACIÓN: Luis Arráez cambio MLB 2026: destinos del venezolano
¿Cómo se lesionó Luis Arráez con los Phillies?
Le lesión de Arráez se produjo en la sexta entrada ante Milwaukee, con el encuentro igualado 1-1. Arráez conectó un rodado al campocorto Cooper Pratt, quien realizó un tiro desviado hacia la primera base. Jake Bauers tuvo que salir de la almohadilla para recibir la pelota e intentar el toque.
Arráez se desplazó hacia su derecha para esquivar a Bauers, pero apoyó mal el pie y se torció el tobillo izquierdo. El venezolano cayó de inmediato sobre el terreno, se tomó la zona afectada y requirió atención del personal médico. Posteriormente salió del campo con ayuda, sin poder avanzar con normalidad hacia la cueva.
La jugada también terminó con un out por salirse de la línea de carrera, una decisión que generó protesta desde el dugout de Philadelphia. El resultado, sin embargo, quedó en segundo plano. La preocupación pasó a ser la condición física de uno de los bateadores más difíciles de retirar en las Grandes Ligas.
¿Qué dijeron los Phillies sobre la lesión de Arráez?
Los Phillies confirmaron un esguince en el tobillo izquierdo y anunciaron una evaluación adicional durante este viernes para poder tener una visión más completa de su lesión.
El mánager Don Mattingly evitó adelantar un pronóstico sobre el tiempo de recuperación. “Espero que pueda jugar, pero veremos”, señaló tras el partido. También explicó que el cuerpo médico revisaría al venezolano este viernes para conocer su respuesta al tratamiento y evaluar su movilidad.
Mattingly dejó claro que el equipo no cuenta todavía con una fecha de regreso. El diagnóstico de esguince abre un margen amplio, porque la gravedad depende del daño en los ligamentos, la inflamación y la capacidad del jugador para apoyar el pie sin dolor. Philadelphia entra en horas decisivas y no puede planificar con certeza la disponibilidad de Arráez.
¿Cómo puede afectar Luis Arráez a los playoffs de Philadelphia?
La lesión amenaza con alterar la identidad ofensiva de los Phillies. Arráez no depende del poder para impactar un juego. Su valor aparece en la frecuencia con la que pone la pelota en juego, evita los ponches y crea oportunidades para los bateadores de fuerza que vienen detrás en el orden.
Philadelphia lo adquirió desde San Francisco en la fecha límite de cambios con la intención de sumar un bate de élite para el cierre de la campaña. Su promedio de .310 lo mantiene al frente de la Liga Nacional y lo coloca en la pelea por otro título de bateo. Perderlo, incluso por pocos juegos, reduce la calidad del lineup en una etapa donde cada turno puede definir una clasificación o una serie corta.
La situación adquiere más peso porque la posible Serie de Comodines comenzaría la próxima semana. El calendario ofrece poco margen para recuperar estabilidad, especialmente en una lesión de tobillo que afecta los arranques, los cambios de dirección y la defensa en el cuadro.
Edmundo Sosa entró en reemplazo de Arráez durante el juego ante Milwaukee, pero los Phillies podrían necesitar más ajustes en el infield si el venezolano no responde bien en los próximos días. Una ausencia prolongada obligaría al club a redistribuir posiciones y a cubrir un vacío complicado en la parte alta o media del orden.
Philadelphia conserva alternativas para seguir adelante, pero ninguna replica el perfil de Arráez. El venezolano aporta una habilidad que gana valor en octubre: poner la pelota en juego bajo presión. Por ahora, los Phillies celebran que no exista fractura, aunque esperan una noticia todavía más importante: que el esguince no lo saque de los juegos que pueden definir su temporada.

item.content:encoded:
The Toronto Blue Jays have endured a highly disappointing season after winning the American League last year.
The Blue Jays have now officially been eliminated from MLB postseason contention after being swept by the Baltimore Orioles earlier this week. The team struggled to find consistent production throughout the season, and now sits in last place in the AL East at 77-82.
One of the biggest disappointments during an overall frustrating season has been first baseman Vladimir Guerrero Jr.
The six-time All-Star signed a 14-year, $500 million extension with Toronto in April of 2025 and followed it with an excellent season and a trip to the World Series. However, in the 2026 season, he has seen a steep drop-off in production.
A season to forget
Sep 18, 2026; Arlington, Texas, USA; Toronto Blue Jays first baseman Vladimir Guerrero Jr. (27) walks to the dugout after the end of the fifth inning against the Texas Rangers at Globe Life Field. Mandatory Credit: Raymond Carlin III-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
Guerrero is slashing .263/.335/.360 with just nine home runs and 56 RBIs in 142 games. His .695 OPS is the lowest mark of his career. With Toronto's season effectively over, Guerrero's recent comments surrounding his contract were met with a flurry of scrutiny.
In a conversation with Veronica Batista, Guerrero said in Spanish, "The money they gave me wasn't for what I'm going to do. It was for what I already did. They didn't pay me because I'm going to hit 40 every year. They paid me for what I already accomplished."
Given his struggles this season, fans criticized the comments. Guerrero later stood by his remarks, making it clear he is not looking to avoid responsibility.
Guerrero has since received support from Hall of Fame pitcher Pedro Martínez, who is also Guerrero's godfather. Martínez defended Guerrero, stating he was misunderstood and was not intending to excuse his current performance.
Martínez pushes back
Phillip Feliz spoke with Martínez, who said, "He was misinterpreted. What he meant is that contract came from what he's already done, and what he can still do. That's a young man talking. He just didn't explain himself the right way."
Pedro Martínez, Vladdy's godfather, on the contract comments:
"He was misinterpreted. What he meant is that contract came from what he's already done, and what he can still do. That's a young man talking. He just didn't explain himself the right way." pic.twitter.com/W0wXvrGh5y
— Master Flip | Phillip Feliz 🇩🇴 (@Masterflip_) September 25, 2026
Guerrero's comments may have sounded poorly timed given his and the team's struggles this season. However, Martínez wants critics to know that the contract rewarded what Guerrero had already established while also reflecting the belief that he can still produce at a high level moving forward.
For Guerrero, a rebound at the plate next season will be the clearest way to move past this controversy. With 13 seasons left on his deal, he has plenty of time to show Blue Jays fans that he can live up to the expectations of his extension.

item.content:encoded:
The Philadelphia Phillies’ lineup has looked completely different since the addition of second baseman Luis Arraez.
While his production hasn’t been as prolific with the Phillies as it was with the San Francisco Giants, having him as protection for Bryce Harper as the cleanup hitter has enabled the Philadelphia star to take his performance to another level.
The contact-first approach that Arraez brings is something the rest of the team bought into. In August, the Phillies had one of the best offenses in the MLB, improving their on-base percentage and coming up with timely hits.
However, Philadelphia looks like it could be without Arraez for the time being after he suffered a lower leg injury in the series finale against the Milwaukee Brewers. With him, the Phillies were placed last among the lineups of playoff contenders by Stephen J. Nesbitt and Chad Jennings of The Athletic (subscription required); without him, they are solidified in that spot.
Where does Phillies lineup rank among playoff contenders?
They placed the team 13th, and it is hard to argue with that placement based on the numbers in 2026. There are a lot of big names in the lineup, but not much production.
Entering the final series of the regular season, there are only two healthy Phillies players who have a wRC+ that is above the league average: Harper, with a team-high 135, and designated hitter Kyle Schwarber, with a 130.
Arraez was third with a 110, and for a lineup that has been so underwhelming for large chunks of the season, losing him creates a major void in the lineup. Right now, the most consistent hitter beyond that duo is probably Alec Bohm, who got off to a historically poor start but has been excellent in the second half.
He has a .312/.379/.445 slash line in 243 plate appearances and is batting over .300 for the second straight month.
Phillies need supporting cast to step up
Will players on the team wake up and turn things around in October? On paper, this is a star-studded group, loaded with All-Stars such as shortstop Trea Turner, catcher J.T. Realmuto and outfielder Brandon Marsh.
Unfortunately, the first two are in the midst of the least productive seasons of their respective careers, and Marsh has been arguably the worst hitter in baseball for nearly three months. Philadelphia desperately needs them, along with Bryson Stott, to catch fire once again as they did in August.
This team has proven capable of getting hot and producing at a high level. But the odds are certainly stacked against them heading into the postseason, especially with Arraez potentially being sidelined.

item.content:encoded:
Luis Arraez suffered an ankle injury on Thursday night against the Milwaukee Brewers and was on the ground in pain afterward.
He exited the game, and it was revealed that his X-rays were negative and that he has an ankle sprain. With the postseason starting on Tuesday and the Phillies fighting for a spot, his status is unclear. While speaking to reporters, interim manager Don Mattingly revealed he is unsure what Arraez's status is moving forward, but he is hopeful he will return.
"I'm hopeful that he's going to play, but we'll see," Mattingly said to reporters after the game, per 97.5 The Fanatic's Colin Newby. "We'll see where it goes."
Arraez was the Phillies' big acquisition at the trade deadline. He is having a career year defensively and has been an elite hitter for his entire career. The Phillies moved Alec Bohm to first base, Bryce Harper to right field and Bryson Stott to third base to accommodate Arraez, but now they are at risk of missing the postseason. The typical recovery time for an ankle sprain would indicate that he will at least miss the Wild Card Series, but the team will further evaluate him on Friday, per Mattingly.
The Phillies still have a two-game lead over the Arizona Diamondbacks for the final Wild Card spot, but without Arraez, things are not looking great. Arraez's batting average has taken a hit since he joined the Phillies, as he is only hitting .278 with a .678 OPS. However, he is still on pace to win his fourth career batting title.
Losing him for the final series could cost the Phillies a postseason spot, and not having him for the Wild Card Series could have an extremely negative impact on their offense. He has 21 RBIs in 46 games with the Phillies and has a .778 OPS this season with runners in scoring position.
More MLB: Red Sox's Curtis Mead To Take Major Step Toward Return On Friday

item.content:encoded:
Fernando Tatis Jr. saw an opportunity amid a wild celebration in the San Diego Padres locker room and went for it.
As Marty Caswell of Foul Territory interviewed Padres president of baseball operations and general manager AJ Preller after San Diego’s 4-2 win over the Los Angeles Dodgers on Thursday, Tatis entered the picture and endorsed a contract extension for his teammate and relief pitcher Adrian Morejon.
While Tatis was making his case for his buddy, Morejon could be seen in the background making a money gesture a la Johnny Manziel. Preller and Morejon then dapped up before the GM returned to the interview.
Here is a video of those interactions.
Fernando Tatís interrupted my interview with AJ Preller to tell him to re-sign Adrian Morejón @FriarTerritory pic.twitter.com/9t4xc9CaBC
— Marty Caswell (@MartyCaswell) September 25, 2026
Tatis, Morejon, Preller and all the Padres were simply in a great mood after beating the reigning World Series champions at Dodger Stadium in Los Angeles, Calif., to officially punch their ticket to the MLB postseason.
Morejon has been among San Diego’s top performers in 2026, with a 2.86 ERA through 73 appearances and 85.0 innings. Between that and an All-Star nod in 2025, the 27-year-old pitcher has made a strong case for a big new contract with San Diego, which signed him to a 1-year, $3.9 million deal in January to avoid arbitration.
But he can prove himself further in the postseason, as the Padres look to make a deep run and perhaps surprise the baseball world by winning the World Series.

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — A new face in the Arizona Diamondbacks’ 2026 roster has made a surprisingly familiar impression across the baseball world this season, and his jersey sales reflect that.
This player isn’t the team’s longest-tenured star. He’s not one of the young faces fans have watched develop in Arizona, and he might not even be the player most people would expect to lead the way in popularity when it comes to baseball jerseys.
But when MLB and MLB Players, Inc. (MLBPI) posted Nike jersey sales from the Fanatics network of sites — including MLBShop.com — one lone Diamondbacks player made the cut in the top 20: Nolan Arenado.
The best-selling jerseys of the 2026 MLB season pic.twitter.com/6bC6Wd4eCe
— Talkin’ Baseball (@TalkinBaseball_) September 25, 2026
Arenado ranked No. 19 on the list, trailing San Diego Padres shortstop Jackson Merrill and just above Chicago White Sox infielder Munetaka Murakami. Not even Corbin Carroll or Ketel Marte, two of Arizona’s most recognizable players, cracked the list.
The recognition comes after the third baseman’s first year in the desert, one that began with plenty of adjustment and eventually turned into a career rebound.
Arenado arrived in Arizona after spending the previous five seasons with the St. Louis Cardinals. A 10-time Gold Glove winner and eight-time All-Star, the veteran brought plenty of recognition with him, but his transition to the D-Backs didn’t immediately translate into production.
He struggled early and at one point saw his batting average dip below .200. But as the season progressed, Arenado found his footing and put together some of his best offensive numbers in several years.
Arenado currently leads the team in home runs (29) and RBIs (83). That production, combined with his veteran presence, has kept the D-Backs alive in the postseason race.
2026 may have brought Arenado to a new organization, but it also marked something more. He isn’t just helping the Snakes chase a postseason berth; he’s turning a new page in his career.
And perhaps the No. 19 jersey on MLB’s list is another sign of that transition.
Arenado may have been the new guy in Arizona, but his name was already familiar to baseball fans. After a season in which he rediscovered his offensive production and became a central part of the D-Backs’ lineup, that familiarity followed him into the desert — and onto the backs of fans around the country.

Junior Caminero and his Tampa Bay Rays will face the Philadelphia Phillies at Citizens Bank Park, on Friday, Sept. 25 at 6:40 p.m. ET. Caminero has +410 odds to hit a home run as of Friday afternoon.
What It Means
Caminero is hitting for a .275 BA, .360 OBP and .522 SLG with an 18.2% strikeout rate and an 11.3% walk rate. His OPS is .882, which ranks 9th in MLB, and he has scored 96 runs. In 692 plate appearances, he has hit 41 home runs (3rd in MLB) and driven in 99 runs (8th in MLB). He had two hits (going 2 for 5 with two RBIs) in his last game against the Yankees.
Cristopher Sanchez gets the start for the Phillies, his 33rd of the season. He is 18-6 with a 2.93 ERA and 221 strikeouts through 200 2/3 innings pitched.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] William Contreras' Surprise Benching Explained for Brewers
item.dc:creator: Patrick McAvoy
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers have a certain style of play and they aren't going to stray from it, even in a franchise history-making win. item.content:encoded:
The Milwaukee Brewers have a certain style of play and they aren't going to stray from it, even in a franchise history-making win.
On Thursday, Milwaukee won its 100th game of the season, which is the first time in franchise history that a club has reached triple digits, and the Brewers clinched the No. 1 seed in the National League playoffs at the same time. It was a big night, to say the least. Still, despite everything on the line, Milwaukee didn't change how it handles things. For example, William Contreras — who has been red-hot recently — was benched in the eighth inning with the score knotted at one for not running out a grounder earlier in the game.
Jackson Chourio pinch-hit for Contreras and after the game, Brewers manager Pat Murphy confirmed the reason for the All-Star backstop being pulled, as transcribed by Brewers broadcaster Dominic Cotroneo of 620 WTMJ.
The Brewers Play The Game The Right Way
"He didn't run the ball out and [Trea Turner] muffed it," Cotroneo wrote. "I didn't know whether he was gonna be safe. Everyone knows how much William does for our team, how hard he plays, how much he competes. ... But we don't accept that, and he knows that."
The Brewers play the game the right way, and this is yet another example of how. With win No. 100 and the No. 1 seed in the National League on the line, Milwaukee stuck with the precedent it has had all season. Back in August, Brewers shortstop Cooper Pratt was benched in a game for the same thing. He didn't run hard out of the box on a ball that dropped in and got a single, rather than a double.
In Contreras' case, he has been one of the hottest hitters in Milwaukee's lineup recently. Since Aug. 27, he has been slashing .282/.354/.565 with a .918 OPS, six home runs, 28 RBIs, 11 walks, and six doubles. He has been elite and is a big reason why the Brewers were in the position they were in to clinch. That's why it's even more important that the Brewers handled the situation the same way as with the rookie.
They have set the tone and whether you're a multi-time All-Star or a rookie finding your way, in Milwaukee everyone is held to the same standards. It's a good practice to have in professional sports. Plus, it doesn't hurt that Chourio came in and walked, stole a base and then eventually blasted his 25th homer of the season. That makes the decision look a little better, to say the least. The Brewers play the game the right way and were rewarded for it.
Patrick McAvoy's experiences include local and national sports coverage at the New England Sports Network with a focus on baseball and basketball. Outside of journalism, Patrick received an MBA at Brandeis University. For all business/marketing inquiries regarding "Milwaukee Brewers On SI," please reach out to Scott Neville: scott@moreviewsmedia.com
