For more home run swings across the rest of the board, see our MLB home run picks hub, and our guide to finding +EV bets walks through the de-vig math behind Lindy's Trout read.
FAQ
Who Is Lindy And Where Can I Follow His MLB Picks?
Lindy is Eric Lindquist, who hosts "Lindy's Leans, Likes & Locks" on the OddsShopper channel and posts his full daily card on Tails.
What Was Lindy's Biggest Play On The Wednesday, September 23 Card?
His headline play was Mike Trout (LAA) to hit a home run against left-hander Jeffrey Springs at plus-350. He backed it with six more official plays: Toronto's moneyline in Game 2 of their Baltimore doubleheader, Philadelphia's moneyline against Milwaukee, the under on Cardinals-Pirates, the over on White Sox-Royals, a Foster Griffin strikeout prop, and the Dodgers' moneyline against San Francisco.
Does A Lean Count The Same As An Official Play?
No. Lindy talks through spots he's watching but hasn't bet, like Wednesday's Houston and Yankees moneyline leans, separately from the plays he's actually on. This recap only credits him with the seven he officially fired.

item.content:encoded:
Sep 23, 2026, 11:45 AM ET
Toronto Blue Jays first baseman Vladimir Guerrero Jr. (back) remains out of action for Game 1 of Wednesday's doubleheader at Camden Yards against the division-rival Baltimore Orioles, per MLB.com. Sean Keys will make another start at first base and will bat fifth against Orioles right-hander Chris Bassitt. Guerrero is considered day-to-day right now in the final week of the regular season after departing Sunday's game early against the Texas Rangers due to tightness in his lower back. It is something that the 27-year-old Canadian slugger has already dealt with this year, and it could explain why the six-time All-Star has had a very disappointing 2026 campaign. Guerrero enters play on Wednesday with a .263/.336/.359 slash line, a .695 OPS, only nine home runs, 56 RBI, 71 runs scored, and seven steals across his 529 at-bats. Toronto entered play on Wednesday four games out of the final wild-card spot in the American League and on the brink of elimination. If they lose the first game of Wednesday's doubleheader, Guerrero could be shut down for the rest of the week.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com
More Recent News
Jeremy Pena Suffers Wrist Injury on Tuesday


Keith Hernandez




Sep 23, 2026, 11:38 AM ET
Houston Astros shortstop Jeremy Pena (wrist) was hit on the right wrist with a 96.4 mph sinker in Tuesday's game against the Seattle Mariners and was removed in the eighth inning, according to Chandler Rome of The Athletic. Pena attempted to stay in the contest, but he was eventually replaced by Nick Allen at shortstop after going 1-for-4 at the plate with two runs scored and two strikeouts. The Astros likely sent Pena for X-rays, and we will pass along the results when we have them. Fantasy managers will want to check back later to see if the Astros' starting shortstop will be available for Wednesday's game in Seattle against the Mariners. Losing Pena for the rest of the final week of the 2026 regular season would be a huge blow, with the Astros going into Wednesday's action tied for first in the American League West with the Texas Rangers. The 29-year-old Pena has missed time this year due to various injuries, but he has been solid when healthy, slashing .275/.325/.469 with a .795 OPS, 20 home runs, 51 RBI, 77 runs scored, and 10 stolen bases in 107 games across 461 plate appearances.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Athletic - Chandler Rome
Ceddanne Rafaela Set to Return From Injured List on Wednesday


Keith Hernandez




Sep 22, 2026, 11:08 PM ET
The Boston Red Sox plan to activate second baseman/outfielder Ceddanne Rafaela (quadriceps) from the 10-day injured list on Wednesday, manager Chad Tracy told Tim Healey of The Boston Globe. Rafaela should be back in the starting lineup for Boston in Game 2 of the series against the Cleveland Guardians. He has been out since Sept. 6 with a strained right quad but did not play in a minor-league rehab game. The 26-year-old continues to contribute across most fantasy baseball categories, but he could be a little rusty upon his return to the big leagues as the Red Sox try to get him going again before the wild-card series against the division-rival New York Yankees begins next week. Rafaela made the All-Star team for the first time in his career in 2026 and will return to a nice .282/.317/.443 slash line, a career-high .760 OPS, 16 home runs, 70 RBI, 17 stolen bases, and 67 runs scored across 135 games played. If Rafaela hits a home run by the end of the weekend, he will have a new career high in home runs in his fourth year in the majors.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Boston Globe - Tim Healey
Sep 22, 2026, 11:00 PM ET
Chicago Cubs manager Craig Counsell said that third baseman Alex Bregman (face) will not be placed on the injured list and could return to the team's lineup before the end of the regular season, per Russell Dorsey of Yahoo Sports. Bregman was struck in the face by a foul ball while standing in the on-deck circle during Chicago's game against the Cincinnati Reds on Sunday. The 32-year-old suffered multiple facial fractures, but he was able to avoid surgery and appears to be on track to return to the Cubs for the postseason. Across 693 plate appearances in 2026, Bregman is hitting .262/.352/.452 with 26 home runs, 89 RBI, 89 runs scored, and three stolen bases. He's been one of the best hitters in baseball in the second half of the season, hitting .296 with 17 home runs across 262 plate appearances since the All-Star break. With Bregman in the middle of it, the Cubs lineup profiles as arguably the best in MLB in 2026.--Will Brady
Source: Yahoo Sports - Russell Dorsey
Sep 22, 2026, 10:52 PM ET
Boston Red Sox manager Chad Tracy said that closer Aroldis Chapman (lat) "should be cleared in the next day or two," per Tim Healey of The Boston Globe. Chapman has not pitched since September 13 due to lat tightness, but it appears as though the 38-year-old is on the doorstep of a return to his role in the ninth inning for the Red Sox. Across 50 2/3 innings (52 games) in 2026, Chapman has recorded a 1.95 ERA and 1.14 WHIP with 68 strikeouts and 34 saves. The veteran left-hander has not been quite as dominant as he was in his first season with Boston in 2025, but he's still posted an excellent 32.4% strikeout rate and blown just two save chances. When healthy, Chapman remains a must-start closer for fantasy managers.--Will Brady
Source: The Boston Globe - Tim Healey
Joc Pederson Placed on 10-Day Injured List


Will Brady




Sep 22, 2026, 10:47 PM ET
Texas Rangers designated hitter Joc Pederson (hand) has been placed on the 10-day injured list (retroactive to September 19) due to a fracture in his left hand. The 34-year-old had been attempting to play through the injury, but it appears that he and the team ultimately came to the conclusion that a trip to the IL was necessary. Pederson bounced back from a brutal 2025 campaign with a solid year at the plate in 2026, hitting .235/.329/.487 with 26 home runs, 53 RBI, 56 runs scored, and two stolen bases. The veteran lefty slugger re-established himself as an excellent source of big-side platoon power, posting an 11.2% barrel rate and a 50.7% hard-hit rate. With Pederson now sidelined through at least the remainder of the regular season, Texas has rotated shortstop Corey Seager and backup catcher Elias Diaz through its DH spot.--Will Brady
Source: Texas Rangers
Landen Roupp Shut Down for Remainder of 2026


Will Brady




Sep 22, 2026, 10:34 PM ET
San Francisco Giants starting pitcher Landen Roupp told reporters on Tuesday that his 2026 season is over, per Justice delos Santos of The Mercury News. Per delos Santos, Roupp feels fine physically, but is being shut down because he has already blown past his previous career high in innings pitched. Across 155 innings (29 starts) this year, the 28-year-old recorded a 9-14 record with a 4.01 ERA, 1.30 WHIP, and 143 strikeouts. Roupp limits power (0.64 HR/9), which has helped him develop into a capable innings eater for fantasy managers. However, the right-hander's production upside is limited by his middling strikeout rate (21.8%) and his poor walk rate (11.4%). Between his penchant for allowing walks and generating ground balls, Roupp is unlikely to be an asset in the WHIP category without a change in his approach on the mound.--Will Brady
Source: The Mercury News - Justice delos Santos
Sep 22, 2026, 10:29 PM ET
Seattle Mariners closer Andres Munoz (knee) "should be ok" and could be available to his team on Tuesday night after undergoing an MRI on his injured knee, per Shannon Drayer of Seattle Sports 710. Munoz was pulled from his most recent appearance on Sunday after tweaking his right knee, but he appears to have avoided serious injury. It's been a disappointing year overall for the 27-year-old, who has recorded a 4.24 ERA, 1.22 WHIP, 89 strikeouts, and 28 saves across 57 1/3 innings (61 games). Munoz has struggled with home runs (1.41 HR/9) and has blown a career-high 10 saves. However, the hard-throwing right-hander is still averaging 99.7 miles per hour on his fastball and has logged an elite 37.1% strikeout rate. Heading into 2027, Munoz could be an excellent buy-low candidate for fantasy managers.--Will Brady
Source: Seattle Sports 710 - Shannon Drayer
Sep 22, 2026, 10:22 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers left-hander Blake Snell (groin) is scheduled to start against the San Francisco Giants on Saturday, per David Vassegh of AM 570 LA Sports. Snell exited early from his most recent start on September 16 due to a groin issue. However, it appears that Snell will be able to make one final start before the postseason. It's been a lost season due to injury for the 33-year-old, who has missed time due to elbow and shoulder troubles. Still, Snell has been effective when healthy, recording a 4-1 record with a 1.86 ERA, 1.09 WHIP, and 52 strikeouts across 38 2/3 innings (eight starts). Fantasy managers may be able to get one more solid outing from Snell on Saturday, but the Dodgers also have little incentive to push his pitch count deep into the game.--Will Brady
Source: AM 570 LA Sports - David Vassegh
Sep 22, 2026, 10:11 PM ET
Atlanta Braves outfielder Ronald Acuna Jr. (shin) exited early from his team's 4-0 loss to the Cincinnati Reds on Tuesday after fouling a ball off his leg. Per Mark Bowman of MLB.com, X-rays on the leg were negative, and the star outfielder is now being listed as day-to-day with a shin contusion. Acuna Jr. was hitless in one plate appearance before leaving the game. While it appears that he's avoided a serious injury, Atlanta could still choose to be extremely cautious with Acuna Jr. in the final week of the regular season. The Braves have already clinched the National League East title and are likely locked into the number three seed in the NL. Across 455 plate appearances in 2026, Acuna Jr. is hitting .259/.352/.462 with 20 home runs, 55 RBI, 60 runs scored, and eight stolen bases. If he misses any time, Braves outfielders Brewer Hicklen and Mike Yastrzemski would likely see an increase in at-bats.--Will Brady
Source: MLB.com - Mark Bowman
Shohei Ohtani Expected to Return on Wednesday


Keith Hernandez




Sep 22, 2026, 7:50 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers two-way superstar Shohei Ohtani (knee) is expected to be activated from the injured list on Wednesday, as had been the hope, manager Dave Roberts told Sonja Chen of MLB.com. Ohtani is getting ready to return from a stay on the IL that lasted for several weeks. The four-time MVP has not made a start as a pitcher since July 3 against the Padres, and he is not expected to be an option on the mound for the Dodgers at all the rest of the regular season or postseason. But Roberts expects Ohtani to be ready to return on Wednesday against San Diego as the team's primary designated hitter. They will want the 32-year-old Japanese superstar to get some live at-bats going into the final weekend of the regular season before the playoffs begin in October. Ohtani's two-way status has taken a toll on him physically in 2026, although he still has hit a strong .277/.380/.522 with 30 home runs, 80 RBI, 11 stolen bases, and 89 runs scored in 130 games. While he probably will not win a fourth straight MVP award, Ohtani can definitely still help the Dodgers win an unprecedented third straight World Series title if he is past his knee and biceps injuries that have bothered him for around half the season.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com - Sonja Chen
Kyle Tucker Back in Action Tuesday Against Padres


Keith Hernandez




Sep 22, 2026, 7:44 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Kyle Tucker (knee, shin) is starting in right field and is hitting fifth for Tuesday's series opener against the division-rival San Diego Padres and right-hander Michael King, per MLB.com. Tucker was held out of the series finale on Sunday against the division-rival San Francisco Giants with a minor knee/shin injury, but he is ready for this week in a crucial series at Dodger Stadium. The 29-year-old lefty slugger has not had the first season in L.A. that he envisioned, and he enters Tuesday's action with a .234/.334/.393 slash line, a .727 OPS, 17 home runs, 70 RBI, 88 runs scored, and 11 stolen bases across 148 games and 602 plate appearances. The former first-rounder's production has picked up in September, though, which has been good timing for the Dodgers with two-way superstar Shohei Ohtani (knee, biceps) on the injured list. Tucker has hit .283 (17-for-60) with a 1.059 OPS, six homers, and 13 RBI in 19 games in September. Against King in 12 career at-bats, he is hitting .083 with one RBI.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com
Xavier Edwards Still Sidelined Against Cubs


Keith Hernandez




Sep 22, 2026, 5:32 PM ET
Miami Marlins middle infielder Xavier Edwards (thumb) remains out of action for Tuesday's series opener at Wrigley Field against the Chicago Cubs, according to MLB.com. Jared Serna will make the start at the keystone for the Fish on Tuesday and will bat ninth against Cubs left-hander Shota Imanaga. Edwards is missing a second straight start after he injured his thumb on Saturday in San Diego against the Padres. The Marlins are eliminated from postseason contention, but the hope is that Edwards will be able to return during the final week of the 2026 regular season. In his fourth season in the big leagues with the Marlins, the 27-year-old has had another strong season, hitting .280/.360/.371 with a .730 OPS, a career-high six home runs, 52 RBI, 21 stolen bases, and 61 runs scored in 142 games played and 595 plate appearances. Edwards is more of a contact-oriented slap hitter, but he now has three straight seasons with 20-plus stolen bases while being eligible in Yahoo leagues at both second base and shortstop.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com
Sep 22, 2026, 4:58 PM ET
In a surprise move, the New York Mets announced on Tuesday that they agreed to a three-year contract with Andy Green to make him their full-time manager. The Mets have elected to remove Green's interim tag, and he will now be with the team through the 2029 season. Since taking over for previous manager Carlos Mendoza at the end of June, the Mets have gone 37-38. "Andy has connected with and pushed our players to perform, despite the disappointment of the season," owners Steve and Alex Cohen said in a statement. "Over the last several months, he has brought discipline, accountability and positivity to the clubhouse, attributes we were seeking in our next manager." Green was previously the Mets' vice president of player development before becoming the interim manager in New York. He managed the San Diego Padres for almost four seasons from 2016 to 2019 and went 274-366.--Keith Hernandez
Source: New York Mets
Cade Cavalli Done for the Year


Keith Hernandez




Sep 22, 2026, 4:52 PM ET
Washington Nationals right-hander Cade Cavalli is done for the year and will not make another start in the final week of the 2026 season, according to Spencer Nusbaum of The Athletic. Cavalli is healthy, but the Nationals will shut him down given all of his innings and where they are in the standings with no hope of a playoff berth. The 28-year-old former first-rounder in 2020 from the University of Oklahoma had a breakout 2026 campaign in his first full year in the big leagues in D.C., going 13-5 with a 3.02 ERA (3.25 FIP) and 1.15 WHIP with a career-high 200 strikeouts and 48 walks in 169 2/3 innings pitched across his 32 starts. Going into the year, Cavalli had only made 11 starts and had missed all of 2023 after having Tommy John surgery. Washington recently rewarded the rising young arm with a four-year, $47 million contract extension last week. Cavalli will be an intriguing starting-pitching target in all fantasy formats next year after raising his strikeout rate to a career-high 28.3% in 2026.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Athletic - Spencer Nusbaum
Brandon Nimmo Returns From Illness on Tuesday


Keith Hernandez




Sep 22, 2026, 4:44 PM ET
Texas Rangers outfielder Brandon Nimmo (illness) is starting in right field and batting fifth on Tuesday against the visiting New York Mets and left-hander Sean Manaea, according to MLB.com. Nimmo is feeling good enough to play on Tuesday against his old team after a scheduled day off on Monday. The 33-year-old has not lived up to expectations in his first season with the Rangers in 2026, slashing .260/.325/.407 with a .732 OPS, 14 home runs, 61 RBI, 61 runs scored, and seven stolen bases across his 570 at-bats after reaching the 20-homer mark in his final three seasons with the Mets, including a career-high 25 round-trippers in 2025. The former first-rounder in 2011 has slumped in the final month of the regular season, too, going 15-for-66 (.227) with zero home runs, four doubles, eight RBI, five runs scored, six walks, and 22 strikeouts in 17 games in September. Nimmo will attempt to turn things around in the final week of the season and try to help Texas win the American League West division. He has actually hit much better against lefties this year, going 59-for-179 (.330) against them with five of his 14 homers on the year.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com
Jack Flaherty Expected to Pitch This Weekend


Keith Hernandez




Sep 22, 2026, 4:35 PM ET
Detroit Tigers right-hander Jack Flaherty (forearm) is expected to come off the 15-day injured list to make one more appearance this weekend against the Pittsburgh Pirates in the final series of the season, according to Cody Stavenhagen of The Athletic. Flaherty has been sidelined since late July with inflammation in his right flexor, and without going on a minor-league rehab assignment, it seems likely that the veteran hurler will be a piggyback option for the Tigers this weekend in a meaningless game for either veteran Justin Verlander or pitching prospect River Ryan. The 30-year-old has gone 3-8 with a 4.59 ERA (4.09 FIP) and 1.41 WHIP with 102 strikeouts and 42 walks in 86 1/3 innings pitched across his 19 starts in 2026 in his second year in Motown. Fantasy managers still fighting for a championship right down to the wire this weekend should not be looking to stream Flaherty against the Bucs.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Athletic - Cody Stavenhagen
Willson Contreras Still Out With Hand Injury on Tuesday


Keith Hernandez




Sep 22, 2026, 4:10 PM ET
Boston Red Sox first baseman Willson Contreras (hand) remains sidelined for Tuesday's series opener at Fenway Park against the Cleveland Guardians, per MLB.com. Nick Sogard is playing first base again and will bat out of the two-hole against Guardians left-hander Parker Messick. Contreras suffered a bruised right hand when he was hit by a pitch in last week's game against the Texas Rangers, and this will be his fourth straight absence. His hand injury is not considered serious, but the Red Sox are playing it safe with one of their best hitters this year, with the playoffs quickly approaching next week. The 34-year-old Venezuelan has hit .276/.387/.518 this year with a .905 OPS, a career-high 27 home runs, 81 RBI, 68 runs scored, and three stolen bases across his 446 at-bats in his first year in Beantown. The four-time All-Star has played in just four games in September, though, and that came after hitting just .217 (18-for-83) with a .715 OPS in 23 games in August. Contreras should return at some point this week in hopes that he can get back into an offensive groove heading into the wild-card series next week against the division-rival New York Yankees.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com
Christian Scott Closes Out 2026 Season on Injured List


Keith Hernandez




Sep 22, 2026, 4:04 PM ET
The New York Mets announced on Tuesday that they placed right-hander Christian Scott (knee) on the 15-day injured list with inflammation in his left knee and reinstated right-handed reliever Devin Williams (shoulder) from the 15-day IL in a corresponding move. The Mets will shut the 27-year-old down early with nothing left to play for in the final week of the season. After missing all of the 2025 campaign due to Tommy John surgery on his right elbow, Scott returned this year to go 4-5 with a 3.85 ERA (3.61 FIP), 1.27 WHIP, and 134:47 K:BB in 110 innings pitched across 23 starts in just his second year in the big leagues. He only made nine starts as a rookie back in 2024 and went 0-3 with a 4.56 ERA, 1.20 WHIP, and 39:12 K:BB in 47 1/3 innings pitched. Scott is a promising young arm for the Mets and fantasy managers and should be a lock for New York's starting rotation next season as long as he gets through spring training healthy.--Keith Hernandez
Source: New York Mets
Devin Williams Reinstated From Injured List on Tuesday


Keith Hernandez




Sep 22, 2026, 3:59 PM ET
The New York Mets announced on Tuesday that they reinstated right-handed reliever Devin Williams (shoulder) from the 15-day injured list and placed right-hander Christian Scott (knee) on the 15-day IL in a corresponding move. Williams is back for the final week of the 2026 regular season after missing the last six weeks with a strained right shoulder. Right-hander Kodai Senga has become the Mets' primary closer in Williams' absence, and it does not sound like the Mets plan to force Williams into the ninth inning now that he is back for their final six games. The 32-year-old veteran's fantasy stock will be down again going into the 2027 season after another inconsistent season in New York. Williams has gone 3-2 with a 4.66 ERA (3.10 FIP), 1.65 WHIP, 16 saves, 51 strikeouts, and 21 walks in 38 2/3 innings pitched out of the bullpen in his eighth year in the majors. He signed a three-year, $51 million deal with the Mets in December of last year and does not have any opt-outs.--Keith Hernandez
Source: New York Mets
Carlos Rodon Won't Start on Sunday


Keith Hernandez




Sep 22, 2026, 3:47 PM ET
New York Yankees left-hander Carlos Rodon's eight shutout innings with eight strikeouts on Tuesday against the division-rival Tampa Bay Rays was "potentially" his last start of the 2026 regular season, manager Aaron Boone told Chris Kirschner of The Athletic. Rodon will not make the start on Sunday in the regular-season finale against the division-rival Baltimore Orioles as the Yankees prepare for the postseason. With Sunday's regular-season finale unlikely to matter much for playoff purposes, the Yankees will most likely go with a bullpen game and rest Rodon until the start of the wild-card series next week against the division-rival Boston Red Sox. When considering the 33-year-old veteran dealt with left-elbow issues this year, he had a very solid campaign overall, going 6-3 with a 2.95 ERA (3.69 FIP) and 1.13 WHIP with 83 strikeouts and 38 walks in 76 1/3 innings pitched across his 15 starts. The three-time All-Star will be hoping to continue his dominance over Boston this year after allowing four runs (two earned) with five walks and 11 strikeouts against them in 9 2/3 innings over two starts.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Athletic - Chris Kirschner

item.title: [The Times of India] Meet Julio Rodriguez’s alter ego ‘DJ Pleno’: How the Seattle Mariners star is building a surprising second identity through house music, live sets and his growing passion for DJing
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk
item.description: Seattle Mariners center fielder Julio Rodriguez is one of the most recognisable young faces in Major League Baseball with his energetic personality and impact on the field. But by 2026, Rodriguez is starting to be known for another facet of himself as he delves into music and live DJ sets. She goes by 'DJ Pleno' behind the turntables and is 25 years old. It’s a different identity from his baseball career, allowing Rodriguez to tinker with something that doesn’t have anything to do with the No. 4
item.content:encoded:
Seattle Mariners center fielder Julio Rodriguez is one of the most recognisable young faces in Major League Baseball with his energetic personality and impact on the field. But by 2026, Rodriguez is starting to be known for another facet of himself as he delves into music and live DJ sets.
She goes by 'DJ Pleno' behind the turntables and is 25 years old. It’s a different identity from his baseball career, allowing Rodriguez to tinker with something that doesn’t have anything to do with the No. 44 jersey or his duties as a Mariners star. What began as a simple turntable in his home has now become a hobby that he wants to continue to build on.
MLB star Julio Rodriguez introduces Seattle Mariners fans to DJ Pleno
Rodriguez’s DJ persona morphed from a private hobby to a public performance on August 7, 2026, at T-Mobile Park during the Seattle Mariners’ Alumni Home Run Derby. The event was part of the organization’s 50 Seasons Celebration Weekend and featured a number of former Mariners, including star attraction Ichiro Suzuki.
But while the alumni were in the home run competition, Rodriguez had a different task. The Mariners star DJed live under the 'DJ Pleno' name, bringing house music to the ballpark after the game.
The performance gave Rodriguez an opportunity to show a side of himself that most fans had not seen before.
He was no longer in the batter’s box or patrolling center field he was in charge of music and trying to create an atmosphere for the crowd.
To Rodriguez, the name 'Pleno' has meaning. The word has Spanish origins and is ultimately derived from Latin plēnus and ideas like being full, complete or fulfilled.
That meaning helped Rodriguez find an identity that didn't revolve around baseball. Instead of opting for a name that referenced his number on his jersey, the Mariners or his baseball nickname, he wanted 'DJ Pleno' to be its own thing.
The concept also reflects what Rodriguez wants to embody in the persona. He has associated the project with feeling good, being fulfilled and doing things that bring personal satisfaction in his comments around 'DJ Pleno'.
The Alumni Home Run Derby performance was a big step forward because most of Rodriguez’s previous DJing had been done away from a large crowd.
After the Mariners were knocked out of the playoffs in 2025, he began to tinker with equipment at his home in the Seattle area. His initial set-up was primitive, and Rodriguez admitted he had no idea what all the various controls on the equipment did.
His friends who had DJ experience also made fun of his early equipment and method. Rodriguez did not give up the hobby but bought more equipment and kept on practising.
How Julio Rodriguez discovered his passion for DJing
Rodriguez’s interest in DJing came during a period when he was looking for something outside of baseball. He’s been in the limelight since his teenage years, and his career has kept baseball front and center in his everyday life, from top prospect to established MLB star.
DJing gives Rodriguez a different learning experience
Rodriguez’s interest in music goes back a long way, but it was the decision to learn DJing that made it an active hobby. He bought a basic turntable and started practising at home after the 2025 season.
There was an instant learning curve. Rodriguez said he initially had difficulty understanding the controls, but repeated practice helped him become more comfortable with the equipment and the process of mixing tracks.
His musical preferences lie in house music and he is associated with artists such as Martin Garrix and Black Coffee. He doesn’t have a strict daily routine for DJing. Instead, Rodriguez likes to train when the mood is right.
There’s an interesting link to Rodriguez’s baseball career and his new hobby. He has spent most of his life working on his baseball skills, so a lot of the game comes on instinct through years of repetition.
As a novice, Rodriguez has to relearn the fundamentals, make mistakes and slowly improve. And that process has allowed him to think about his own development as a baseball player and to appreciate how much work went into getting to the major leagues.
Rodriguez has likened the thrill of having control of a DJ set to the sensation of creating a big moment on a baseball field.
If you’re a player accustomed to the decibel levels at T-Mobile Park, then playing music in front of a crowd isn’t all that foreign. The energy may be similar, but the source of attention is different.
What comes next for Julio Rodriguez and DJ Pleno
Rodriguez has described 'DJ Pleno' as a work in progress. There doesn’t seem to be a concrete, long-term business plan for the project, but the Mariners star has said he’d like to continue to grow and eventually expand what he’s able to do with music.
He wants to do more than just mix. Rodriguez has said he wants to do his own music in the future, which could see the project move from DJing to production.
Next for Rodriguez is to get more confidence technically and gain more experience in front of audiences. The Alumni Home Run Derby was an important first major opportunity, but the center fielder has hinted there could be more performances to come.
In August 2026, the singer-songwriter Ed Sheeran visited T-Mobile Park, and Rodriguez also discussed his DJing interest with him.
Sheeran told Rodriguez to keep practicing and honing the skill, even if friends or others don’t immediately respond positively to the music. The advice was a simple fact of learning a creative discipline: to improve, you have to repeat and persevere.
What Rodriguez has in store for DJ Pleno is still up in the air. He’s said he’d like to do some original music and play for bigger crowds, but has also teased another possible project during the offseason.
The point of this story is that this DJ persona was purposefully created away from baseball. Rodriguez has long been known as a star for the Seattle Mariners, but 'DJ Pleno' gives him a space to be creative on his own.
For now, 'DJ Pleno' is a budding identity, not a substitute for Julio Rodriguez’s baseball career, but an addition to it. The Seattle Mariners star is creating a name for himself on the pitch, and house music is providing him with another outlet for expression.

item.title: [macombdaily.com] Tigers had the perfect sendoff for Miguel Cabrera. Can they do it again for Justin Verlander?
item.dc:creator: Tribune News Service
item.description: By Evan Woodbery, mlive.com DETROIT — The Detroit Tigers were working off a loose script for how they hoped Miguel Cabrera’s final game would end in 2023. Some of the best parts, however, weren’t in the script. Cabrera had struck out twice and popped out in his first three plate appearances against the Cleveland Guardians on the final day of the season. When he walked in the seventh inning, hardly the storybook ending anyone had envisioned, umpires asked Tigers manager A.J. Hinch if he wanted to
item.content:encoded:
By Evan Woodbery, mlive.com
DETROIT — The Detroit Tigers were working off a loose script for how they hoped Miguel Cabrera’s final game would end in 2023.
Some of the best parts, however, weren’t in the script.
Cabrera had struck out twice and popped out in his first three plate appearances against the Cleveland Guardians on the final day of the season. When he walked in the seventh inning, hardly the storybook ending anyone had envisioned, umpires asked Tigers manager A.J. Hinch if he wanted to stop the game.
Hinch told them to keep playing.
He still had one more scene in mind.
Cabrera, who had not played the field since 2021 and no longer even owned a glove, borrowed one from Spencer Torkelson and trotted to first base for the top of the eighth. His teammates intentionally stayed behind in the dugout for a few moments, leaving Cabrera alone on the field to soak in the cheers.
Then baseball provided the part nobody could have planned.
Steven Kwan hit the first ball of the inning directly to Cabrera, who fielded it and raced to first base for the out. Hinch emerged from the dugout with Cabrera’s three children and removed him from a major-league game for the final time.
It was, as Hinch recalled Tuesday, “the most perfect sendoff of all time.”
Three years later, Hinch is trying to help another Tigers icon reach the finish line.
Justin Verlander will make the final start of his 21-season career on Saturday against the Pittsburgh Pirates at Comerica Park. Once again, the Tigers would love to send one of the greatest players in franchise history into retirement with just the right final moment.
There’s just one problem.
Starting pitchers are a lot harder to script.
“I felt like we could create the moment for [Cabrera] regardless of performance,” Hinch said. “Pitching’s a little bit different.”
With Cabrera, the Tigers controlled much of the setup, except, of course, for Kwan hitting the grounder to first. That was pure baseball serendipity.
With Verlander, almost everything that happens after the first pitch will depend on Verlander himself, the Pirates and the unpredictable rhythm of a baseball game.
Surely the easiest script would be to put Verlander on the mound, wait for something good to happen, perhaps a strikeout, then have Hinch walk out from the dugout and allow Verlander to leave to a standing ovation.
But Verlander has already made clear that he doesn’t want that.
“I don’t just want to go out there and do the one inning and come out and wave,” Verlander said Tuesday. “I would like to toe the rubber one more time in a competitive way and try to win the Detroit Tigers a ballgame.”
Exactly how long that means is anyone’s guess, including Verlander’s.
“No idea. No idea,” he said when asked about his limits.
He told Hinch he would communicate honestly about how he feels Saturday.
“If things are going well and I’m out there and having some success, it doesn’t need to be a perfect game for me to be able to stay out there,” Verlander said. “If I’m able to continue to be healthy and I feel good, who knows what’s going to happen?”
Hinch joked that the ideal scenario would be simple enough.
“We would love the nine-inning no-hitter sendoff,” he said.
Nobody is expecting that, especially from a 43-year-old pitcher who has spent most of the year rehabbing.
The Tigers don’t need Verlander to be perfect Saturday. They don’t even need him to pitch particularly deep into the game.
But they would, naturally, prefer to find the right moment to end it.
A strikeout to finish an inning? Easy enough.
A clean inning after a couple of early jams? That works, too.
But what if Verlander feels good and wants another inning? What if the first batter of that inning doubles? What if the Pirates string together hits? At what point does Hinch decide the competitive portion of Verlander’s afternoon is over and the farewell can begin?
Unlike Cabrera’s final game, there is no defensive position to send him to and no guarantee that baseball will provide an obvious opening.
“The unknown right now is how Justin is going to respond physically to the challenge on Saturday with hitters in the box,” Hinch said. “And there’s no concession on the other side. They’re not just going to get out and make it nice and easy for him.”
That’s important to Verlander.
He wants Saturday to be a farewell, but he also wants it to be baseball.
“He wants to win the game and he wants to contribute to a win and he wants to do his part,” Hinch said.
And somewhere within that competition, Hinch hopes to find the right moment for the sendoff, whether it follows the script or not.
“I do appreciate trying to build the moment to the right time where we can properly say thank you,” he said.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Pete Alonso unanimously named Most Valuable Oriole
item.dc:creator: Mark Brown
item.description: For a lot of the season, there has seemed to be only one obvious choice to end up as the Most Valuable Oriole. You never know if some voters will talk themselves into something silly to stop it from being unanimous. In 2026, it was so obvious that even those people got it right. Pete Alonso was announced ahead of Wednesday's doubleheader as the Most Valuable Oriole for this season. The only real downer about Alonso's first season as an Oriole is the fact that so much of the roster around him was
item.content:encoded:
For a lot of the season, there has seemed to be only one obvious choice to end up as the Most Valuable Oriole. You never know if some voters will talk themselves into something silly to stop it from being unanimous. In 2026, it was so obvious that even those people got it right. Pete Alonso was announced ahead of Wednesday's doubleheader as the Most Valuable Oriole for this season.
The only real downer about Alonso's first season as an Oriole is the fact that so much of the roster around him was incapable for large stretches of the season of doing its part to make this a good Orioles team. Alonso's 40 homers, .265/.359/.510 batting line, and 4.6 bWAR (hopefully with more to come over the last five games) were, in some sense, "wasted." The team will probably be eliminated from postseason contention officially today.
That doesn't take entirely away from the joy that Alonso has brought to the Orioles. He's also brought better-than-advertised first base defense. If he doesn't win a Gold Glove, that would be an egregious snub. He seems excited to be an Oriole in a way that comes along maybe once or twice in a decade, and his sign-off of every interview with "Let's go O's" is charming. We can all feel good about that contract going for four more years, at least for now.
The unanimous selection of Alonso marked the first time that the team had a unanimous winner since Cedric Mullins was the choice in 2021. That was the year that Mullins had the 30 home run/30 stolen base season for the Orioles, breaking out at the plate after giving up on being a switch hitter.
The Orioles do not announce the exact vote breakdown, or even who votes for this award. It is a mystery list of media and broadcasters who cover the team. Camden Chat is not included on that list. Ballots are submitted with a first place, second place, and third place, and the winner is tallied based on a points system. It's easy when it's unanimous for first place.
What the Orioles do announce is a list of players who did not win but also received votes. These guys were all on at least one voter's ballot, in addition to the unanimous winner, Alonso: Blaze Alexander, Samuel Basallo, Shane Baz, Kyle Bradish, Christian Encarnacion-Strand, Rico Garcia, Gunnar Henderson, Trevor Rogers, and Brandon Young.
Weird votes are typically a fixture of this opaque process. Last year was a bigger "weird vote" year – somebody actually voted for interim manager Tony Mansolino a year ago. Somebody else, or maybe the same person, voted for Dylan Carlson, who was a -0.7 bWAR player for the 2025 Orioles. Most of these guys on the 2026 list were at least good for part of the season and can be somewhat justified as choices. Nobody voted for Craig Albernaz or this year's negative bWAR outfielders, Dylan Beavers and Leody Taveras.
In the case of Alexander and Encarnacion-Strand, they just didn't get to play enough to demonstrate more value; their overall performance was good in the games that they played. Alexander missed a bunch of games due to getting bones broken by a hit by pitch. Encarnacion-Strand only arrived in the organization during the season. He might turn out to be a Ryan O'Hearn kind of late bloomer story, or he might turn out to be a Jeremiah Jackson kind of flash in the plan.
When it comes to guys like Bradish, Henderson, Rogers, and Mayo, they weren't good for significant portions of the season, so their season numbers don't look like anything special. You have to squint more for some than for others to see the case. Mayo is closing out the season with three excellent months. Henderson has been hitting well since about mid-August and has maintained value with solid shortstop defense – that's not to say it's flawless, but the good has outweighed the bad even in what is another disappointing year for him overall. For Bradish, I don't know. It felt good when he got that contract extension.
For me, Alonso is at the top, followed by Young and Rogers. Young's surprisingly-good season was probably the only thing that prevented the Orioles from being completely buried in May or June. The team is 19-8 in Young starts this year. Whoever voted for Baz clearly didn't hold the team's 10-21 record in his starts against him. Baz probably "deserves" like 15-16 in his starts.
After Alonso and Young, you can make the case for a lot of people as third place, and that's reflected in the variety of names who also received votes. Rogers was not good in April and May but has looked like a fringe Cy Young candidate ever since. That picks up on last year, when he was a Cy Young-caliber pitcher in the 18 starts that he made. That's why I'd pick him for the third place spot; Rogers was the MVO winner a year ago.
Somebody's going to pay Rogers this offseason. I don't have any hope that it will be the Orioles.

item.title: [MLB.com] Alonso named unanimous winner of '26 Most Valuable Oriole Award
item.dc:creator: Jake Rill
item.description: BALTIMORE -- Every season, one Baltimore player receives the Most Valuable Oriole Award, an honor that is voted on by members of the local print and broadcast media who cover the team on a regular basis. And some years, it can be a difficult decision resulting in a close race. That was not the case in 2026. Pete Alonso was unanimously named the winner of this year’s Most Valuable Oriole Award, the club announced Wednesday. The 31-year-old slugger was the runaway favorite for the recognition, as
item.content:encoded:
BALTIMORE -- Every season, one Baltimore player receives the Most Valuable Oriole Award, an honor that is voted on by members of the local print and broadcast media who cover the team on a regular basis. And some years, it can be a difficult decision resulting in a close race.
That was not the case in 2026.
Pete Alonso was unanimously named the winner of this year’s Most Valuable Oriole Award, the club announced Wednesday. The 31-year-old slugger was the runaway favorite for the recognition, as he was clearly the team’s top player during his first season in Baltimore.
Ballots included up to three players, with points tabulated in a 5-3-1 format (for first, second and third, respectively). The other O’s players to receive votes this year were utility man Blaze Alexander, catcher Samuel Basallo, right-hander Shane Baz, right-hander Kyle Bradish, infielder Christian Encarnacion-Strand, right-hander Rico Garcia, shortstop Gunnar Henderson, infielder Coby Mayo, left-hander Trevor Rogers and right-hander Brandon Young.
But nobody was coming close to Alonso, who has lived up to lofty expectations since signing a five-year, $155 million deal to join the Orioles last December.
Alonso has been racking up honors of late, as he was the Orioles’ nominee for the Roberto Clemente Award and also their recipient of the Heart & Hustle Award. Now, he’s the Most Valuable Oriole -- the first unanimous winner since outfielder Cedric Mullins in 2021 -- and it wouldn’t be surprising if he finishes quite high in American League MVP Award voting after his strong conclusion to the season.
Entering Wednesday, Alonso led Baltimore in hits (156), runs scored (94), home runs (40), RBIs (108), batting average (.265), slugging percentage (.510) and OPS (.869). He’s also the only O’s player to start all 157 games this season.
All of the numbers are impressive. But Alonso’s power and run production have stood out most.
Now sitting at 304 career home runs, Alonso has clubbed at least 37 homers in six of his eight MLB seasons and has reached the 40-homer mark four times. The Polar Bear is the ninth player in Orioles history (since 1954) to hit 40 in a season, marking the 10th overall occurrence.
Alonso’s 108 RBIs are the most in the AL. He is on pace to become the first player in AL/NL history to post a season in which he led the league in RBIs in both leagues. (Alonso had a National League-high 131 RBIs for the Mets in 2022.)
The stats have never been the most important thing to Alonso, though.
“I just want to leave it all out there,” Alonso recently said. “I really love playing the game, and for me, I just want to be all I can be and do whatever I can every single night to win the game, you know? I really take pride in wanting to win and giving it all I have.”
The Orioles (76-81 entering Wednesday) are unlikely to reach the postseason, as they’re close to elimination. But Alonso has four more years remaining on his contract and is hopeful he can lead the club back to the playoffs as soon as possible.
Players to win MVO in first season with Orioles
OF Chuck Diering (1954)
OF Dave Philley (1955)
RHP Stu Miller (1963)
OF Frank Robinson (1966)
OF Ken Singleton (1975)
RHP Rodrigo Lopez (2002, rookie)
SS Miguel Tejada (2004)
DH Nelson Cruz (2014)
C Adley Rutschman (2022, rookie)
1B Pete Alonso (2026)
Alonso has hit well, played strong defense at first base and become a leader inside Baltimore’s clubhouse. He’s been an even better fit with the O’s than those in the organization could have imagined he’d be this past winter.
“My belief on any long-term contract is, if you’re going to do anything over three years -- especially when you get into the five-year, 10-year range -- that person has to have behaviors that impact the environment. You want that guy to have a compound effect where he gets people better,” bench coach Donnie Ecker said. “Pete’s up there with the best I’ve seen, just in terms of caring for the people around him and really not ever settling for average.”

item.title: [Empire Sports Media] Cody Bellinger saved the Yankees' afternoon but the bigger problem survived
item.dc:creator: Alexander Wilson
item.description: Cody Bellinger hit the ball out in the fourth inning, and for a few hours the Yankees had exactly what they needed. His two-run shot was the entire offense in a 2-0 win over Tampa Bay. Carlos Rodon gave them eight scoreless innings. No one needed to discuss the lineup after that first game. The second game changed the conversation. New York lost 6-1, scored only three runs across the doubleheader and watched the Rays clinch the division. item.content:encoded:
Cody Bellinger hit the ball out in the fourth inning, and for a few hours the Yankees had exactly what they needed. His two-run shot was the entire offense in a 2-0 win over Tampa Bay. Carlos Rodon gave them eight scoreless innings. No one needed to discuss the lineup after that first game.
The second game changed the conversation. New York lost 6-1, scored only three runs across the doubleheader and watched the Rays clinch the division. Bellinger’s swing won a game; it did not make the Yankees’ scoring issue disappear.
The Yankees needed that homer from Bellinger
There is a difference between calling one swing a cure and appreciating what it did. Bellinger has 17 home runs and 73 RBI with a .268 average and .779 OPS after Tuesday. He does not need to hit 40 homers to help this club, but his power has to show up in the games where one mistake pitch can decide the result.
He got that pitch from Nick Martinez and did not miss it. The sight of Bellinger rounding the bases mattered more because the Yankees were playing without much margin for error. It was also a reminder that Ben Rice and the rest of the order cannot leave the run production to one man every afternoon.
Tuesday’s opener was a clean illustration of how this team wins when the bats are light: a dominant starter, one big hit and a quiet ninth inning. The evening loss was the other side of the same bet.
A good afternoon cannot carry the whole Yankees lineup
I liked the homer, especially against the club New York spent months chasing. I do not think it is fair to treat it as proof the offense is ready for three October games in a row. Drew Rasmussen held the Yankees down in the nightcap, and they did not find another answer until it was too late.
With Aaron Judge’s availability already under a microscope, the supporting bats have to contribute more than an occasional solo moment. Bellinger delivered on Tuesday. The Yankees still need several hitters to do the same when a short series starts.

item.content:encoded:
The Orioles today announced that first baseman PETE ALONSO has been unanimously voted the winner of the 2026 Louis M. Hatter Most Valuable Oriole Award by members of the local media who cover the team on a regular basis. He will be recognized for his accomplishments during an on-field ceremony prior to tonight’s game against the Toronto Blue Jays.
Alonso is the eighth first baseman (18th instance) in franchise history to be named Most Valuable Oriole, joining JIM GENTILE (1961), BOOG POWELL (1969-1970), LEE MAY (1976), EDDIE MURRAY (1978, 1981-1985, and 1988), RAFAEL PALMEIRO (1995-1996 and 1998), JEFF CONINE (2001), and CHRIS DAVIS (2013 and 2015). He is also the first to be named the unanimous winner of the award since CEDRIC MULLINS in 2021.
The right-handed slugger is slashing .265/.359/.510 (156-for-588) with 24 doubles, 40 home runs, 94 runs, 108 RBI, 78 walks (5 IBB), 11 hit-by-pitches, and five stolen bases, starting all 157 games for the Orioles this season. He enters play today leading the American League in RBI while ranking third in homers, third in total bases (300), fifth in slugging percentage, fifth in OPS (.869), sixth in extra-base hits (64), seventh in hits, and eighth in runs. He paces all Orioles hitters in hits, homers, runs, RBI, total bases, and extra-base hits. Alonso has played in 573 consecutive games, the second-longest active streak in the majors behind Atlanta’s Matt Olson (939 G).
The 31-year-old leads the Orioles with 4.6 Baseball Reference Wins Above Replacement (bWAR) and 4.5 Fangraphs Wins Above Replacement (fWAR), ranking first among all MLB first basemen in fWAR. His 4.6 bWAR is the highest by an Orioles first baseman since CHRIS DAVIS (4.9 bWAR) in 2015.
Alonso earned AL Player of the Week honors for the week of August 10-16 when he slashed .545/.630/.864 (12-for-22) with one double, two home runs, five runs, five RBI, and four walks in six games played. He was the first Oriole to earn the honor since GUNNAR HENDERSON on September 7, 2024, and the first Orioles first baseman since RYAN MOUNTCASTLE on June 5, 2021.
This season, he became the eighth Oriole to hit at least 30 home runs in his first season with the team, joining FRANK ROBINSON (49 in 1966), MARK TRUMBO (47 in 2016), NELSON CRUZ (40 in 2014), MARK REYNOLDS (37 in 2011), ALBERT BELLE (37 in 1999), MIGUEL TEJADA (34 in 2004), and J.J. HARDY (30 in 2011). He also became the fifth player in MLB history to hit 30+ home runs in at least seven of his first eight seasons, joining Mark Teixeira, Albert Pujols, Eddie Mathews, and Ralph Kiner. On September 21, he became the ninth Oriole (10th occurrence) with a 40-homer season, joining CHRIS DAVIS (53 in 2013 and 47 in 2015), BRADY ANDERSON (50 in 1996), FRANK ROBINSON (49 in 1966), MARK TRUMBO (47 in 2016), JIM GENTILE (46 in 1961), ANTHONY SANTANDER (44 in 2024), RAFAEL PALMEIRO(43 in 1998), and NELSON CRUZ (40 in 2014).
The Most Valuable Oriole Award is named in honor of the late LOU HATTER, a former sportswriter for The Baltimore Sun who covered the Orioles for 27 years. Balloting for the Most Valuable Oriole Award concluded last week, with voting on a 5-3-1 basis. Ten other players received a second or third-place vote: BLAZE ALEXANDER, SAMUEL BASALLO, SHANE BAZ, KYLE BRADISH, CHRISTIAN ENCARNACION-STRAND, RICO GARCIA, GUNNAR HENDERSON, COBY MAYO, TREVOR ROGERS, and BRANDON YOUNG.

item.content:encoded:
By LUKE OLSON Associated Press
SEATTLE (AP) — Yordan Alvarez resumed his Triple Crown push with a home run and three RBIs as the Houston Astros beat the Seattle Mariners 7-0 on Tuesday night to pull even with Texas atop the AL West.
Houston snapped a three-game skid and tied the Rangers at 78-79 following their 6-3 loss to the New York Mets at home. Both teams have five games remaining, and the Astros hold the head-to-head tiebreaker.
Seattle (73-84) is on the brink of playoff elimination, one season after winning the AL West for the first time in 24 years and coming within one victory of the franchise’s first World Series appearance.
Alvarez hit a two-run drive to right field in the eighth inning to tie Junior Caminero of the Tampa Bay Rays for the American League lead with 41 homers. Alvarez is first in batting average at .314 and he has 102 RBIs, six behind Baltimore Orioles slugger Pete Alonso for most in the AL.
Miguel Cabrera of the Detroit Tigers in 2012 was the most recent hitter to win a Triple Crown by leading his league in all three of those statistical categories.
Alvarez hit an RBI single in the first to reach 100 RBIs for the second time in his career. Christian Walker belted a three-run homer to make it 4-0 in the third, and Isaac Paredes added a solo shot in the sixth.
It was the 200th home run of Walker’s career and his 26th this season.
Cam Smith snapped an 0-for-26 skid with a double.
Houston starter Cristian Javier was removed after two innings with right groin tightness. He threw 45 pitches. Miguel Ullola (1-0) followed with two innings of one-hit ball for his first major league win.
Bennett Sousa, AJ Blubaugh and Logan VanWey completed the four-hitter.
Mariners starter Logan Gilbert (12-11) lasted only four innings, yielding four runs on 10 hits — the most hits he’s allowed in a game this season.
Up next
Rookie right-hander Ethan Pecko (1-0, 3.77 ERA) makes his fifth major league start Wednesday for Houston against Seattle RHP George Kirby (9-11, 4.24).
___
This story has been corrected to show that Alvarez homered in the eighth inning.

(Photo credit: Kim Klement Neitzel)
The New York Mets removed the interim tag from manager Andy Green by signing him to a three-year deal Tuesday afternoon.
Hours later, the Mets celebrated by nudging the Texas Rangers one step closer to focusing on next season instead of a wild-card series next week.
The Rangers will look to get back on track Wednesday night when they host the Mets in the middle contest of a three-game interleague series in Arlington, Texas.
Left-hander Cody Bradford (0-5, 4.19 ERA) is slated to start for the Rangers against Mets right-hander Nolan McLean (11-10, 3.18).
The Rangers fell out of first place in the American League West on Tuesday night, when Mets southpaw Sean Manaea and a trio of relievers combined on a three-hitter in New York's 6-3 win.
The Rangers (78-79) have the same record as the Houston Astros, who blanked the Seattle Mariners 7-0 later Tuesday. But Texas must win the division outright because the Astros have the tiebreaker by going 9-4 in the season series between the clubs.
No team has ever made the playoffs in a full season with a .500 or worse record.
The Rangers looked like they might climb over .500 when Elias Diaz and Wyatt Langford hit sacrifice flies in the fourth inning to seize a 3-2 lead.
But Texas had just one baserunner the rest of the way and helped the Mets take the lead in the sixth with a pair of defensive miscues.
'To be completely frank, it was a bad showing on multiple fronts,' first baseman Jake Burger said. 'Obviously, it sucks. We wanted to win this game but can't really dwell on it anymore. I'll put my head down on the pillow and focus on tomorrow.'
The Mets (72-85) unofficially have been focused on next year since at least June 26, when Green replaced Carlos Mendoza following a 34-47 start. Green initially said he didn't want the job on a permanent basis because he wanted to focus on his family, including twin daughters who just began their senior year of high school.
But Green said Tuesday he began changing his mind around the trade deadline, when president of baseball operations David Stearns dealt seven veterans, and he discussed the possibility of pursuing the job with his family.
The Mets are 38-38 under Green, including 25-19 since the Aug. 3 trade deadline.
'I suppose late July, which is a tough time to say you started feeling more passion for being in the dugout,' Green said. 'It was the trade deadline, we weren't necessarily winning baseball games, there was a lot of tough conversations that had to be had with players to help walk them through different chapters. But I started thinking if I have such a passion for the hard times, I'm looking forward to the good times.'
Bradford didn't factor into the decision in his most recent appearance last Thursday, when he tossed 4 1/3 scoreless innings as the bulk reliever in the Rangers' 4-3 loss to the Boston Red Sox. He has never faced the Mets.
McLean took the loss last Thursday after giving up one run over six innings as the Mets dropped a 3-0 decision to the Philadelphia Phillies. He didn't factor into the decision in his lone start against the Rangers on Sept. 14, 2025, when he threw six scoreless innings in New York's 5-2, 10-inning victory.
--Field Level Media

Cody Bellinger News: Clubs 17th homer
Bellinger went 1-for-4 with a two-run home run in the first game of Tuesday's doubleheader against the Rays.
The veteran outfielder accounted for the only offense in the matinee when he took Nick Martinez deep in the fourth innings. The Yankees lost the nightcap, however, ending their chances of winning the AL East and locking them into a wild-card spot. Bellinger is having a string close to the regular season, launching five of his 17 homers on the year over the last 13 games while producing a .308/.339/.635 slash line with two steals, nine runs and 11 RBI.

The good news is that we’re less than a week from the end of this disappointing season. Anyway, here’s what’s happening around baseball. item.content:encoded:
Good morning folks!
The Mariners dropped another massive stinker in yesterday’s 7-0 loss to the Astros. The good news is that we’re less than a week from the end of this disappointing season.
Anyway, here’s what’s happening around baseball.
In Mariners news…
- Eric Sanford wants to know what your favorite moments were from this godawful season.
- Over on The Feed, commenter Jose Luis took a crack at outlining an offseason plan for the Mariners.
Around the league…
- The Red Sox have committed to keeping manager Chad Tracy and chief baseball officer Craig Breslow through at least 2029.
- The Mets have agreed to a three-year contract extension with manager Andy Green.
- The Yankees do not expect superstar outfielder Aaron Judge to be available during the Wild Card round.
- Michael Baumann at Fangraphs wonders if the Yanks have what it takes to be successful in the postseason without Judge in the lineup.
- The Cubs are not planning to place third baseman Alex Bregman on the injured list after he suffered multiple fractures in his face from a foul ball.
- The Rays have released former Mariners outfielder Jake Fraley.
- The Rockies became the fifth team in MLB history to have four straight seasons with 100+ losses.
- Paul Skenes blamed the World Baseball Classic for his declining velocity in 2026. As long as players continue to participate in the tournament I’m going to remain skeptical that they sincerely believe any of this.
- David Roth at Defector offered up a different theory: Team USA’s players are being punished for their redassery during the tournament.
- The MLB strike zone shrank a good deal in 2026, reports J.J. Cooper at Baseball America. ($)
- David Schoenfield at ESPN gave his regular season grades for all 30 clubs.
- Jeff Passan handed out his regular season superlatives high school yearbook style.
- Ryan Blake outlined the five biggest questions facing the sport in the run-up to the 2026 postseason.

item.title: [heavy.com] Family of Former Top Red Sox Prospect Marcelo Mayer React to Giants Trade
item.dc:creator: Dan Morrison
item.description: There was a time when the Boston Red Sox had hoped that infielder Marcelo Mayer would be a future cornerstone. That didn’t happen, though, and the California native was traded to the San Francisco Giants for relief pitcher Erik Miller. It was a kind of fresh start that he and the Red Sox both needed. After years of not living up to expectations, sometimes that change of scenery helps. Certainly, his father Enrique Mayer was happy enough to jump “30 feet in the air” when he found out, per the San
item.content:encoded:
There was a time when the Boston Red Sox had hoped that infielder Marcelo Mayer would be a future cornerstone. That didn’t happen, though, and the California native was traded to the San Francisco Giants for relief pitcher Erik Miller.
It was a kind of fresh start that he and the Red Sox both needed. After years of not living up to expectations, sometimes that change of scenery helps. Certainly, his father Enrique Mayer was happy enough to jump “30 feet in the air” when he found out, per the San Francisco Chronicle.
“In Boston, if you’re going well, you’re a god and if you’re struggling, they’re going to tear you apart,” Enrique Mayer said. “He didn’t come out as hot this year and the fans thought he didn’t care — that’s the most ridiculous thing to say about a major-league baseball player, people don’t know the sacrifices and work it takes just to get there. But he got a bad rap and if you get a little bit of one in Boston, it just snowballs.”
Marcelo Mayer was the No. 4 overall pick in the 2021 MLB Draft as a high schooler. He was given a slot price of $6.66 million, and would quickly be put on a pedestal among prospects within the Red Sox Farm System. However, that also added pressure in an intense media market that he struggled to live up to.
“If you set a record for signing bonus, you’re going to have the spotlight on you anywhere — in Boston, multiply that by 10,” Enrique Mayer said. “It was intense. Marcelo started feeling a ridiculous amount of pressure. He’d say, ‘Dad, I’m on the on-deck circle and they’re ripping me apart, yelling, ‘Go back to Cali! ’”
Marcelo Mayer Consistently Dealt With Injuries With the Boston Red Sox
One of the narratives around Marcelo Mayer with the Boston Red Sox was that he was injury prone. Worse, that he wasn’t willing to play through pain or discomfort. However, his father also pushed back on that.
“Marcelo got a cortisone shot to be ready to come back a month and a half early to help the team in the playoffs and then he gets the rap he doesn’t play in pain?” Enrique Mayer said. “That couldn’t be further from the truth.”
Whether the injuries were bad and real or not, they were becoming very common for Mayer. In 2023, he dealt with a shoulder injury, and then a wrist injury. In fact, wrist injuries were a common issue for Mayer, who would see them end his rookie season in 2025 early.
In 2026, Mayer’s dealt with a foot contusion and then a forearm stress reaction. It was the forearm injury that put him on the IL when the Red Sox finally traded him to the Giants.
For his part, Mayer blames the injuries on working too hard. Overuse, in particular, leading to the breakdowns.
“My whole life I’ve always tried to perfect my craft,” Mayer said. “I train really hard and do all I can, that’s how I was raised, but I definitely need to learn how to turn it down a notch sometimes.”
Marcelo Mayer with the San Francisco Giants
When Marcelo Mayer was traded to the Giants, he needed to get healthy. It was a move then that San Francisco hoped would help for the future.
On September 21st, Mayer was finally able to make his debut with the Giants. He’s had four at-bats in those two games, only one of which he played the entirety of. That was his 0-4 debut with 4 strikeouts on off-speed pitches low in the zone, a weakness from his time with the Red Sox.
There is less than a week left in the regular season, but after an up-and-down year, Mayer would love to finish strong. After that, the Giants will be on the outside looking in at the postseason.

item.title: [98.5 The Sports Hub] Marcelo Mayer and his dad couldn't handle Boston
item.dc:creator: Matt Dolloff
item.description: BOSTON, MA – JULY 2: Marcelo Mayer #39 of the Boston Red Sox heads back to the dugout after flying out against the Cincinnati Reds during the fourth inning at Fenway Park on July 2, 2025 in Boston, Massachusetts. (Photo By Winslow Townson/Getty Images) Winslow Townson/Getty Images Even if Marcelo Mayer overcomes his early-career struggles to reach his previously huge potential as a major leaguer, it's clear now that he was never going to be a fit for the city of Boston. Playing for the Red Sox i
item.content:encoded:
BOSTON, MA – JULY 2: Marcelo Mayer #39 of the Boston Red Sox heads back to the dugout after flying out against the Cincinnati Reds during the fourth inning at Fenway Park on July 2, 2025 in Boston, Massachusetts. (Photo By Winslow Townson/Getty Images)
Winslow Townson/Getty Images
Even if Marcelo Mayer overcomes his early-career struggles to reach his previously huge potential as a major leaguer, it's clear now that he was never going to be a fit for the city of Boston.
Playing for the Red Sox is to experience the emotional extremes that come with any kind of intensely passionate fanbase. Succeed at the highest level, and you land somewhere between hero and legend. Fail, and the response can be challenging to handle. It's even harder these days, with the direct access that fans have to athletes through social media. So you're inevitably getting some that cross lines, that make you resent the very city you're calling home at the time.
Boston's fanbase is practically unmatched in sports, so some athletes can deal with the ups and downs better than others. Mayer is obviously on the list of guys that could not deal with it, based on a new story in the San Francisco Chronicle covering the Red Sox' decision to trade him to the Giants and specifically that he and his father Enrique are particularly "thrilled" to be back in California. The Mayers are much closer to their more comfortable surroundings in Marcelo's native Chula Vista, which is still about 500 miles from San Fran, but more importantly, down by the southwestern corner of the United States -- about as far away from Boston as you can get.
“When I found out, I jumped 30 feet in the air,” Enrique Mayer said of the trade. “I can’t explain how happy we are.”
Get the latest Red Sox news.
Marcelo admitted "outside the lines, it's a lot" in Boston while playing for the Red Sox. As he struggled mightily at the major league level -- especially at the plate, where he hit only three home runs with a .594 OPS in 228 plate appearances for Boston this season -- the criticism got to him. The article leads out mentioning a fan allegedly yelling at Mayer to "Go back to Cali!", but that frankly sounds tame and sanitized for a Boston fan. The expectations are higher for a heckler to have the biting cynicism that Bostonians are pretty much born with at this point.
We tend to find it hilarious. A native Californian may feel otherwise.
“In Boston, if you’re going well, you’re a god and if you’re struggling, they’re going to tear you apart,” Enrique said. “He didn’t come out as hot this year and the fans thought he didn’t care — that’s the most ridiculous thing to say about a major-league baseball player, people don’t know the sacrifices and work it takes just to get there. But he got a bad rap and if you get a little bit of one in Boston, it just snowballs.”
L-R: Carlos Correa, Marcelo Mayer
Enrique also pushed back on the notion that Marcelo wasn't willing to play through pain, as he missed significant time due to various injuries during his time in the Red Sox organization. And he's not necessarily wrong about the "sacrifices and work" part; every pro athlete ever has to put the work in just to stay in shape, let alone get to the highest level. The problem is that on the scale of major leaguers, Mayer has fallen woefully short of the expectations placed on him as soon as Boston made him its highest draft pick in franchise history. He could be playing on the moon and there would still be someone asking him what's wrong.
But it's likely going to be much easier for the Mayers to work their way through the problems. Which don't seem to have disappeared yet, by the way. Mayer made his Giants debut on Monday night and went 0-for-4 with four strikeouts. He entered Tuesday's game as a ninth-inning defensive replacement, and if he can't unlock his bat, he'll become that kind of player permanently in a hurry.
There's little doubt that Mayer sifted through some nasty comments directed his way. Boston, due to the aforementioned intense passion, is certainly heavier on that than your average fanbase and harder to deal with than San Francisco Giants fans. Mayer apparently got "threats" on top of that, which are unfortunately more common than they should be on the internet. But it's mostly just empty noise. Mayer needed to ignore the noise the best he could in order to succeed for the Red Sox, and he simply could not.
It's now on him to prove Boston wrong and make the city regret what he must perceive as running him out of town (it definitely wasn't his .193 batting average against curveballs or .122 average against off-speed pitches that did that). Last thing he should want is to validate the accusations of softness and lack of work ethic. But if he flames out, at least he won't deal with as many mean comments about it.

item.content:encoded:
Playoff spots are still up for grabs in Major League Baseball with less than a week to go in the regular season, meaning plenty of teams have their stars in the lineup for a loaded 16-game slate on Wednesday.
For the second day in a row, we have a doubleheader, this time with the Baltimore Orioles and Toronto Blue Jays facing off with their AL wild card hopes hanging by a thread. I’m targeting Orioles star Gunnar Henderson in Game 1 of this doubleheader, as he’s really come on as of late after a largely disappointing 2026 season.
Henderson isn’t the only player to consider, as there’s even a prop set at north of 5/1 odds that I l like on Wednesday night.
Betting on home run props isn’t easy – after all the best players are going deep around 30 to 40 times per season – but they are exciting to bet and can offer some decent payouts if you’re able to pick on correctly.
I view them as a fun way to stay involved in the action during the long MLB season.
So, let’s take a look at the three players I’m eyeing on Wednesday, along with the latest odds from the best betting sites.
Best MLB Home Run Prop Bet Picks for Wednesday, Sept. 23
Hunter Goodman to Hit a Home Run (+287)
Colorado Rockies catcher Hunter Goodman has 39 home runs in the 2026 season, posting an .834 OPS in the process.
An All-Star in 2026, Goodman has been one of the lone bright spots for a Rockies team that remains in the bottom of the standings in the NL West.
On Wednesday, he takes on the Arizona Diamondbacks and Merrill Kelly, who has given up 28 home runs in as many outings this season, posting a 5.00 ERA.
The D-Backs are barely alive in the NL wild card race, but I expect them to have a bit of a quick hook with Kelly if he struggles early on Wednesday. Still, Goodman is worth a look in this market, especially since he’s already homered off of Kelly in his career (15 at-bats).
The Rockies catcher has been slumping a bit as of late, homering just twice over his last 21 games and hitting .200 over that stretch. Still, he has 28 homers against right-handed pitching and hasn’t hit for a crazy average all season long.
I think he’s worth a look in this NL West showdown tonight.
Gunnar Henderson to Hit a Home Run (+466)
Henderson has 24 home runs in the 2026 season, posting just a .224 batting average and a .718 OPS. He’s taken a bit of a step back at the dish, but the one-time All-Star has been hot over the final month of the regular season.
The O’s shortstop has two home runs in his last 10 games, hitting. 342 with a 1.024 OPS during that stretch. On top of that, Henderson is hitting .350 with three extra-base hits in his last five games.
On Wednesday, he takes on Toronto Blue Jays veteran Max Scherzer, who has a 6.07 ERA and has allowed 14 home runs in 16 appearances this season.
Henderson has some strong numbers against Scherzer in his career, going 4-for-10 with a double and a .955 OPS. He hasn’t homered against the former Cy Young winner, but Scherzer has clearly been prone to the long ball in 2026.
At +466, Henderson is a pretty solid value in Game 1 of Wednesday’s doubleheader.
Cody Bellinger to Hit a Home Run (+553)
New York Yankees star Cody Bellinger homered in Game 1 of the team’s doubleheader with the Tampa Bay Rays on Tuesday, and he could have another big game on Wednesday night against left-hander Ian Seymour.
Bellinger is 3-for-5 with a double, a home run and a 2.000 OPS against Seymour in his career, and the star outfielder has been red hot since coming off the injured list earlier in the summer.
Over his last 26 games (25 starts), Bellinger is hitting .305 with five home runs and an .810 OPS. All five of those homers have come in the last 13 games, and the Yankees star is now up to 17 long balls in the 2026 season.
Seymour has struggled to limit home runs, allowing 25 in 127.1 innings of work in 2026. He’s worked as both a reliever and a starter, but the lefty has given up a homer in seven straight outings, allowing 12 homers during that stretch.
Bellinger is an awesome value at +553 in Game 3 of this four-game set.
Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change.
