item.title: [FanSided] The stats make Mets' Pete Alonso decision look historically bad
item.dc:creator: Jake Elman
item.description: Pete Alonso has spent much of the last week going viral, much to Baltimore Orioles fans’ pleasure and New York Mets fans’ … well, we’d call it dismay, but Citi Field viewed things far differently. Alonso has since left New York in more ways than one, and the Orioles are back in Charm City for their final home series. The five-time All-Star hit his 39th and 40th homers in Monday’s 4-3 win over the Blue Jays, becoming only the ninth player in franchise history to join such a club. Fans might dig t
item.content:encoded:
Pete Alonso has spent much of the last week going viral, much to Baltimore Orioles fans’ pleasure and New York Mets fans’ … well, we’d call it dismay, but Citi Field viewed things far differently.
Alonso has since left New York in more ways than one, and the Orioles are back in Charm City for their final home series. The five-time All-Star hit his 39th and 40th homers in Monday’s 4-3 win over the Blue Jays, becoming only the ninth player in franchise history to join such a club.
Fans might dig the long ball, but Alonso has done far more than round the bases so frequently. He entered Tuesday leading the American League with 108 RBIs, and he's only three behind the Cardinals' Alec Burleson for the most in the majors. Despite a relatively slow start, the veteran first baseman has a healthy lead over the Astros' Yordan Alvarez (99) and Rays' Junior Caminero (97) with six games left.
All of that sounds great, but here’s the kicker: At his current pace, Alonso would become the first player in MLB history to lead the AL and NL in RBIs in two separate seasons; he and Aaron Judge tied for an MLB-high 131 RBIs in 2022.
Pete Alonso continues to further humiliate Steve Cohen’s New York Mets
First off, can we just appreciate the fact that no player has ever won the RBI title in separate leagues? You’d think Frank Robinson would have done it seeing as he became the first player to win the MVP in both the AL and NL, but apparently not. Our dark horse pick would have been Mark McGwire.
Alonso’s 4.6 bWAR is his highest since 2019, and he's on track to finish with career highs in on-base percentage (.359) and walk rate (11.4 percent). He cleared the 300-homer mark last week and is currently at 304, so he stands an excellent chance at reaching 400 within the coming years.
All of this follows the Mets allegedly not making Alonso — their all-time home run leader and one of the most beloved players in the post-David Wright era — a formal contract offer this past offseason. Steve Cohen and David Stearns instead opted for Jorge Polanco, who hit .148 with a .431 OPS and -1.4 bWAR over 37 games. Great job, all.
The concerns about how Alonso would age as a power-heavy first baseman were valid, but not offering him a contract easily ranks among the worst decisions in Mets history. You don’t let one of your all-time greats leave without a fight, especially not when he’s still playing at an All-Star level. It’s not like Alonso had a realistic chance to receive $300 million on the open market.
But “what could have been” is the story of the New York Mets’ existence. How far would they have gone in the postseason had they not collapsed in 2007, 2008, and 2025? Would Tom Seaver have helped the Mets return to form rather than join the Reds in the “Midnight Massacre?”
At least Alonso seemingly landed in a place where leadership respects him — and if they’re smart, they’ll consult him on any potential offseason moves. Here’s an idea: Do everything that the Mets wouldn’t do.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Brewers Manager Makes Joey Ortiz's Playoff Role Crystal Clear
item.dc:creator: Patrick McAvoy
item.description: When the Milwaukee Brewers faced off against the Philadelphia Phillies on Tuesday night, they didn't have third baseman Joey Ortiz in the lineup. Ortiz is someone who has had a roller coaster of a season, to say the least. He spent the first few months at shortstop and was very good defensively, but really struggled offensively. At the time, it was talked about how Cooper Pratt would be coming at some point and that would be bad news for Ortiz's role. When Pratt did arrive, Ortiz moved to third
item.content:encoded:
When the Milwaukee Brewers faced off against the Philadelphia Phillies on Tuesday night, they didn't have third baseman Joey Ortiz in the lineup.
Ortiz is someone who has had a roller coaster of a season, to say the least. He spent the first few months at shortstop and was very good defensively, but really struggled offensively. At the time, it was talked about how Cooper Pratt would be coming at some point and that would be bad news for Ortiz's role. When Pratt did arrive, Ortiz moved to third base. At the time, his bat also came alive.
He has turned his season around and he has become a key cog in this lineup, which at one point was very unexpected. But he wasn't in the lineup on Tuesday against the righty Zack Wheeler. Is that something Brewers fans should expect in the playoffs? Brewers manager Pat Murphy broke down that very question, as shared on X by MLB.com's Adam McCalvy.
"Joey doesn't work as well versus that two-seamer, but if it was the playoffs today, Joey would be in there," Murphy said. "He's been so good for us, and I don't want to waver his confidence at all. But he's got a little abdominal strain thing going on that he's been fighting. I noticed a little bit of it a couple of days ago. We're looking to get him a break. And we need to get [David Hamilton] in there. Same with [Luis Lara]. I would probably start [Sal Frelick] today, but we have to get Lara some at-bats against right-handers, too."
Joey Ortiz Will Help Milwaukee
This is an intriguing insight into how the club is viewing the playoff lineup already. Earlier in the season, there was more of a committee at third base. Ortiz and Hamilton both got a chunk of time, but Ortiz really has turned around his season to the point that he deserves to be the main guy.
Ortiz has played in 131 games so far this season and is slashing .267/.326/.403 with a .729 OPS, nine home runs, 46 RBIs, nine stolen bases, 14 doubles, four triples and 49 runs scored. Plus, on top of his elite defense, he doesn't strike out. Ortiz has struck out just 78 times in his 131 games played.
When it comes to the Phillies, they are realistically a team Milwaukee could face in the National League Division Series. If the season were to end today, the Phillies would face the Chicago Cubs in the Wild Card round with the winner of the three-game series heading to face Milwaukee.
If the Brewers and the Phillies face off in the playoffs, Milwaukee will very likely see Wheeler again and it sounds like the lineup would look different, especially with Ortiz. Murphy noted that he would probably start Sal Frelick in a playoff game in this scenario as well.
It may have just been a regular season game on a Tuesday. But we did get some valuable insights into how this club is viewing the lineup heading into the postseason.
Patrick McAvoy's experiences include local and national sports coverage at the New England Sports Network with a focus on baseball and basketball. Outside of journalism, Patrick received an MBA at Brandeis University. Two interim managers have been able to remove “interim” from their titles as the Mets and Red Sox make things official with Andy Green and Chad Tracy. We also know two players who might not be participating in the postseason, at least not right away. Aaron Judge will miss the Wild Card for sure, and Joc Pederson will be sidelined into the postseason.
Also, we look at Paul Skenes, who is pointing to the WBC as a possible culprit for his pitching issues, and we have some questions about the Angels.
Let’s just get right into it.
- Ben Clemens makes a case for Kyle Harrison in the postseason.
- Jay Jaffe tries to make sense of all the potential tiebreaker scenarios in the final week of the season.
- Michael Baumann gets into how things look for the Yankees now that Aaron Judge is back on the bench and might miss the Wild Card series.
- Brian Murphy looks at how this week might change things in the MVP frontrunner races.
- Nick Selbe looks at how the Angels managed to find themselves with an elite starting rotation.
- The big stories that matter in the final week of the season. Story by Karl Rasmussen.
- Paul Skenes has suggested that participating in the WBC may have contributed to his velocity dip this season. (ESPN)
- Robert Murray looks at why players won’t budge on a salary cap.
- The Mets will be standing by their interim manager.
- Ryan Phillips explains why hiring Andy Green is both safe and a leap of faith for the Mets.
- Dan Szymborski wonders, “When will the Angels be competitive again?”
- Joc Pederson is heading to the IL with a hand fracture, but hopes to be back for the postseason. Story by Kennedi Landry.
- Jason Beck reports that Justin Verlander will make one final start this weekend before he retires.
- Jenna West shares the Rays’ new road gray jerseys. (The Athletic subscription required.)
- This is kind of crazy.
- Davy Andrews makes an MVP case for Bobby Witt Jr.
- Zack Wheeler reaches 2000 career strikeouts. Story by Todd Zolecki.
- Tom Verducci looks at the good and the bad going on with the Phillies ahead of the postseason.
- The Athletic staff rank postseason pitching rotations. (The Athletic subscription required.)
- Another interim manager is sticking around for the long haul.
And tomorrow will be a better day than today, Buster. Make it so.

item.title: [rumbunter.com] Pirates Prospect Update: Seth Hernandez, Minor league All-Stars, Connor Wietgrefe
item.dc:creator: Emma Lingan
item.description: Seth Hernandez is wasting little time establishing himself as one of the most important pieces of the Pittsburgh Pirates’ future. Pittsburgh’s top prospect was named the Florida State League’s Top MLB Prospect for 2026 after overwhelming hitters during his brief stint with Low-A Bradenton. item.content:encoded:
Seth Hernandez is wasting little time establishing himself as one of the most important pieces of the Pittsburgh Pirates’ future.
Pittsburgh’s top prospect was named the Florida State League’s Top MLB Prospect for 2026 after overwhelming hitters during his brief stint with Low-A Bradenton. Hernandez made only six starts for the Marauders before earning a promotion to High-A Greensboro on May 12, but his performance left little doubt that he was ready for a bigger challenge.
The 20-year-old right-hander posted a 0.96 ERA with 50 strikeouts across 28 innings, recording at least seven strikeouts in every appearance. He also delivered three consecutive nine-strikeout outings.
Hernandez was named FSL Pitcher of the Month for April after going 2-0 with a 0.53 ERA, 32 strikeouts and five walks in 17 innings. He also earned Pitcher of the Week honors following five scoreless, one-hit innings against Clearwater.
The Pirates selected Hernandez sixth overall in the 2025 MLB Draft, and his stock has only climbed since. After entering 2026 ranked No. 26 overall by MLB Pipeline, Hernandez now sits at No. 7.
Hernandez's season was cut short due to an oblique strain he suffered at the end of July. He still finished the season 6-1 with a 2.43 ERA and 118 strikeouts in 74 innings, putting himself firmly on track to become another potential impact arm in Pittsburgh’s long-term rotation.
Trio of High-A Pirates prospects named South Atlantic League All-Stars
The Pirates’ High-A affiliate produced three more postseason honors, with Axiel Plaz, Jared Jones and Wyatt Sanford all being named South Atlantic League All-Stars for their performances with Greensboro.
Jones earned the nod at first base after an impressive first full professional season. Pittsburgh’s 2025 ninth-round pick hit .311/.411/.567 with 23 home runs, flashing the type of impact bat that has quickly made him an intriguing name in the system despite missing time with injuries.
Plaz was selected at catcher, continuing his development into one of the Pirates’ better offensive prospects. The 20-year-old showed significant power growth at Greensboro, including a two-homer game in August, and currently ranks among Pittsburgh’s top prospects.
Sanford, meanwhile, earned the All-Star spot at shortstop. Pittsburgh’s No. 5 prospect has continued to build on the athleticism and offensive upside that made him one of the system’s more promising young position players.
The three were part of a strong Greensboro club that reached the South Atlantic League championship series, giving Pittsburgh another encouraging sign that its next wave of position-player talent is beginning to take shape.
Connor Wietgrefe, Nick Cimillo earn International League weekly honors to close out 2026
Connor Wietgrefe and Nick Cimillo both finished 2026 on a high note for Triple-A Indianapolis, with the Pirates prospects sweeping the International League’s weekly awards for Sept. 14-20.
Wietgrefe was named Pitcher of the Week after tossing six scoreless, hitless innings against Gwinnett on Sept. 17 with seven strikeouts and two walks. The 24-year-old left-hander closed the season with a 0.51 ERA, 16 strikeouts and a 0.91 WHIP over his final three starts.
Just as importantly, Wietgrefe showed the durability Pittsburgh could value in 2027. He threw 151.1 innings this season, third most among all minor leaguers, and completed at least six innings in nine of his 15 starts with Indianapolis.
Cimillo, meanwhile, earned Player of the Week after hitting .381 with four doubles, two home runs, 13 RBI and a 1.301 OPS. The 26-year-old first baseman was especially hot in September, batting .333 with six homers and 23 RBI in 15 games.
Both finished the year by strengthening their cases for major league consideration, with Wietgrefe in particular looking increasingly close to providing Pittsburgh with rotation depth.

item.title: [Field Level Media] Tigers' Framber Valdez looks to end season on high note against Nats
item.description: Framber Valdez will make his final start of the season when the Detroit Tigers wrap up a three-game home series against the Washington Nationals on Wednesday afternoon. Valdez’s inconsistency is one of the reasons why the Tigers (74-84) find themselves out of the playoff picture. item.content:encoded:
Framber Valdez will make his final start of the season when the Detroit Tigers wrap up a three-game home series against the Washington Nationals on Wednesday afternoon.
Valdez’s inconsistency is one of the reasons why the Tigers (74-84) find themselves out of the playoff picture. The 32-year-old left-hander was signed in the offseason to a three-year contract as a free agent to be the team’s No. 2 starter behind ace Tarik Skubal.
By default, Valdez is the only member of the original five-man starting staff who has lasted the season. Skubal and Casey Mize, both of whom are headed to free agency, were dealt for prospects. Jack Flaherty and Justin Verlander had their seasons wrecked by injuries.
Valdez posted winning records in each of his last six seasons with Houston and never finished with an ERA higher than 3.66 in that time. He enters his 31st start this season with a 10-11 record and 4.06 ERA.
His recent outings reflect the up-and-down nature of his first season in Detroit. He gave up three or more earned runs in each of his last four August starts. He then posted quality starts against Cleveland and Colorado to open September, not allowing an earned run over 13 innings while tallying two victories.
In his most recent outing on Thursday, however, he lasted just five innings against the Chicago White Sox. He gave up a three-run homer to Munetaka Murakami in the first inning.
“I think there was one pitch to regret,” he said through an interpreter. “I think I just left it there hanging and he managed to make good contact with it. But if you put that aside, I was doing my job, being aggressive, having them hit as many ground balls as possible.”
His innings were limited by control problems — he walked four batters. Valdez is 1-0 with a 1.31 ERA in three career starts against the Nationals.
Washington will answer with Richard Lovelady, a reliever by trade who will make sixth start of the season (37th appearance) in a bullpen game. He is 3-4 with a 3.86 ERA and four saves this season.
Over his career, he has made five relief appearances with an 0-1 record and an ERA of 9.00 in four innings.
At the plate, the Nationals’ most dynamic young players, James Wood and CJ Abrams, have gone 4-for-15 during the first two games of the series.
Wood missed most of last month due to an oblique strain but has still racked up 30 homers and 76 RBIs while scoring 104 runs and stealing 21 bases. Abrams has a career-high 33 homers and 102 RBIs while scoring 92 runs and stealing 33 bases.
Abrams provided all the offense the Nationals would need on Tuesday. He reached the 100-RBI mark with a solo homer. He then broke a 1-1 tie by clubbing a two-run shot in the seventh inning. Washington held on for a 3-1 win.
They’re building blocks for a franchise that hasn’t sniffed the postseason since winning it all in 2019. The Nationals (74-84) haven’t posted a winning season since winning the World Series in 2019 but if they can improve their woeful bullpen, Wood and Abrams could carry them to the postseason as early as next year.
“The athleticism — they’re both dynamic players and bring so much to the table outside of when they’re in the batter’s box,” manager Blake Butera said. “I think, honestly, our job is just to set them free and let them go play and do what they do best. … They’re both total-package players, and I’m lucky just to be able to sit there and watch them do their thing. I’m happy they’re on our team.”
–Field Level Media

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Pirates ace Paul Skenes cites WBC as contributor to drop in velocity
item.dc:creator: Jaiman White
item.description: Pittsburgh Pirates' starting pitcher Paul Skenes has come out and revealed that he believes his involvement in the World Baseball Classic is one reason to blame for his inconsistency and alarming drop in velocity in 2026. Skenes spoke to the Pittsburgh Post Gazette on Monday and discussed his mechanics throughout the year, and the challenges that came with playing in the WBC before of the regular season. "There are a lot of other factors, so I don't want to put everything on [the WBC]," Skenes s
item.content:encoded:
Pittsburgh Pirates' starting pitcher Paul Skenes has come out and revealed that he believes his involvement in the World Baseball Classic is one reason to blame for his inconsistency and alarming drop in velocity in 2026.
Skenes spoke to the Pittsburgh Post Gazette on Monday and discussed his mechanics throughout the year, and the challenges that came with playing in the WBC before of the regular season.
"There are a lot of other factors, so I don't want to put everything on [the WBC]," Skenes said. "But I feel like that was kind of the root of it a little bit."
Of course the most glaring disparity in Skenes' game in 2026 was his drop in velocity. His fastball velocity averaged 96.8 mph in 2026, a big tick down from 98.1 mph in 2025 and 98.8 mph in 2024. As the season has gone on it has gotten worse as in his most recent start against the Kansas City Royals saw his fastball average 96.1 mph, and just 95.7 mph in his last start against Miami, which was the lowest in his career.
Although he does not regret his participation in the WBC for Team USA, Skenes did acknowledge that it did completely change his process in the offseason and how he did not have ample time to prepare his body for live innings so early in the year.
"Usually, that time of year, you're kind of ramping up and it's a little bit slow," Skenes said. "You can kind of get onto the slope and find your body. One live [batting practice], you're topping at 97, and then the next you're 98, 99. And that wasn't the case this year. … Looking back, I don't think that really helped."
Skenes went on to say that even in the early months of April and May where he looked like his usual dominant self, he wasn't satisfied with his mechanics and knew that something was off. The former National League Cy Young Award winner had a 1.09 ERA through eight starts in April and May.
"Even then, I didn't feel like I had my delivery," Skenes said. "It's just weird. It's easier to kind of put your finger on it after the fact than it is in the moment. It definitely affected the year. Unfortunately, I don't think I'm the only one. … Yeah, I don't know. [The WBC] definitely didn't make things easier."
Skenes has a 10-11 record this season with the Pirates and with a 3.91 ERA was often all over the place with pitch delivery, location, mechanics and the aforementioned velocity. He's hopeful to get back to his dominant self next season with a full and healthy offseason ahead of him, with regaining his mechanics being a top priority for the Pirates' ace.

item.content:encoded:
The Tampa Bay Rays (96-61) split a day-night double-header with the New York Yankees (90-67) 6-1 on Tuesday night at Yankee Stadium. With the win, the Rays clinched the American League East championship for the first time since 2021, and will be the #1 seed in the American League Playoffs.
The Rays dropped the first game of the day 2-0, before winning the second game 6-1. In the first game, Carlos Rodon (7-3, 2.67) kept the Rays off-balance throughout. He pitched eight shutout innings allowing just three hits while striking out eight and walking none. Cody Bellinger hit a two-run homer in the fourth inning off Nick Martinez (15-5, 2.94) that would be the only offense of the game.
In the second game, it was Drew Rasmussen (16-5, 2.67) picking up the win in a dominant effort. He did not allow a hit in the game until the seventh inning - he finished his night allowing one earned run on just one hit while striking out eleven and walking three. The Rays got one run in the third before adding three huge runs in the seventh to take control of the game. Bryan Baker got the final three outs to close out the division-clinching win.
With the American League East race decided, the Rays and Yankees now look ahead to game three of a four-game series on Wednesday. Ian Seymour (9-7, 4.38) is scheduled to start for the Rays and face Gerrit Cole (9-9, 3.63) for the Yankees. First pitch Wednesday is scheduled for 7:05 PM at Yankee Stadium - pregame coverage begins with Ronnie Lane hosting Inside Pitch at 6:00 PM on 95.7 WDAE & AM 620, your Home of Rays Baseball.
COVER PHOTO COURTESY GETTY IMAGES

item.title: [heraldglobe.com] MLB roundup: Drew Rasmussen helps Rays smother Yankees for AL East title
item.description:
Field Level Media
23 Sep 2026, 12:25 GMT+10
(Photo credit: Brad Penner) Drew Rasmussen allowed one hit in 6 2/3 outstanding innings and the visiting Tampa Bay Rays clinched the American League East with a 6-1 victory over the New York Yankees on Tuesday night in the nightcap of a day-night doubleheader. The Rays won for the 20th time in 28 games and clinched their fifth division title. Tampa Bay last won the AL East in 2021 when it won a team-record 100 games. Yandy
item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

23 Sep 2026, 12:25 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Brad Penner)
Drew Rasmussen allowed one hit in 6 2/3 outstanding innings and the visiting Tampa Bay Rays clinched the American League East with a 6-1 victory over the New York Yankees on Tuesday night in the nightcap of a day-night doubleheader.
The Rays won for the 20th time in 28 games and clinched their fifth division title. Tampa Bay last won the AL East in 2021 when it won a team-record 100 games. Yandy Diaz drove in four runs on a pair of singles.
Rasmussen (16-5) took a no-hitter into the seventh until Heliot Ramos opened the inning with a double to left for New York. Ramos eventually scored on an RBI single by rookie George Lombard Jr. off Kevin Kelly.
Rasmussen finished with 11 strikeouts for his fourth career double-digit strikeout performance. He finished two shy of his career-high set June 10 against the Boston Red Sox and the Rays won his 12th consecutive start.
Yankees 2, Rays 0 (Game 1)
Cody Bellinger hit a two-run home run in the fourth inning as host New York recorded a shutout over Tampa Bay in the opener of a day-night doubleheader.
With the victory, the Yankees temporarily prevented the Rays from clinching the AL East and moved six games ahead of the Boston Red Sox for the American League's top wild-card spot.
New York's Carlos Rodon (7-3) scattered three singles over eight innings as the Yankees finished off the victory in a brisk 2 hours, 2 minutes. Rodon struck out eight in his 100th career win and also reached 1,500 strikeouts for his career. Rays right-hander Nick Martinez (15-5) allowed two runs on five hits over six innings with seven strikeouts to take his first loss since July 9.
Dodgers 7, Padres 0
Freddie Freeman drove in three runs, Will Smith and Tommy Edman hit home runs, and Los Angeles inched closer to the best record in the National League with a shutout of visiting San Diego.
Eight Dodgers pitchers held down the red-hot Padres offense in a bullpen game, with Justin Wrobleski (12-5) earning the win. Roki Sasaki struck out two in one inning in his return from a blister issue. The Dodgers extended their home winning streak to 11 games.
Los Angeles moved to within one game of the NL-best Milwaukee Brewers and reduced its magic number for a top-two NL spot and a bye into the National League Division Series to one. Luis Campusano had two hits for the Padres, whose magic number to clinch a playoff spot remained at two.
Phillies 6, Brewers 4
Bryson Stott delivered the tiebreaking hit in the eighth inning to guide Philadelphia to a victory over visiting Milwaukee. Brandon Marsh homered and knocked in three runs as the Phillies lowered their magic number to two to clinch a postseason berth.
Zack Wheeler ended up with a no-decision after striking out 11 while giving up three runs and five hits in 5 2/3 innings. Wheeler struck out the first seven batters he faced, setting a Phillies record for consecutive strikeouts to begin a game. His first-inning strikeout of Brice Turang was the 2,000th of his career.
The Brewers saw their lead over the Dodgers for the top record in the majors shrink to one as they lost just the third time in their last 13 games. William Contreras knocked in three runs.
Marlins 8, Cubs 2 (12 innings)
Griffin Conine plated the go-ahead run that ignited a six-run 12th inning for visiting Miami, which snapped a three-game losing by beating Chicago and postponing the Cubs' playoff celebration for at least a day.
On a night when runs were scarce until the final inning, both teams endured a pair of scoreless extra frames before Conine broke the drought with a leadoff, golf-shot single off Caleb Thielbar that fell just inside the left field line. Esteury Ruiz, the automatic runner, scored from second to make it 3-2 as the Marlins sent 10 batters to the plate in the inning.
The Cubs could have clinched a wild-card playoff spot with a win or Arizona loss, but neither of those happened keeping the Diamondbacks mathematically alive. Josh Ekness (3-4) struck out a pair in the 11th inning to get the win while Thielbar (3-4) gave up three runs -- two earned -- in his inning of work.
Guardians 3, Red Sox 2
Nathaniel Lowe drove in Chase DeLauter with a sacrifice fly in the ninth inning and Cleveland held on to beat host Boston in the first game of a three-game series.
Cleveland not only extended its winning streak to six but maintained its one-game lead over the Chicago White Sox for first place in the AL Central.
Parker Messick held Boston to one run on five hits in five innings, his 14th straight start allowing three runs or fewer. Payton Tolle started for the Red Sox and gave up two runs on eight hits in 5 2/3 innings as the Guardians went 1-for-12 with runners in scoring position and stranded 15.
White Sox 14, Royals 11
Chase Meidroth smacked a three-run home run among his three hits and drove in five, and Brenton Doyle, Randal Grichuk and Munetaka Murakami also homered to power Chicago past host Kansas City.
Chicago won for the fourth time in five games to remain one game behind the AL Central-leading Cleveland Guardians. The White Sox, who hold the third and final AL wild-card spot, reduced their magic number to earn a playoff berth to three.
Vinnie Pasquantino hit a ninth-inning grand slam for the Royals, who lost their fifth straight. He went 3-for-5 with a double and also drove in five.
Nationals 3, Tigers 1
CJ Abrams hit a pair of home runs and drove in all three runs as visiting Washington topped Detroit. Abrams reached 100 RBIs for the season with his solo shot in the second inning, then broke a 1-1 tie in the seventh with his 33rd long ball of the season, a two-run blast.
Dylan Crews had two hits and scored the other run for the Nationals. Rookie Jackson Kent (2-4) earned the win in long relief. He allowed one run on six hits over four innings and struck out three. Opener Riley Cornelio lasted 2 2/3 innings, striking out four and walking three.
Ben Malgeri scored the Tigers' only run. Kevin McGonigle and Max Clark each had two hits.
Pirates 2, Cardinals 0
Jared Jones and two relievers combined on a one-hitter as Pittsburgh beat visiting St. Louis for a fifth straight win. Jones (5-6) lowered his ERA to 1.08 in four September starts and struck out nine with zero walks over seven innings while throwing 63 of his 86 pitches for strikes.
Pittsburgh broke a scoreless tie with two outs in the sixth inning on Ryan O'Hearn's RBI single against Andre Pallante (12-8). Pallante allowed one run on three hits with two walks and two strikeouts over six innings.
St. Louis struck out 14 times and lost for the fifth time in its last six games.
Astros 7, Mariners 0
Christian Walker hit a three-run home run, Yordan Alvarez launched a two-run homer and Isaac Paredes added a solo shot as Houston slugged and pitched its way past host Seattle.
Jose Altuve, Yainer Diaz, Alvarez and Paredes each collected two hits for the Astros, who pulled into a first-place tie with the Texas Rangers in the West. Five Astros pitchers combined to throw a four-hit shutout. Miguel Ullola (1-0) earned his first major league win, allowing one hit and striking out two over two innings of relief.
Julio Rodriguez notched two hits for Seattle. The Mariners went 0-for-3 with runners in scoring position and stranded nine.
Reds 4, Braves 0
Brandon Williamson fired six scoreless innings and Cincinnati supported him with three solo homers to defeat host Atlanta in the opener of a three-game series.
Cincinnati ended a two-game losing streak and evened the season series with Atlanta at 2-2. Williamson (5-4) worked six scoreless innings, allowing three hits and two strikeouts. Elly De La Cruz (29), Dane Myers (8) and Eugenio Suarez (25) each hit a home run for the Reds. It was Suarez's 350th career homer, making him the 10th active player to reach that mark.
Atlanta starter JR Ritchie (1-4) pitched five innings and allowed one run on four hits and three walks. The rookie struck out a career-high eight batters.
Mets 6, Rangers 3
Francisco Alvarez laced a go-ahead two-run double in the sixth, then scored an insurance run on an unusual sacrifice fly for visiting New York, who damaged Texas' playoff hopes with a win in the opener of a three-game interleague series in Arlington.
Juan Soto had an RBI single in the third, and Carson Benge capped the scoring with a run-scoring double in the seventh for the Mets. The club won hours after removing the interim tag from manager Andy Green and signing him to a three-year extension.
Josh Jung had an RBI double in the third, and Elias Diaz and Wyatt Langford lofted sacrifice flies in the fourth for the Rangers, who entered Tuesday with a one-game lead over the Houston Astros in the AL West.
Diamondbacks 7, Rockies 2
Nolan Arenado homered and doubled among his three hits, Michael Soroka tossed seven strong innings, and Arizona kept its slim postseason hopes alive with a win over host Colorado in Denver.
Geraldo Perdomo also had three hits and Ildemaro Vargas finished with two hits for Arizona, which remains alive in the NL wild-card race, sitting four games behind Philadelphia, San Diego and the Chicago Cubs for the third and final spot with five games to go.
Mickey Moniak homered for Colorado, which finished with just three hits and just one after the third inning. The Rockies (57-100) are the first team to lose 100 or more games in four straight seasons since the 1962-65 New York Mets.
Twins 3, Giants 2
Walker Jenkins homered, Luke Keaschall contributed both offensively and defensively, and Minnesota evened its road interleague series against San Francisco.
Taj Bradley (12-6) combined with four relievers on a six-hitter for the Twins, who used two late diving catches by Keaschall in right field to prevent the Giants from taking the first two of the series.
Bradley allowed just one other hit -- a fifth-inning single by Drew Gilbert -- in his six innings. He walked three and struck out six. Keaschall's one-out triple scored Ryan Kreidler, then Brooks Lee gave Minnesota the lead for good with a run-scoring single to plate Keaschall.
A's 9, Angels 7
Carlos Cortes hit a go-ahead two-run homer in the bottom of the eighth inning and the Athletics overcame a six-run deficit to beat Los Angeles in West Sacramento, Calif.
In addition to the homer off Sam Bachman, Cortes also delivered a pinch-hit RBI triple in the seventh, helping the Athletics end a six-game losing streak. Zack Gelof hit a two-run homer later in the eighth for the A's. Shea Langeliers and Lawrence Butler each had three hits and an RBI for the Athletics.
Denzer Guzman homered and drove in four RBIs for the Angels, who have lost four of their last six games. Mike Trout added three hits and two runs for Los Angeles (60-97), which has never lost 100 games in a season.
Blue Jays at Orioles, ppd.
The scheduled game between Toronto and host Baltimore was postponed due to ongoing inclement weather. The game will be made up as part of a split doubleheader on Wednesday, with games starting at 1:35 p.m. and 6:35 p.m. ET.
--Field Level Media

item.title: [heraldglobe.com] Astros slug 3 homers, blank Mariners to pull even in AL West
item.description:
Field Level Media

Field Level Media

23 Sep 2026, 10:35 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Joe Nicholson)
Christian Walker hit a three-run home run, Yordan Alvarez launched a two-run homer and Isaac Paredes added a solo shot as the visiting Houston Astros slugged their way to a 7-0 victory over the Seattle Mariners on Tuesday.
Jose Altuve, Yainer Diaz, Alvarez and Paredes each collected two hits for the Astros (78-79), who pulled into a first-place tie with the Texas Rangers in the American League West. Houston owns the head-to-head tiebreaker over Texas, so would win the division if the teams remain tied at the end of the season.
Five Astros pitchers combined to throw a four-hit shutout. Miguel Ullola (1-0) earned his first major league win, allowing one hit and striking out two over two innings.
Julio Rodriguez notched two hits for Seattle (73-84). The Mariners went 0-for-3 with runners in scoring position and stranded nine.
Jeremy Pena led off the game with an infield single to shortstop, stole second, and scored on Alvarez's single to right. It marked the 100th RBI of the season for Alvarez, the second time in his career he's reached that milestone. Paredes and Altuve followed with singles, loading the bases with no outs.
Seattle starter Logan Gilbert (12-11) escaped the first-inning jam when Diaz struck out looking before Walker and Taylor Trammell flied out.
Altuve and Diaz opened the third with back-to-back singles before Walker launched his 26th home run of the season and the 200th of his career, a three-run shot to deep left, giving the Astros a 4-0 lead.
In the fifth, J.P. Crawford drew a one-out walk. After Randy Arozarena struck out swinging, Dominic Canzone singled to center. Crawford advanced to third, but Cal Raleigh struck out to end the inning.
Houston's advantage increased to 5-0 on Paredes' solo homer in the sixth.
With one out in the eighth, Pena was hit by a pitch, and Alvarez belted a slider over the wall in right for his 41st home run of the season, extending Houston's lead to 7-0.
Houston starter Cristian Javier tossed two shutout innings, allowing one hit and two walks while striking out two. The Astros announced Javier exited the game with groin tightness.
Gilbert gave up four runs on 10 hits over four innings, walking two and striking out three.
--Field Level Media

item.title: [mlb.com] Boundless confidence powers Rays to AL East title, home-field through ALCS
item.dc:creator: Adam Berry
item.description: NEW YORK -- Back in Spring Training, the preseason predictions and projection systems were skeptical of the Rays. After consecutive fourth-place finishes, they were widely picked to finish last in the American League East this year. Those doubts persisted throughout an up-and-down start to the season. They seemed to reappear every time the Rays stumbled through a brief losing streak. Slights surfaced in other ways, too, with pundits repeatedly referring to other clubs as the team to beat in a di
item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK -- Back in Spring Training, the preseason predictions and projection systems were skeptical of the Rays. After consecutive fourth-place finishes, they were widely picked to finish last in the American League East this year.
Those doubts persisted throughout an up-and-down start to the season. They seemed to reappear every time the Rays stumbled through a brief losing streak. Slights surfaced in other ways, too, with pundits repeatedly referring to other clubs as the team to beat in a division led by Tampa Bay.
Now, there can be no doubt. The Rays are once again AL East champions, and the road to the World Series in the AL will run through Tropicana Field.
“I don't think anything was handed to us all year. Obviously, I think a lot of guys expected [the Yankees] to run away with it, and [it] probably to be New York, Boston and Toronto at the top,” veteran starter Nick Martinez said. “No one really expected us to be here, so we've had to fight for it from the beginning of the season.”
Fittingly, the Rays had to fight to make it official on Tuesday night. After a 2-0 loss in Game 1 of a doubleheader at Yankee Stadium, the Rays held on to win Game 2, 6-1, behind a dominant performance by ace Drew Rasmussen, who struck out 11 on a career-high 114 pitches and carried a no-hit bid into the seventh inning.
In what was expected to be a four-team race, the fifth team finished first.
“Four teams got all the attention in this division, and they're four really good teams, right?” president of baseball operations Erik Neander said. “Just a testament to these guys and just an unbelievable year, and they deserve this. They deserve to enjoy this.”
That they did.
After shortstop Taylor Walls scooped a grounder from George Lombard Jr. and fired it to first baseman Jonathan Aranda for the final out, the team poured onto the field for handshakes, high fives and hugs. Coaches, players and staff changed into AL East “CHAMPS” shirts and hats and gathered in front of the mound for a team photo, then took the celebration inside.
The Rays popped bottles of champagne, poured beer, sprayed silly string, smoked cigars and danced. Manager Kevin Cash started the party with a reminder that they want to do this three more times next month.
“This group has deserved it all year long, and it's a special group,” Yandy Díaz said through interpreter Kevin Vera. “This is just the beginning, and in our minds, the biggest and the most important celebration is the World Series one.”
This is the fifth division title in franchise history, joining 2008, ‘10 and ‘20-21. It’s the fourth time the Rays have claimed the AL’s best record, as they also did so in 2010, ‘20 and ‘21. And they found it fitting to clinch this time while debuting new road jerseys that put their home region front and center.
“Sitting there in the ninth inning, watching that with ‘Tampa Bay’ across our chests, with all that this franchise has been through in this past year, man, it's a great time to be a fan of the Tampa Bay Rays,” Rays CEO Ken Babby said. “So proud of this group.”
For all the questions they've faced, the Rays have spent nearly the entire season as the top team in the AL. Tuesday was their 88th consecutive day in first place, dating back to June 27, and their 128th day overall atop the AL East standings.
“To have the opportunity to run the race from start to finish is special,” Rasmussen said. “We know this isn't the finish line. We know that this is a regular-season accomplishment. 
“But man, it feels really good.”
While other contenders have risen, fallen, surged and struggled behind them, the Rays haven’t had a full month with a losing record all season. And they aren’t taking their foot off the gas, having won nine of their last 11 games while putting together an MLB-best 40-19 record since July 20.
That felt like an appropriate date to look back on Tuesday morning, when the Rays reported to Yankee Stadium knowing that just one win in this series would seal the deal. It was, as Walls put it, “a pivotal moment” in Tampa Bay’s season.
Coming out of the All-Star break, the Rays were swept by the Red Sox in a four-game series at Fenway Park from July 17-19. Maybe their nice little run was nearing an end.
But then Martinez scaled the mound and fired six strong innings in Toronto, providing leadership on and off the field, as he’s done all season. The Rays won three straight against the Blue Jays, followed that up with a winning homestand, then reeled off a perfect 9-0 road trip out west.
They haven’t looked back since.
“You can tell a lot about a team with how they respond to something like that,” Walls said. “Just being able to stop the bleeding when it's happening, being able to get back up, get going, focus on what's ahead of you and not focus too much on the past -- I feel like that's kind of been the difference this year.”
Ask around the clubhouse about where that consistency comes from, and you’ll hear different versions of the same answer. It’s chemistry that carried them through the course of the season, the bond that brought them together and the belief that they could do what nobody else expected.
“I'm very happy, very happy, because this is a special group,” Junior Caminero said. “When I got to Spring Training, first day, I [saw] this group, and I [told] them, ‘We've got to play [in] October this year.’
“And we did it.”

item.title: [Bozeman Daily Chronicle] Triple Crown still within reach for Astros slugger Yordan Alvarez after big game in Seattle
item.dc:creator: LUKE OLSON
item.description: SEATTLE (AP) — Houston Astros slugger Yordan Alvarez gained some ground Tuesday night in his chase for a Triple Crown. He still has plenty of work to do this week. The AL MVP front-runner went 2 for 4 with his 41st home run and three RBIs in the Astros' 7-0 win over the Seattle Mariners. item.content:encoded:
SEATTLE (AP) — Houston Astros slugger Yordan Alvarez gained some ground Tuesday night in his chase for a Triple Crown.
He still has plenty of work to do this week.
The AL MVP front-runner went 2 for 4 with his 41st home run and three RBIs in the Astros' 7-0 win over the Seattle Mariners. Alvarez hit an RBI single in the first inning, was intentionally walked in the second and then belted a 386-foot homer in the eighth with a 109.5 mph exit velocity.
“At this point, I keep wondering why guys are pitching to him,” Houston first baseman Christian Walker said. “He just seems to come through in every moment. He's dangerous at the plate right now.”
Alvarez, who is quiet and shows little emotion, orchestrated a team meeting after the Astros (78-79) were swept by Atlanta on Sunday, squandering their lead in the AL West. His performance on Tuesday was much-needed to put Houston in a tie with the Texas Rangers atop the division with five games left this season.
“He's been backing it up all year,” Astros manager Joe Espada said.
Alvarez's two-run shot to right field tied him with Junior Caminero of the Tampa Bay Rays for the American League lead with 41 homers. Alvarez is first in batting average at .314 — five points ahead of Tampa Bay's Chandler Simpson — and he has 102 RBIs, six behind Baltimore Orioles slugger Pete Alonso for most in the AL.
Alonso drove in three runs with two homers Monday against Toronto, but the teams were rained out Tuesday in Baltimore because of bad weather. They are scheduled to play a split doubleheader Wednesday.
Alvarez has six homers since Aug. 1, and the 29-year-old designated hitter has eight RBIs over 17 games in September. He'll need more to become baseball’s first Triple Crown winner since Miguel Cabrera in 2012.
Alvarez leads the AL in slugging percentage (.601), OPS (1.032), total bases (329) and walks (106). Logan Gilbert intentionally walked Alvarez in the second inning Tuesday, which was the 33rd time for Alvarez this season, already a franchise record.
It’s been a historic season for the four-time All-Star after he was limited to 48 games in 2025 because of a broken hand and an ankle injury.
If he wins the AL MVP award, the Cuban slugger will join Shohei Ohtani of the Los Angeles Dodgers as the only players to win an MVP award while primarily serving as a designated hitter. Othani was close to winning a Triple Crown in 2024 after leading the NL in homers (50) and RBIs (130), but his .310 average fell just short to Luis Arráez’s .314.

item.content:encoded:
BOSTON — Nathaniel Lowe had a tiebreaking sacrifice fly off reliever Erik Miller in the ninth inning, and the Cleveland Guardians maintained their slim in the AL Central with a 3-2 victory over the Boston Red Sox on Tuesday night.
Angel Martínez had three hits for the Guardians, who entered the day with a one-game lead over the White Sox atop the division. Chicago owns the tiebreaker by winning the season series. Cleveland stranded 15 baserunners.
The loss was Boston’s eighth in 12 games, spoiling Chad Tracy’s first game as manager after the club named him its 49th in team history.
Adley Rutschman added three hits for Boston, which clinched one of the AL’s wild-card spots on Sunday.
Boston pinch hitter Mickey Gasper hit Hunter Gaddis’ first pitch, tying it at 2-2 leading off the eighth.
Gaddis (5-3) got the win and Cade Smith recorded the final three outs for his 40th save.
Miller (4-2) hit a batter and gave up two hits in an inning.
A strong candidate for the AL Rookie of the Year, Cleveland left-hander Parker Messick gave up a run over five innings. He lowered his ERA to 2.55 and is on pace to become the fourth rookie starting pitcher in MLB history with an ERA under 2.60 and averaging 9.0 or more strikeouts per nine innings.
In his tune-up for a likely playoff start next week, Boston lefty Payton Tolle struggled with his control over 5 2/3 innings, giving up two runs on eight hits.
Up next
Guardians LHP Foster Griffin (15-5, 3.67 ERA) is set to face Red Sox RHP Sonny Gray (17-5, 2.82) on Wednesday in the middle game of the three-game series.

item.content:encoded:
It wasn’t the (potential) final Coors Field game Kyle Freeland dreamed of.
Unfortunately, the Rockies lost their 100th game of the season, and he only pitched three innings in the loss. The Rockies mustered just eight baserunners, and only two came around to score early in the game they lost to the Arizona Diamondbacks, 7-2.
(Potential) Coors Field Swan Song
In what could be Kyle Freeland’s final start at Coors Field as a Rockie, he wasn’t very sharp. He gave up a lead-off single to Ildemaro Vargas, but then got Rockies-killer Ketel Marte to pop out to short. Following that, Gabriel Moreno doubled to score Vargas, and Geraldo Perdomo singled to score Moreno and put the Diamondbacks up 2-0. Nolan Arenado singled to reach base for the 11th time in 11 games against the Rockies this year, but then Freeland was able to strike out Jordan Lawlar. Other Rockies-killer Corbin Carroll added another run on another double before Tim Tawa walked to load the bases. However, Jose Fernandez grounded out to end the inning.
Freeland allowed just a single to Marte in the second, but then gave up a lead-off double to Arenado in the third. Lawlar grounded out and Carroll lined out, but then Tawa hit a ground-rule double — the fourth of the ballgame — to score Arenado. Fernandez struck out on a foul tip to end the inning.
Freeland came out for the fourth, but allowed a single to Vargas that turned into two bases when Zac Veen committed an error. Unfortunately, that was the end for the Denver native in this game. His final line: 3.0 IP, 9 H, 5 ER, 1 BB, 2 K. He threw 69 pitches, 44 for strikes.
“I think he was behind in counts early,” manager Warren Schaeffer said, noting that the Diamondbacks had “a good plan.”
“I don’t think he was as sharp in the zone,” he added.
When his press conference had ended, Schaeffer added this: “This guy’s meant to much to our organization over the years, and the ultimate pro. You hate to see it end like that.” Schaeffer thanked him for his contributions on the field and in the community.
“Not how you want to draw it up,” an emotional Freeland said, thanking his teammates, coaches, family, and fans.
“It was an emotional day,” he noted. “I made sure to soak up every single minute of it.”
Freeland added to fans, “I appreciate you so much. I love you so much,” adding, “I’m proud to be a Colorado Rockie.”
Baserunners galore, but runs no more
The Rockies offense was befuddled by Michael Soroka early, but finally broke through in the third inning. Mickey Moniak broke out of his slump with a solo shot to right-center to break up the shutout.
Troy Johnston then doubled and Veen reached on an error by Tawa. Jake McCarthy grounded into a force out that nabbed Veen at second, and then Johnston came around to score on a Connor Norby sac fly, cutting the lead in half, 4-2.
Unfortunately, McCarthy tried to do McCarthy things and was picked off trying to steal second. And even more unfortunately, the next eight were retired until Norby walked with two outs in the sixth. But then TJ Rumfield flied out to left to end the threat.
In the seventh, Cole Carrigg was hit by a pitch after Hunter Goodman struck out, and then Kyle Karros and Moniak struck out. In the eighth, Johnston was hit by a 99.5-mph fastball to kick things off. Veen then flew out to left and McCarthy struck out swinging, snapping his career-best 22-game on-base streak. Norby struck out to end the inning and strand another baserunner.
In the ninth, Rumfield flew out to end his 24-game on-base streak — the longest active streak in the Majors and longest by a Rockie since Tyler Freeman’s 25-gamer from June 13-July 12, 2025 — while Goodman grounded out. Carrigg singled for just the third hit of the game, but Karros grounded into a fielder’s choice to end the game.
The Rockies offense mustered eight baserunners all game: three hits, two errors, two hit batters and one walk. The two runs came around to score on the back-to-back hits in the third inning.
Still, Schaeffer remains positive.
“I see a lot of hope, and I see a lot of progress,” he said. “This is obviously not where we want to be.”
He added, “You have to focus on the positives moving forward.”
Gritty Bullpen
Zach Agnos came in to relieve Freeland, immediately getting Marte to ground back out to him. But Moreno hit a sac fly to add another run, 5-2, and then Perdomo singled and stole second. Arenado was called out on strikes to end the inning.
In the fifth, Lawlar led off with a double and Carroll grounded out to Goodman. And Tawa hit a sac fly to score Lawlar from third to make the score 6-2. Fernandez popped out to third to end the inning.
In the sixth, Agnos issued a lead-off walk to Vargas. Luckily, he got the next three batters out. But then Arenado smacked a 421-foot homer to lead off the seventh, putting him a triple away from the cycle (which he would ultimately not get).
Luckily, though, he retired the next three batters thanks in part to a diving play from Carrigg to nab Tawa.
Nick Frasso came in to relieve Agnos in the eighth and was able to pitch a 1-2-3 inning. Juan Mejia took the ninth, and pitched (kind of) a 1-2-3 inning. Moreno grounded out to first and Perdomo singled. Arenado popped out to dash his cycle hopes, and then Perdomo got caught in a rundown trying to steal second to end the inning.
Up Next
The Rockies will look to regroup tomorrow, and the Diamondbacks will look to keep their postseason aspirations alive.
Mason Adams (0-1, 5.09 ERA) will face off against Merrill Kelly (9-14, 5.00 ERA). First pitch is at 6:40pm.
See you then!

item.title: [Claro Sports] Pete Alonso busca una marca histórica que nadie ha conseguido en 106 años de Grandes Ligas
item.dc:creator: Juan Carlos Campos Rodríguez
item.description: El primera base de los Orioles está cerca de alcanzar un registro que no tiene registro desde hace más de un siglo en las Grandes Ligas Pete Alonso está cerca de conseguir una marca inédita en la historia de las Grandes Ligas. El Oso Polar vive una temp
item.content:encoded:
El primera base de los Orioles está cerca de alcanzar un registro que no tiene registro desde hace más de un siglo en las Grandes Ligas
Pete Alonso está cerca de conseguir una marca inédita en la historia de las Grandes Ligas. El primera base de los Orioles de Baltimore tiene la oportunidad de convertirse en el primer jugador en más de un siglo de MLB que termina como líder de carreras impulsadas en ambas ligas, una estadística oficial que se tiene registro desde 1920.
El Oso Polar vive una temporada destacada con Baltimore y llega a la recta final del calendario como uno de los principales productores ofensivos de la Liga Americana. Su objetivo es completar una hazaña que ningún pelotero ha logrado desde la creación de las Grandes Ligas modernas.
La posibilidad de Alonso tiene como antecedente su rendimiento cuando formaba parte de la Liga Nacional. El toletero ya consiguió encabezar ese departamento en 2022 con los Mets de Nueva York y ahora busca repetir la hazaña del otro lado de la MLB con los Mets de Nueva York.
MÁS INFORMACIÓN: Justin Verlander prepara su última apertura en las Grandes Ligas
Alonso busca dominar las carreras impulsadas en ambas ligas
El reto de Pete Alonso está relacionado con su capacidad para producir carreras, una de las principales características que ha mostrado durante su trayectoria en las Grandes Ligas.
El primera base llegó a la temporada 2026 con una carrera consolidada como uno de los bateadores de mayor poder en MLB y ahora tiene la oportunidad de sumar un logro que ningún jugador ha alcanzado en 106 años de historia.
Durante su etapa anterior en la Liga Nacional, Alonso logró posicionarse como uno de los mejores productores ofensivos del circuito con 131 carreras impulsadas. Ahora, con los Orioles, busca repetir ese dominio en la Liga Americana.
De acuerdo con los registros históricos, ningún pelotero ha terminado una temporada como líder de carreras impulsadas en ambas ligas, por lo que Alonso podría convertirse en el primero en conseguirlo.
MÁS INFORMACIÓN: Alex Bregman recibe pelotazo en el rostro y abandona juego
Una temporada histórica con los Orioles
Pete Alonso llegó a Baltimore como una de las principales incorporaciones ofensivas del equipo y rápidamente asumió un papel importante dentro del orden al bate. El jugador ha mantenido su capacidad para generar extrabases y producir carreras, características que lo han acompañado desde su debut en MLB en 2019.
Además de su producción ofensiva, Alonso continúa ampliando su legado dentro del béisbol profesional. En 2026 también alcanzó una marca importante al llegar a los 300 cuadrangulares en su carrera, logro que consiguió como jugador de los Orioles frente a los Mets, su antiguo equipo.
Alonso busca entrar en la historia de MLB
La recta final de la temporada será determinante para conocer si Pete Alonso consigue completar una de las hazañas más difíciles del béisbol moderno. A menos de una semana de finalizar su primera temporada con los Orioles de Baltimore, Pete Alonso se mantiene en la pelea por una marca histórica. El primera base suma 108 carreras impulsadas, nueve más que el cubano Yordan Álvarez, quien acumula 99 y ocupa el segundo lugar de la Liga Americana en este departamento.
Con la recta final del calendario por disputarse, Alonso tiene una ventaja importante para quedarse con el liderato de impulsadas. Salvo que Álvarez tenga una última semana extraordinaria, el jugador de Baltimore podría terminar la campaña en la cima de este rubro y acercarse a una hazaña que no se consigue desde hace más de un siglo.

item.dc:creator: Mac Cerullo
item.description: For all intents and purposes, none of these last games down the stretch mean anything to the Red Sox. They have already punched their ticket to the playoffs and nothing that happens from here on out will change that. item.content:encoded:
For all intents and purposes, none of these last games down the stretch mean anything to the Red Sox. They have already punched their ticket to the playoffs and nothing that happens from here on out will change that.
But while readying themselves for the games that matter, the Red Sox would still prefer to go into the postseason with some momentum, and Tuesday’s performance was at times pretty hard to watch.
Playing without three projected postseason starters, the Red Sox suffered a listless 3-2 loss in their series opener against the Cleveland Guardians. Despite a game-tying pinch hit home run by Mickey Gasper in the bottom of the eighth, the Red Sox gave the lead right back in the ninth, capping off a night riddled with poor decisions and uncharacteristic mistakes.
Reliever Erik Miller saw his struggles continue by allowing two hits, a walk, a hit batsman and the go-ahead sacrifice fly by Angel Martinez in the top of the ninth, and outside of Gasper and Adley Rutschman going 3 for 4 with two doubles and a run scored, there wasn’t much to write home about as the Red Sox suffered their third straight defeat.
“He’s working through stuff,” Red Sox manager Chad Tracy said postgame of Miller. “I thought today was even another step in the right direction, the hit batter, the free passes are what gets you and I think he also got some bad batted ball (luck).”
Making his final start before the playoffs, Payton Tolle wasn’t as sharp as he would’ve hoped, but once again he gave the Red Sox a chance to win.
After posting a scoreless first, Tolle allowed two runs and five baserunners over the course of a challenging second inning. He started by giving up a leadoff double, had a soft grounder from David Fry deflect off his leg and into the outfield for an RBI single, and allowed another single and a walk to load the bases with nobody out.
Tolle was able to minimize the damage from there, allowing a second run to score on a double play ball by Brayan Rocchio before escaping the inning. He continued facing traffic for the rest of his outing but grinded his way into the sixth and departed to a standing ovation from the Fenway Park faithful.
Tolle finished with two runs allowed on eight hits, two walks and a hit batsman over 5 2/3 innings with five strikeouts. He fell one out short of recording another quality start, leaving him with 13 in 26 outings, and he ends his rookie regular season with a 3.03 ERA and 171 strikeouts in 148 2/3 innings.
When Tolle next takes the mound, it will most likely be at Yankee Stadium to start a game in the AL Wild Card Series.
“I’m really proud of this group,” Tolle said. “I’ve had so much fun obviously with these guys and to continue to go into the postseason with them and I’m really excited about us.”
The Red Sox got a run back in the bottom of the second after Rutschman led off with a double and came around to score on an RBI groundout by Andruw Monasterio, but otherwise the bats struggled against Guardians rookie Parker Messick. The left-hander, who came into the game with a 2.57 ERA and projects as a possible AL Cy Young Award finalist, limited the Red Sox to one run on five hits over five innings.
One thing Boston was able to do was drive up the rookie’s pitch count, particularly in the fourth when Monasterio was able to work a 12-pitch walk. That helped force the lefty from the game after five, giving the Red Sox a chance to try their luck against Cleveland’s bullpen.
The Red Sox let a golden opportunity go to waste in the bottom of the sixth, leaving men at second and third, but Alec Gamboa kept it a one-run game in the top of the seventh despite the Guardians taking advantage of some sloppy baseball to get runners at second and third themselves with one out.
Cleveland’s Fry, who had already grounded into a fielder’s choice where the runner was thrown out at the plate earlier in the third inning, did so a second time for the second out of the seventh, and Gamboa struck out former No. 1 overall pick Travis Bazzana to end the inning.
Then, in the bottom of the eighth, Gasper struck for his 10th home run of the season, hitting the first pitch he saw from Guardians reliever Hunter Gaddis 390 feet to the right field stands.
The good vibes didn’t last long.
Miller, who had proven an impactful bullpen addition since his arrival at the trade deadline, saw his recent control issues continue with his latest ugly outing. The left-hander hit the first batter he faced, gave up the lead on a sacrifice fly by Martinez and eventually loaded the bases before getting a fly out to keep things from spiraling further.
Miller has now allowed six runs and six walks over his past 3 1/3 innings, a trend the Red Sox can’t afford to continue if he’s to remain a high-leverage option in the playoffs. Miller said postgame that he felt less comfortable on Tuesday than he had the last time out in Tampa Bay, but while his patience is wearing thin the only way to overcome his struggles is by pitching through them.
“I would like to have been through this by now and be over it but all I can do is keep taking the ball and get through it,” Miller said. “There’s no way I can feel better and get through without throwing in games so that’s how it’s going to have to be, just keep throwing and get through it.”
As for what he hopes to see from his club over the last week, Tracy said the big thing is keeping everyone healthy and engaged.
“You’re still working on timing, you’re still working on things with your swing, so all of that matters,” Tracy said, adding that the other big priority is being proactive with the pitching staff. “Looking at it before the game, who do we want available today, being strict to it and trying to get the guys in the bullpen the work that they need but still being competitive in that game. So there’s a lot of things that you’re doing.
“I told the guys before we earned the right to be in a position to line things up, but that being said we still want to go out and win games,” Tracy continued. “We had a chance to do that tonight, we did some things well, I think we were (0 for 9) with runners in scoring position, so we had our chances.”
Rafaela expected back
Following the game Tracy said he expects Ceddanne Rafaela will be activated from the injured list on Wednesday. Willson Contreras still has some soreness in his hand and won’t return to the lineup but is getting closer, and Tracy confirmed Trevor Story was given a scheduled day off to give him some rest ahead of the playoffs.
Aroldis Chapman, who has been dealing with some lat tightness, may also be ready to return to action on Wednesday as well, though Tracy said they’ll want to make sure he feels good pregame before making that call.

item.dc:creator: The Associated Press
item.description: DENVER (AP) — Nolan Arenado had his team-leading 28th homer of the season among his three hits, Michael Soroka struck out nine in seven innings of one-run ball and the Arizona Diamondbacks beat Colorado 7-2 Tuesday night, sending the Rockies to their 100th loss of the season. The victory kept the Diamondbacks four games behind Philadelphia in the race for the third and final NL wild-card spot with five regular-season games remaining for both teams. The Rockies’ loss made Colorado the first franc
item.content:encoded:
DENVER (AP) — Nolan Arenado had his team-leading 28th homer of the season among his three hits, Michael Soroka struck out nine in seven innings of one-run ball and the Arizona Diamondbacks beat Colorado 7-2 Tuesday night, sending the Rockies to their 100th loss of the season.
The victory kept the Diamondbacks four games behind Philadelphia in the race for the third and final NL wild-card spot with five regular-season games remaining for both teams.
The Rockies’ loss made Colorado the first franchise to lose at least 100 games in four consecutive seasons since the New York Mets from 1962-65.
Arenado, a four-time All-Star in his time with Colorado, extended his on-base streak to 16 games. During that stretch, he is batting .379 with seven homers and 14 RBIs.
Gabriel Moreno drove in two runs, giving him 10 RBIs in Arizona’s past 16 games. Geraldo Perdomo added three hits and an RBI for the Diamondbacks.
In four starts against the Rockies this season, Soroka (9-5) has allowed just four earned runs in 23 innings, with 23 strikeouts and six walks.
Kyle Freeland (4-11) took the loss for Colorado, allowing five earned runs in three innings. The Denver native made his final home start of the season for Colorado, where he has played his entire 10-year MLB career.
Mickey Moniak and Connor Norby drove in Colorado’s runs. Moniak hit his 23rd home run of the season. TJ Rumfield and Jake McCarthy failed to record a hit or walk. The two entered the game with the longest active on-base streaks in the majors, with Rumfield at 24 games and McCarthy at 22.
Up next
Arizona RHP Merrill Kelly (9-14, 5.00 ERA) will take on Colorado RHP Mason Adams (0-1, 5.09) on Wednesday in the second game of a three-game series.
___
See AP’s full MLB coverage here
Craig Meyer, The Associated Press

item.dc:creator: The Associated Press
item.description: PITTSBURGH (AP) — Jared Jones allowed one hit over seven dominant innings and the Pittsburgh Pirates inched closer to the franchise’s first winning season in eight years with a 2-0 win over St. Louis on Tuesday night. The hard-throwing Jones (5-6) retired the first 16 batters he faced before Nathan Church’s bloop landed just beyond the outstretched glove of Pirates third baseman Jacob Gonzalez with one out in the sixth. Church sprinted to second for a double but remained there after Masyn Wynn l
item.content:encoded:
PITTSBURGH (AP) — Jared Jones allowed one hit over seven dominant innings and the Pittsburgh Pirates inched closer to the franchise’s first winning season in eight years with a 2-0 win over St. Louis on Tuesday night.
The hard-throwing Jones (5-6) retired the first 16 batters he faced before Nathan Church’s bloop landed just beyond the outstretched glove of Pirates third baseman Jacob Gonzalez with one out in the sixth. Church sprinted to second for a double but remained there after Masyn Wynn lined out and J.J. Wetherholt struck out to end the inning.
Jones, who returned from Tommy John surgery in late May, tied a season high with nine strikeouts in seven innings and improved to 3-0 with a 1.13 ERA in four starts in September. Gregory Soto worked around a leadoff walk to record his 16th save.
Ryan O’Hearn delivered an RBI-single for the Pirates and rookie shortstop Konnor Griffin had two hits for Pittsburgh, and Bryan Reynolds added his major league-leading 40th double. The Pirates have won five straight to improve to 80-77 with five games remaining. Pittsburgh is seeking its first winning campaign since going 82-79 in 2018.
Andre Pallant (12-8) nearly matched Jones pitch for pitch in six innings of work. The right-hander’s only hiccup came in the sixth, when Oneil Cruz walked with one out, moved to second on a fielder’s choice and scored on O’Hearn’s sharp single to left. Pallant is just 2-2 in 10 starts since the All-Star break despite pitching to a 3.00 ERA over that span.
The Cardinals fell to 76-81 with the loss. If St. Louis doesn’t win out, the franchise will experience consecutive losing seasons for the first time since 1958 and 1959, the second-longest stretch between consecutive losing years in the history of major North American professional sports.
Up next
The series continues on Wednesday. Matthew Liberatore (5-14, 5.36 ERA) gets the start for the Cardinals. The Pirates have yet to announce a starter in what is likely a bullpen game.
___
See AP’s full MLB coverage here
Will Graves, The Associated Press

Angel Martínez had three hits for the Guardians, who hold a one-game lead over the White Sox atop the Central and have won six straight. Chicago, which won 14-11 over Kansas City, owns the tiebreaker by winning the season series. Cleveland strande
item.content:encoded:
BOSTON (AP) — Nathaniel Lowe had a tiebreaking sacrifice fly off reliever Erik Miller in the ninth inning, and the Cleveland Guardians maintained their slim first-place lead in the AL Central with a 3-2 victory over the Boston Red Sox on Tuesday night.
Angel Martínez had three hits for the Guardians, who hold a one-game lead over the White Sox atop the Central and have won six straight. Chicago, which won 14-11 over Kansas City, owns the tiebreaker by winning the season series. Cleveland stranded a season-high for a nine-inning game of 15 baserunners.
The loss was Boston’s eighth in 12 games, spoiling Chad Tracy’s first game as manager after the club named him its 49th in team history.
Adley Rutschman added three hits for Boston, which clinched one of the AL’s wild-card spots Sunday.
Boston pinch hitter Mickey Gasper hit Hunter Gaddis’ first pitch, tying it at 2-2 leading off the eighth.
Gaddis (5-3) got the win and Cade Smith the final three outs for his 40th save.
Miller (4-2) hit a batter and gave up two hits in an inning.
A strong candidate for the AL Rookie of the Year, Cleveland left-hander Parker Messick gave up a run over five innings. He lowered his ERA to 2.55 and is on pace to become the fourth rookie starting pitcher in MLB history with an ERA under 2.60 and averaging 9.0 or more strikeouts per nine innings.
In his tune-up for a likely playoff start next week, Boston lefty Payton Tolle struggled with his control over 5 2/3 innings, giving up two runs on eight hits. In his previous start on Sept. 13, he had Boston’s second recorded immaculate inning that opened a game.
Up next
Guardians LHP Foster Griffin (15-5, 3.67 ERA) is set to face Red Sox RHP Sonny Gray (17-5, 2.82) on Wednesday in the middle game of the three-game series.
___
See AP’s full MLB coverage here
Ken Powtak, The Associated Press

item.title: [thebiglead.com] Don Mattingly offers Jesús Luzardo update ahead of Phillies postseason
item.dc:creator: Tate Mosher

The club is currently 86-70 and the No. 6 seed in the National League. Philadelphia is four games up on the outside-looking-in Arizona Diamondbacks, and only one game back of both the San Diego Padres and Chicago Cubs for the higher Wild Card seeds. item.content:encoded:
As the 2026 MLB season concludes, the Philadelphia Phillies are days away from clinching a postseason berth for the fifth straight year. The club is currently 86-70 and the No. 6 seed in the National League.
Philadelphia is four games up on the outside-looking-in Arizona Diamondbacks, and only one game back of both the San Diego Padres and Chicago Cubs for the higher Wild Card seeds.
The Phillies, if they make the playoffs, will have to play in the best-of-three Wild Card round. One would have to think that lefty ace Cristopher Sánchez and veteran righty Zack Wheeler will pitch.
That being said, their best pitcher over the last few months has been presently injured left-hander Jesús Luzardo. Before landing on the 15-day injured list with left shoulder inflammation retroactive to Sept. 12, he had a 1.65 ERA with 124 strikeouts in his 14 most recent starts.
Luzardo’s playoff availability
An injury like pitching arm shoulder inflammation can be tricky when it comes to putting a timeline on it. Luzardo apparently suffered the injury after his Labor Day start versus the Atlanta Braves, so he has been out of action for approximately two weeks.
The Wild Card round runs from Sept. 29 through Oct. 1, so it may be doubtful that Luzardo can make a start for that series. However, it may be possible for him to take on a bullpen role.
When asked on Tuesday, Phillies manager Don Mattingly said that Luzardo is “trending in the right direction.” The quote was reported by Tim Kelly of OnPattison.
Phillies’ postseason outlook
If the season ended today, the Phillies would take on their division rival Braves in Atlanta for the Wild Card round. If they take that series, they would then play the Los Angeles Dodgers at their house.
If Luzardo is not a go for the Wild Card, then the club will perhaps need to find a capable Game 3 starter. That would likely put longtime Phillie Aaron Nola on the bump. Though his season numbers are not great, he has pitched exceptionally well lately.
Nola’s run as of late included back-to-back starts against the Braves early in September, where he twirled 13 ⅓ innings while allowing only three runs. He could be a worthy option if Luzardo cannot go.

item.content:encoded:
●　カブス　2－8　マーリンズ　○
＜現地時間9月22日　リグリー・フィールド＞
シカゴ・カブスが 先発登板した今永昇太投手（32）は5回1失点の投球で勝敗付かず。鈴木誠也外野手（32）は「2番・右翼」でフル出場し、
9月に入ってから3戦全勝の今永は序盤3イニングを無失点の好スタートを切るも、4回裏に一死一、三塁と最初のピンチを招き、5番ラミレスの適時打で先制点を与えた。最終的に5回91球を投げて4被安打、1死球、7奪三振、1失点で降板。今季成績は11勝10敗、防御率3.74となった。
カブス打線は2点を追う6回裏、先頭打者ピート・クローアームストロングが内野安打で出塁し、鈴木が右前安打で繋いで無死一、三塁とチャンスメイク。相手の適時失策で1点を返すと、5番イアン・ハップの右前適時打で鈴木が同点のホームを踏んだ。
鈴木は7回裏の第4打席で右中間への二塁打を放つも、後続倒れて勝ち越し点には繋がらず。9回裏には二死二塁の好機で第5打席に立ったが、二飛を打ち上げて無得点に終わり、試合は延長タイブレークに突入した。
延長11回裏には二死一、二塁と再びサヨナラの好機で鈴木を迎えるも、二ゴロに打ち取られて決着をつけることはできず。12回表に投手陣が一挙6点を失い、ポストシーズン進出決定は明日以降に持ち越しとなった。
なお、クローアームストロングは3回裏に今季39個目の盗塁に成功。今季成績を打率.282、45本塁打、39盗塁、OPS.952とし、MLB史上7人目の「40－40」達成に王手をかけた。

item.title: [royalsreview.com] Inspired Royals offense not enough to overcome uninspired Royals pitching
item.dc:creator: Matthew LaMar

item.content:encoded:
The last time I was physically here at Kauffman Stadium for a baseball game was on September 4, where I witnessed Daniel Lynch IV immediately give up five runs in two innings and functionally take the Royals out of the contest before it began. I got worked up enough about it that I wrote about it that weekend, where I said that the Lynch starter experiment was going exactly how everyone knew it would because of Lynch’s inability to get right-handed batters out with his awful changeup. I linked multiple videos of Lynch hanging changes on a line to those righties.
You can therefore imagine my displeasure at walking into the clubhouse this afternoon, checking my phone to see who was officially starting, and seeing Lynch’s name pop up. I feared a Groundhog’s Day situation.
Unfortunately for me and the meager collection of Royals die-hards watching in person, that’s what happened. The White Sox crushed Royals pitching to the tune of 14 runs, and no amount of late game heroics could lessen the gap. Final score: 14-11, White Sox.
It began early. Witness this rocket line drive off a changeup in the first inning! It was from right-handed batter Chase Meidroth.
Oh, and this laser of an opposite-field home run from right-handed Brenton Doyle. It came off, you guessed it, a changeup.
And this—hark! Another Meidroth homer off another changeup!
After three innings, the White Sox had thwomped their way to a 6-0 lead, which was cut to a whole 6-1 lead by a solo Nick Loftin home run in the bottom of the sixth.
But Lynch was still pitching, and so you could probably bet that five-run lead might balloon further. Sure enough, it did. In the fourth inning, Lynch managed to get two outs but then ran into a row of right-handed batters and, well. You know what happened. Miguel Vargas single, Tommy Pham walk, Randal Grichuk home run. 9-1, White Sox.
At this point, I packed up my belongings and left to listen to the game on the drive and follow from home. Getting credentials is an honor, but what is also great is that, since I’m not a beat writer, I can bail when it’s clear that postgame pressers are not going to yield any particularly interesting pieces of information. Both teams packed it in after the seventh inning; the White Sox removed Miguel Vargas, Tommy Pham, and Braden Montgomery, while the Royals removed Bobby Witt Jr. and Salvador Perez.
Kansas City’s offense, however, did not go quietly into the night. The Royals struck in three consecutive innings against Chicago starter Anthony Kay, with Witt accruing three hits. They managed a trio of runs against Trevor Richards in the eighth, with a pair of extra base hits by the Italian Stallions Jac Caglianone and Vinnie Pasquantino providing the power. And then, in the ninth inning, Tyler Tolbert singled, and Caglianone singled, and Maikel Garcia worked his third walk of the game. Pasquantino then crushed a grand slam to right-center field. It was glorious.
But any hope the Royals had of a great comeback was stymied by, you guessed it, the bullpen. In his Royals debut and his 2026 debut, Tony Gonsolin—who has only pitched 36 MLB innings the last two seasons due to injury—pitched two clean innings and exploded in the seventh, giving up a double to Grichuk and a homer to Munetaka Murakami. Then, he loaded the bases and walked home another run, which prompted Matt Quatraro to remove him in favor of Nolan Hoffman. Hoffman immediately gave up a single to Andrew Benintendi to push the score to 14-4.
As a result, even though the Royals scored 11 runs, they didn’t score a single run down by less than six. Since August 30, the Royals have won two (2) games where they have scored fewer than five runs. That’s because they’ve given up, on average, 5.5 games during that 20-game span.
This is the Royals’ fifth consecutive loss, their eighth loss in their last nine games, and their 15th in their last 20. Remember when the Royals won 13 of 15? They were 13 games under .500 after that first win.
Tonight, the Royals officially wipe all those gains away, and are now 13 games under again. Winning 70 games seems like a longshot. Eat Arby’s.
